Q5 A8 proof package: three complete transfer branches and five residual orbits

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer output; independent review pending.

Claim

Let F be any matching of the complete graph on V(Q5) with exactly eight holes, three of one parity and five of the other. For every specified hole v in the larger class, there is a simple cycle on exactly V(Q5)⧵{v} containing F, with every edge outside F short. Required edges may be arbitrary long edges and may join equal parities.

Status

NOT CURRENTLY JUSTIFIED. The original statement is unchanged. This package proves the augmentation branch and every instance admitting a coordinate cut of imbalance 1,2, or 3. A complete census reduces the remaining hole geometries to five explicitly listed orbits; their arbitrary matching instances remain open. No failed search is presented as a counterexample, and no sampled success is used to assert a universal claim.

Assumptions and dependency map
  1. Q5 A6, established in A6_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md and its closure reviews.
  2. GQ4-avoid and GQ4-cycle in Q4_GENERAL_AUGMENTATION.md, for arbitrary hole counts of imbalance two and zero, respectively.
  3. The four-hole optional edge bounds O15 and O18 in Section 2 of A6_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md, with their certified finite inputs.
  4. The residual geometry census is the new independent deterministic program A8_geometry_census.py. It enumerates hole sets only, never matching instances. Its output is A8_geometry_census.json.

Items 1--3 are imported results, not new assumptions on F. The partial proof below uses no Q5 A8/A10, higher-hole P6 claim, or Q5 T15 result.

Notation and proof strategy

Call majority parity O and minority parity E; these are labels, not fixed numerical parities. For a coordinate cut let A contain v and B be the other face. Write FA,FB for the internal matching edges, C for the crossing matching, c=|C|, and XA,XB for its endpoint sets. Let HA,HB be the original holes, and set δ=|HA∩O|−|HA∩E|. For t∈A, write t¯ for its short mirror in B, which need not be its required partner.

We add short edges between opposite-parity holes when possible. Otherwise we use a face cycle or a face path, remove an artificial matching, attach the original crossings and selected short bridges, and compress the resulting paths into a matching on the opposite face.

Proof
Step 1. Augmentation and a local geometric fact

If a minority hole is short-adjacent to a majority hole other than v, add that short edge. The augmented matching has two minority and four majority holes and still has v free. Q5 A6 gives the desired cycle; the added edge is short relative to the original matching. Hence we may assume

E∩H has no short edge to (O∩H)⧵{v}.(I)

In Q4, any two distinct same-parity vertices have at least six distinct neighbors: at distance two they have two common neighbors, and at distance four none. Therefore two such vertices cannot simultaneously avoid three vertices of the other parity. We use this fact in each face with its global parity labels.

The identity 2|FA|+c=16−|HA| determines the parity of c.

Step 2. Transfer conventions

If a cycle contains a nonempty matching D, deleting D leaves a path forest with endpoint set V(D). Restoring any proper subset of these removed edges, possibly as internally disjoint paths, leaves a path forest: otherwise the restored subset and the undeleted part of the original cycle would contain a cycle while an edge of the original cycle remained missing. Thus no component closes prematurely in the constructions below.

Compressing disjoint paths to edges gives a matching on their endpoints. If a cycle on the other face contains this matching and avoids its internal vertices, expansion gives one simple cycle. This preserves all required edges, and the only newly added edges outside artificial paths are short edges. Any artificial edge is deleted or expanded.

Step 3. All cuts with δ=2

Here c is even. If c>0, choose any perfect matching D on XA. The holes of FA∪D are exactly HA, of majority excess two. GQ4-avoid gives an A−v cycle containing it. Delete D, attach every edge of C, and compress to R on XB. The matching FB∪R has holes exactly HB, which are balanced because the total excess is two. GQ4-cycle gives its full B cycle, and expansion finishes.

Suppose c=0, and put k=|HA∩E|. The hole counts in A are (k,k+2) and in B are (3−k,3−k). If k=0, the B face has three minority and three nonforbidden majority holes, contradicting (I) and the two-versus-three geometric fact. If k≥2, A has two minority holes and at least three majority holes other than v, with the same contradiction. Consequently k=1. The A holes have counts (1,3), and the B holes (2,2). O15 supplies at least 15 short optional edges among the extending A−v cycles; O18 supplies at least 18 among the full extending B cycles. Under the mirror identification both unions lie in the 32 edges of Q4. Their intersection is nonempty, since 15+18>32. Choose corresponding optional edges in two witnessing cycles, delete these two edges, and join their corresponding endpoints by two short edges across the cut. The result is the required single cycle. The optional edge union argument asserts the existence of separate witnessing cycles for the chosen edge; it does not prescribe many optional edges simultaneously.

Step 4. All cuts with δ=3

The crossing number c is odd and positive. There are at least two nonforbidden majority holes in A. Choose one, t, whose mirror w=t¯ is not the unique B port when c=1; two candidates ensure this choice exists. For c≥3 choose any such hole. By (I), w is covered in the original matching, and has minority parity.

Choose a perfect matching D on XA∪{t}. Adding D reduces the majority excess in the remaining A holes from three to two, so GQ4-avoid gives an A−v cycle. If w is a port, prescribe tx∈D, where x is the original A partner of w; this is possible because t is a hole and x is a port.

If w is internal to FB, delete D, attach C and the bridge tw, and compress to R on XB∪{w}. Let wk∈FB and wq∈R. Suppress these two edges into kq. All other edges remain disjoint, and the holes of the resulting matching are HB∪{w}. The original B majority excess is 2−3=−1; adding the minority hole w gives excess −2. GQ4-avoid therefore applies with minority parity as the larger class and avoids w. Expand kq via kw and the transferred path; expand every other compressed edge.

If w is a port, then c≥3 by the choice for c=1, and |D|≥2. Delete D. The endpoints t,x of its prescribed edge lie in different path components. Attaching tw,xw restores just that gap through w; at least one other gap remains. Attach all other crossings. Compress the resulting forest onto XB⧵{w}; its interiors contain A−v and w. Together with FB this is a matching whose holes are HB∪{w}, again of excess −2. Apply GQ4-avoid avoiding w and expand. This also gives the required cycle.

Step 5. All cuts with δ=1

Put k=|HA∩E|, so |HA∩O|=k+1. If k=0 or 1, the B hole counts are (3−k,4−k), containing two minority and three majority holes, none equal to v. This contradicts (I). Hence k≥2. The crossing number c is odd and positive.

Choose a minority hole y∈A. When c=1, choose y whose mirror w=y¯ is not the unique B port; at least two choices of y exist. For c≥3 any y may be used. By (I), w is covered and has majority parity. Select a root port d∈XA and a perfect matching D on XA⧵{d}. The matching

FA∪D∪{dy}

has original holes HA⧵{y} of majority excess two and contains the free forbidden hole v. GQ4-avoid supplies an A−v cycle containing dy; deleting dy gives an A−v path from d to y.

If w is internal to FB, delete D from the path, attach all crossings and yw, compress, and suppress the unique overlap w as in Step 4. The resulting matching has holes HB∪{w}. The original B excess is one; adding majority hole w gives excess two. GQ4-avoid avoiding w and expansion complete the cycle.

If w is a port, c≥3. Choose d to be its original crossing partner. Then D is nonempty. Deleting D from the d--y path separates its endpoints into different components, since at least one edge of that path was removed. Attach dw,yw and the other crossings; the two endpoint components join through w without closing a cycle. Compress onto XB⧵{w} and apply GQ4-avoid to the matching with holes HB∪{w}, avoiding w. Expansion finishes.

In particular the exceptional k=c=1 endpoint lemma required in the A6 proof never arises in A8. No new finite endpoint input is needed.

Step 6. Exact remaining geometric obligation

Translate v to 0; this makes the majority parity the numerical even parity. Let Z be the four other even holes and W the three odd holes. Condition (I) says every z∈Z is nonadjacent to every w∈W. There are only (154) possibilities for Z. For each one the program lists all odd vertices nonadjacent to Z and all their triples W. This gives exactly 2700 configurations. For coordinate i, the face containing 0 is its zero face, and the program directly computes

δi=1+|{z∈Z:zi=0}|−|{w∈W:wi=0}|.

Exactly 2540 configurations have some δi∈{1,2,3} and are proved by Steps 3--5. For every other configuration the program takes the lexicographically smallest pair (πZ,πW) over all 120 coordinate permutations. The remaining 160 configurations have exactly the following five representatives:

Z W orbit size ordered (δ0,…,δ4) at this representative
3,5,6,15 8,25,26 60 0,0,−1,4,4
3,5,6,15 25,26,28 20 0,0,0,4,5
3,5,15,23 25,26,28 30 −1,0,0,4,4
15,23,27,29 1,2,4 30 −1,0,0,−1,−1
15,23,27,29 2,4,8 20 −2,0,0,0,−1

The census output includes every residual member and its computed deltas, so both coverage and orbit membership are inspectable. Orbit sizes sum to 160. The normalization preserves arbitrary matching edges, the specified forbidden hole, and shortness. The enumerated domain is therefore a complete geometry reduction, not a finite test of selected matching instances.

Corrections or missing assumptions

To prove the original A8 claim it suffices to prove it for every arbitrary matching on the 24 covered vertices in each of the five rows. No matching condition may be silently imposed in that residual theorem.

Open risks

The five residual rows remain open. Delta-zero and delta-four double-bridge transfers can leave a Q4 T15 instance with its genuine triangle obstruction; the existence of Q4 T15 positive cases does not remove this obstruction. The separate A8_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_SUFFICIENT.md proves a sufficient mechanism to avoid it in many matching instances, without asserting complete coverage. No full A8 or full higher-hole P6 closure is claimed by this package.

A8_Q4_T63_CLASSIFICATION.md — Q4 T63: six same-parity holes with three prescribed avoided holes

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：6d99eb27dd3a1c7396a6ae930959871f9124dd27c12d00ace8a999d0cf09c597。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBIT4_FULL_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBIT5_FULL_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBITS2_3_REVIEW.json, Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json, TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json。

Q4 T63: six same-parity holes with three prescribed avoided holes

Date: 2026-11-01. New finite input for A8 exploration; fresh review pending.

Claim

Let L be an arbitrary matching of K(Q4) with six holes H of one parity. Let U⊂H be any prescribed three holes. Then a simple cycle with vertex set exactly Q4⧵U containing L and using only short new edges exists if and only if there is no covered vertex a of opposite parity having exactly one neighbor b outside U with ab∈L.

Status

PROVABLE AS STATED by analytic necessity and complete finite positive certificates. This result awaits independent proof-checker review.

Assumptions, notation, and dependency map

The vertices are the four-bit integers 0,…,15. A short edge has endpoints differing in exactly one bit. The required matching can contain arbitrary edges. The proof uses no Q5 extension theorem and no T15 input. The finite positive files are listed in A8_Q4_T63_manifest.json. The verifier is A8_Q4_T63_verify.py, with output A8_Q4_T63_verified.json.

Proof strategy and proof
Step 1. Analytic obstruction

Every vertex of parity opposite to H is covered by L. Suppose a has just one short neighbor b outside the avoided set U, and ab∈L. In a proposed cycle the edge ab must be present. Because L is a matching, every other edge incident to a in the cycle would be a new short edge. There is no distinct such edge available: the only remaining short neighbor is already b. A simple cycle needs two distinct incident edges at a. This is impossible, proving necessity. This is an explicit degree obstruction, not a Hamilton-search failure.

Step 2. Exhaustive normalization of the finite domains

First assume H is even. There are (86(63=))560 marked geometries (H,U). The automorphisms

x⟼π(x⊕e),

where e is any even vertex and π is any coordinate permutation, give seven orbits. Their representatives and orbit sizes are:

H U orbit size positive matchings degree-obstructed matchings
0,3,5,6,9,10 0,3,5 96 945 0
0,3,5,6,9,10 0,5,6 96 840 105
0,3,5,6,9,10 0,5,9 96 945 0
0,3,5,6,9,10 0,5,10 96 945 0
0,3,5,6,9,10 5,6,9 96 945 0
0,3,5,10,12,15 0,3,5 32 840 105
0,3,5,10,12,15 0,3,12 48 945 0

The verifier regenerates each orbit directly, checks that they are pairwise disjoint, and checks that their union equals the entire set of 560 marked geometries. Hence this is a complete geometry cover. If H is odd, an odd translation makes it even and preserves short edges, matching edges, avoided vertices, and the obstruction condition.

Step 3. Complete matching coverage and explicit cycles

Every representative has ten covered vertices, admitting exactly 9!!=945 matchings. Each binary file has 945 records of 29 bytes: 16 mate bytes, followed by 13 cycle bytes. A mate byte of 255 marks a hole. A 13-byte suffix consisting of 255 marks a negative record.

The verifier independently constructs the set of all 945 unordered edge-set matchings. For each record it checks the exact holes and the fixed-point-free mate involution, removes that matching from the set, and finally checks that the set is empty. Thus there are no omitted or duplicated matching inputs.

For every positive record, it checks 13 distinct vertices, exact vertex set Q4⧵U, containment of every matching edge, and shortness of every cycle edge outside the matching. These explicit cycles prove sufficiency for all 6405 positive records. No assumption about the completeness of the producer's search is needed.

For every negative record, the verifier directly checks the obstruction of Step 1. There are exactly 210 such records: 105 in each of the two negative-bearing representative files. In the second row the forced obstruction edge is 412; in the sixth row it is 19. In each case the three avoided vertices are three of the four short neighbors of the first endpoint, leaving just the second endpoint. Fixing that matching edge leaves eight other covered vertices with 7!!=105 matchings. The count agrees with, and is independently checked against, the explicit records. The verifier also checks absence of an obstruction for each positive record.

Step 4. Transfer back to arbitrary inputs

Choose an automorphism taking (H,U) to one of the representatives. It maps an arbitrary original matching to one of the 945 checked matchings and preserves the obstruction. In the unobstructed case, invert the automorphism on its explicit positive cycle. In the obstructed case apply Step 1 directly. This proves the exact classification.

Reproduction

Run D:\anaconda\python.exe A8_Q4_T63_verify.py in this directory. The verified result records all seven binary hashes and the verifier hash, with totals 560 geometries, seven orbits, 6615 matching records, 6405 positive cycles, and 210 analytic negative records.

Corrections or missing assumptions

T63 is not universally positive. An application in a three-bridge Q5 transfer must exclude a degree-obstruction edge in the final compressed matching, including edges created by suppression. Absence of the fixed edge in the original face matching alone does not suffice.

Open risks

Fresh independent review is pending. The local theorem by itself proves no remaining A8 orbit, no full A8, and no higher-hole P6 layer.

A8_THREE_BRIDGE_SUFFICIENT.md — A8: three-bridge sufficient criterion for a delta-minus-one cut

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：b369c9d167264b5a6478fe2277f9823e6c5a0124824fdc2130decbc9b9e46cf9。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBIT4_FULL_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBIT5_FULL_REVIEW.json, Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json, TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json。

A8: three-bridge sufficient criterion for a delta-minus-one cut

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft; fresh independent review pending.

Claim

Let F be an A8 matching with forbidden majority hole v, satisfying the usual residual nonadjacency condition. Suppose a coordinate face A containing v has exactly three minority holes t1,t2,t3 and two majority holes. Thus its imbalance is −1, and the other face B has three majority holes and no minority holes. Put wi=t¯i. All three wi are covered and have majority parity. The criterion below suffices to extend F to the required cycle on Q5−v.

Status

PROVABLE AS STATED, relative to GQ4-avoid and the new finite T63 classification A8_Q4_T63_CLASSIFICATION.md, which is itself pending fresh independent review. No remaining orbit is claimed to satisfy the criterion universally.

Notation, assumptions, and dependency map

Use FA,FB,C,c,XA,XB as before. Here c is odd because A has five holes. Let T=XA∪{t1,t2,t3} and d=|T|/2=(c+3)/2. Define

G=FB∪C∪{t1w1,t2w2,t3w3}.

The A vertices are exactly T, of degree one. Only the three bridge vertices wi have degree two in B. Every such vertex is incident to a bridge ending in T; consequently every component of G is a path. A cycle could not visit any bridge vertex without also visiting a degree-one endpoint. All other B vertices have degree at most one.

Let P be the matching on T given by the components of G with both endpoints in T. Each consumes at least one bridge vertex, so |P|≤3. A component meeting T with other endpoint in B has that endpoint as its terminal and its T endpoint as its root.

Proof strategy and criterion

If the three avoided vertices w1,w2,w3 have no common short neighbor in the face B, set J=P. Otherwise their common short neighbor a is unique. Indeed two same-parity vertices of Q4 have at most two common neighbors, so two different common neighbors cannot have three distinct common neighbors wi. Let b be the fourth neighbor of a in B, the unique neighbor not among w1,w2,w3.

If b is an original B hole, again set J=P; the edge ab cannot belong to the compressed matching because b remains a hole. Otherwise require ab∉FB. If both a,b are terminals of components of G meeting T, with roots u,r, set J=P∪{ur}. In all other cases set J=P.

The sufficient criterion is

d>|J|.

Here J is a matching: roots of terminal components are distinct and are not endpoints of P. In particular, when an obstruction edge is possible and absent from FB, every cut with c≥7 satisfies this criterion because d≥5 and |J|≤4.

Proof

Complete J to a perfect matching D on T. The holes of FA∪D are just the two original majority holes in A, including v. GQ4-avoid gives a cycle K on A−v containing this matching. Deleting D gives a path matching S on T with S∪D a single cycle after the paths are contracted. The graph S∪J has no cycle, since J is a proper subset of D. Attaching G to the A paths therefore produces a path forest with all endpoints in B⧵{w1,w2,w3}. Compressing gives a matching L on B with exactly six majority-parity holes: the three original B holes and the three bridge vertices.

The T63 classification says that this matching has a cycle avoiding w1,w2,w3 unless it contains ab for the unique possible a,b above. When no common a exists, no obstruction exists. If b is an original hole, ab∉L because b is free in L.

In the remaining case a,b are original covered nonbridge vertices of B. Each has degree one in G. Every component of G with both endpoints in B is an original edge of FB: any longer path would have to pass through a bridge vertex and then end in T. If one of a,b is in such a component, its original partner remains its partner in L, and ab∉FB excludes the obstruction.

If both are terminals rooted at u,r, an edge ab∈L would yield an u--r path in S∪P. Together with ur∈J, it would form a cycle in S∪J, contradicting its acyclicity. Therefore the compressed matching has no T63 obstruction. Take its T63 cycle, expand all paths, and restore each bridge vertex and all of A−v. The resulting cycle contains every original required edge and all new edges are short. This proves the sufficient claim.

Application and remaining finite obligations

For the fourth residual representative of the original census,

v=0,Z={15,23,27,29},W={1,2,4},

the cuts at bits 8 and 16 both have the required A hole counts. Their bridges, common neighbor, and possible obstruction edge are:

cut bit bridge vertices in B common neighbor a fourth neighbor b
8 9,10,12 8 24
16 17,18,20 16 24

The two fixed obstruction edges 824 and 1624 cannot both belong to the original matching. Therefore at least one of these cuts has no fixed obstruction. If that cut has at least seven crossings, the criterion proves the A8 conclusion. It follows that an instance left by both sufficient tests must have a cut with no fixed obstruction and at most five crossings. This is a rigorous reduction to small crossing counts, not a proof that they are all extendable.

Open risks

The T63 classification and this transfer await independent review. Cases with c=1,3,5 and d≤|J| can require other bridges, other cuts, or a finite local certificate package. No large matching census has been run and no full orbit closure is asserted.

AVOIDED_VERTEX_TRANSFER.md — N11、N12及Z9：避开目标的单孔侧转移

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：f44623960b51f85549ea15b6b7c8262222c097f56c37ae10c05b77b6dd8776a7。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_COVERED_REVIEW.json。

N11、N12及Z9：避开目标的单孔侧转移

日期：2026-11-01。局部证明草稿；完整P6未证明。

外部输入与半层事实

引用Fink–Mütze作者全文 https://tmuetze.de/papers/match.pdf 的Theorem 12：m≥5，x,y异奇偶，K(Q_m{x,y})的完美匹配可延拓为避开x,y的圈，当且仅当不含半层。圈必覆盖其全部匹配端点，故这里覆盖全部其余顶点。extension的新增边只能是Q_m短边。

半层H的端点集S及补集T由除其方向j外的坐标和奇偶划分。两侧内部的短边都仅沿j。任何包含H的匹配，其所有短边都沿j：其余边不能接触已被H覆盖的S，故其余短边在T内。相应方向只有两个半层。

N11：近完美匹配的避孔路径

设m≥5，L是K(Q_m)匹配，孔恰为不同的v,a。b被L覆盖且与v异奇偶，记k=L(b)。令

T_b=(L\{bk})∪{ak}。

若T_b不含半层，则存在覆盖V(Q_m){v}的a—b路径，包含全部L，其他边短。

证明：a,v,b,k两两不同，T_b恰不覆盖v,b。Theorem 12给出覆盖除v,b外全部顶点且含T_b的圈。删除辅助ak，得到a—k路径；再接原L边kb，恢复b。原L仅暂删bk，现已恢复；辅助ak消失。得到所需路径。并不要求ab相邻，也不要求L二部。证毕。

N12：有至少四个自由点时的无半层完美补全

设m≥5，v,b异奇偶。F是K(Q_m{v,b})匹配，其在V(Q_m){v,b}内未覆盖集为Y，且|Y|为偶数、|Y|≥4。若F不含半层，则Y上存在配对W，使F∪W仍不含半层。

证明分三种情况。

  1. F的短边使用至少两个方向。任何补全都不可能含半层，因为包含半层的匹配的所有短边只能同方向。
  2. F有短边且只用方向j。在Y上选择不使用任何j短边的完美配对W。其存在如下：j短边在Y中组成匹配；任取一个完美配对，只要它含一条被禁止的j边xy，就取另一条边pq，将xy,pq换为xp,yq。四点不同；x,y各自唯一被禁止的伙伴是对方，所以两条新边都非j边。禁止边数严格减少，最终为0。若F∪W含方向k半层，F保留的短j边迫使k=j；但W没有j边，故该半层原已包含于F，矛盾。
  3. F没有短边。在Y的非短边图中取任意极大匹配W0。剩余顶点两两都以短边相接，否则可再加非短边。Q_m无三角形，故剩余点至多2个；其数为偶数，所以是0或2。若是2就补上其短边，得到完美配对W，至多含一条短边。F∪W至多有一条短边，不能包含有2^(m−2)≥8条边的半层。

证毕。|Y|=2时结论不自动成立，不在本引理范围内。

Z9：目标收缩后的单孔侧转移

设n≥6，M是Q_n短匹配，孔为u,z,w,t，其中u,z偶、w,t奇；v为已覆盖奇目标。记h=M(v)，令

M*=(M\{vh})∪{hu}。

M是K(Q_n)匹配，孔为v,z,w,t；唯一可能的长边hu连接两个偶点。沿某方向i分成A,B，使v∈A，z,w,t∈B；不限制u,h位于哪一侧。记C为M跨层边，X_A,X_B为其端口。A的唯一原孔是v，故|X_A|为正奇数。

选择一个奇孔w（可交换w,t），令b=w⊕e_i∈A。要求b由M_A覆盖，记k=M_A(b)。选择a∈X_A以及X_A{a}上的任意完整图配对D。设

L_A=M_A*∪D，T_b=(L_A\{bk})∪{ak}

不含半层。则M有Hamilton u—v延拓。

证明

L_A恰漏v,a，v奇、b偶，且b不被D覆盖。N11给出A{v}上的a—b路径K_A。删除D；D不接触a,b，且为匹配，故产生互不相交的非平凡路径段，端点集为X_A*∪{b}。

给每个X_A端点接回其C边，再加短跨边bw。所得路径族内点全在A{v}，端点集为X_B∪{w}。各跨端口不同，w是M的孔，因此无端点冲突。把各段缩成形式边R，得B内匹配；它与M_B*覆盖集合不交。

L_B=M_B*∪R恰漏z,t，二者异奇偶；L_B允许任意同奇偶长边。由N10选自由根z到B内任一短邻点y的Hamilton延拓（y与t同奇偶），再加短边zy闭圈，得到B的Hamilton圈C_B。

展开R，得到覆盖Q_n{v}的圈C，包含全部M。所有A内点在不同展开段中恰出现一次，所有B点在C_B中恰出现一次。M_A、M_B及C全部保留。辅助D、ak均已删除，R展开；除M*外新增边全部短。

最后删除hu，得到端点h,u的路径，再在h端接回原边hv。其顶点集变为全部Q_n，端点为u,v；保留全部M。即使hu是跨层长边，也作为M*边保留到这最后一步才删除，不把它误当作普通短跨边。证毕。

可直接使用N12的充分条件

固定w及b，令F_b=M_A{bk}、Y=X_A∪{k}。若|X_A|≥3且F_b不含半层，则N12给出Y的无半层补全W。在W中k的伙伴必为某个a∈X_A；令D=W{ak}，正好得到Z9要求的T_b。对于|X_A*|=1，需直接验证唯一T_b，不能调用N12。

Z9是条件性转移，尚未声称每个输入都有此坐标切分或无半层补全。最终原匹配仍全部是短边；只有中间M*及R允许长边。

BIPARTITE_NEAR_PERFECT.md — 非相邻双孔的二部近完美延拓：N6—N8

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：1cb47da03495d5c2dde0b21f536057a0455bab30f3dcd28ef7c1d4d482746afd。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json。

非相邻双孔的二部近完美延拓：N6—N8

日期：2026-11-01。完整P6仍开放。本稿不假设短边方向数，不使用已知五方向短匹配定理；输入为Fink完整图完美匹配圈定理及GNS二部完美匹配端点定理（n≥5）。

N6：非相邻双孔、任意异奇偶终点

设n≥5，L是B(Q_n)的匹配，恰不覆盖r,s，且d(r,s)>1。那么对每个与r异奇偶的y，存在包含L的Hamilton r—y路径，其余边均为Q_n短边。L允许任意异奇偶长边。

证明

r,s异奇偶。令P=L∪{rs}为B(Q_n)完美匹配。若y=s，Fink定理给出包含P的Hamilton圈，删除rs即可。以下y≠s；因此y被L覆盖。

令I={j:r_j≠s_j}、J={j:r_j≠y_j}。I,J均有奇数个元素且互不相同。其对称差非空且大小为偶数，故至少含两坐标；这些坐标均不在I∩J。因此至少有两个坐标属于[n](I∩J)。

对每个这样的坐标l考虑x=s⊕e_l。至多一个满足x=P(y)，所以可取l∉I∩J并使x≠P(y)。rs非相邻保证x≠r；也有x≠s。x与r同奇偶、y与r异奇偶，故x≠y且xy不属于P。

考虑端点x,y处的压缩匹配

R=(P⧵{xP(x),yP(y)})∪{P(x)P(y)}.

假设R含方向j的半层，端点集S、补集T。压缩端点x,y未被R覆盖，所以x,y∈T。rs是长边，且r,s均非x,y，因此rs仍在R中。半层S每个顶点已由短j边配对，故长边rs的两端r,s均在T。

半层划分由去掉j后的坐标奇偶性决定。x,s∈T且x=s⊕e_l，迫使j=l。r,s∈T且d(r,s)为奇数，迫使j∈I：若j不在I，去掉j后两点仍相差奇数位，应分居两侧。同理r,y∈T迫使j∈J。于是l=j∈I∩J，与选择矛盾。

压缩匹配无半层；GNS端点定理给出包含P的Hamilton x—y路径K，新增边短。P二部且完美，所以沿K的P边统一从p(r)到1−p(r)；特别地rs沿r→s出现。删去rs，反向走r到x的第一段，再加入短边xs，接上s到y的第二段。得到覆盖全部顶点且包含L的r—y路径。只删辅助rs，只加短xs。证毕。

N7：任意二部近完美匹配的圈延拓

设n≥5，L是B(Q_n)的匹配，恰好有两个孔r,s。则L可延拓为Hamilton圈，所有新增边均短。

若r,s相邻，P=L∪{rs}完美；Fink定理直接给出圈，辅助rs本身也是短边，故满足延拓定义。

若r,s不相邻，任取r的短邻点y。N6给出Hamilton r—y延拓；加入短边ry闭圈。路径覆盖至少32个顶点，不能已含两端之间的边ry。证毕。

此结论不声称相邻双孔时，L对每个指定终点也有Hamilton路径；N6的非相邻前提不被删除。

N8：任意二部四孔匹配的自由端点路径

设n≥5，M是B(Q_n)匹配，恰有四个孔。对任意两个异奇偶的自由点u,v，存在包含M的Hamilton u—v路径，新增边全部短。

加入辅助uv得到二部近完美匹配L。由N7得到包含L的Hamilton圈，删去uv，即得所求。L允许原M的多条长边，但uv是新加的一条边，删除它后原M边全部保留，新增边仍短。证毕。

N8包含F6的全部短边输入结论，但不要求M只含短边，也不再使用低方向分支。它仍不处理已覆盖终点。

输入与范围

来源：Fink–Mütze作者全文第1页extension定义和Theorem2、第4页Theorem9。N6只使用B(Q_n)版本；不需要完整图的非二部加强。

N6证明必须保留rs长边在压缩匹配中这一事实；不能把相邻孔直接代入其半层论证。N7相邻分支使用不同的Fink圈论证。这里未证明完整P6或原文任何更强未决猜想，也不声明新颖性。

CANONICAL_A4_CLOSURE.md — Closing the canonical A4 family by flexible endpoints

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：1da0c3e81a36cae53e727fad20878096c32ae442ceaa7277aa986aef5e60e271。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json, CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json, Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json, Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_CLOSURE_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json, TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json。

Closing the canonical A4 family by flexible endpoints

Date: 2026-11-01. Proof status at initial writing: complete argument relative to the listed finite certificates and prior inputs; independent audit pending. The claim here is full Q5 A4, not full Q6 P6. The 8--18-hole P6 levels remain open even if this proof and its dependencies are accepted.

Claim

A4. For every matching F of K(Q5) with exactly four holes of parity counts 3 and 1, and every prescribed majority-parity hole v, there is a cycle through exactly V(Q5)⧵{v} containing every edge of F, with all edges outside F short.

By R1A in A4_SINGLE_GEOMETRY_REDUCTION.md, it remains to prove the claim when the holes are a=0,v=1,b=14,t=22, with v=1 forbidden. That reduction is already independently reviewed and does not assume A4. Original edges of F remain completely arbitrary, including same-parity long edges.

Dependencies
  • R1A and its Q4 inputs: A4_SINGLE_GEOMETRY_REDUCTION.md, Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md, with their corresponding audit reports.
  • Q4 A4_4 and NC_4 from the latter document. A4_4 is a separately certified four-dimensional theorem, not an invocation of the present Q5 A4 claim.
  • Complete Q4 avoided-circle tables below, independently verifiable by explicit positive circles and exhaustive short perfect completions for every negative instance.
  • The finite completion accounting below. Its entire search space is characterized by inverse maps, not by random sampling of Q5 matchings.
1. Complete Q4 two-hole tables

For h=1,7, consider every perfect matching of the 14 vertices V(Q4)⧵{0,h}. A successful instance has a Hamilton circle on those 14 vertices, containing the matching, with short new edges.

There are 13!!=135135 instances for each h. Each record of q4_distance1_avoided_table.bin or q4_distance3_avoided_table.bin contains the 16-byte mate array and a 14-vertex circle, or an all-255 marker for a negative instance. verify_q4_avoided_table.py checks every matching and complete bijective rank coverage, as in the preceding Q4 proof package. It checks every positive circle directly. For a negative, every allowed vertex already has one required matching edge, so every possible extending circle must add a short perfect matching disjoint from the required one. The checker enumerates all such short perfect matchings by matching the seven even vertices to the seven odd vertices, and verifies that every union has more than one connected component. Thus the negative judgment does not rely on the producer's Hamilton search.

holes positive negative negative with half-layer negative without half-layer
0,1 135084 51 15 36
0,7 135082 53 45 8

Coordinate permutations take these tables to every pair 0,y with y odd. Let By denote the corresponding complete set of negative matchings. The tables and permutations therefore decide the extension question for every matching with holes 0,y, for all eight odd y.

2. A path criterion and its exact inverse

Let L be a matching of K(Q4) with exactly the holes 0,d, where d≠0. For an odd vertex y≠d, write k=L(y) and define

Ty(L)=L−yk+dk.

This is a matching with precisely the holes 0,y. If it is not in By, its certified 14-circle contains dk. Delete dk and append the original edge ky, producing a path from d to y on exactly Q4⧵{0}. The path contains L and all new edges are short. The edge ky may be long but is an original required edge of L.

Conversely, such a path must use yk as its final edge, since y is covered by L. Deleting y and adding dk gives the corresponding 14-circle of Ty(L). The newly added dk is a required edge of Ty(L), so it need not be short. Thus this criterion is an equivalence.

For fixed y and d∉{0,y} it has an exact inverse. Given T∈By, let k=T(d) and set

L=T−dk+yk.

Then L has holes 0,d and Ty(L)=T. Every bad pair (L,y) is obtained this way, with no missing matching. The target y=d is separately excluded.

3. Finite completion lemma

Let P be any matching on the 15 vertices Q4⧵{0}, with uncovered vertex set X of odd size c. In the intended application P is the internal A matching and X is its crossing-port set.

A completion consists of a root d∈X and a perfect matching D on X⧵{d}. Put L=P∪D, which has exactly holes 0,d. There are

Tc=c(c−2)!!

distinct completions, using (−1)!!=1. Call an odd target y available for that completion when y≠d and Ty(L)∉By.

The following exact finite facts hold:

  1. Either a completion makes target 7 or 11 available, or P belongs to the finite stall class counted below.
  2. For a stall with c=1 or c=3, at least four distinct odd targets are available for some completion (the completion may depend on the target).
  3. For a stall with c=5 or c=7, there is a set G of four odd vertices, disjoint from X, such that every target y∈G is available for every completion, including every choice of root d∈X.
  4. There are no stalls for c≥9.

Here is the full counting certificate:

c |P| Tc candidate partials stall partials available-target sizes on stalls
1 7 1 256 256 4,5,6
3 6 3 1372 210 4
5 5 15 3048 42 4, all completions
7 4 105 3596 2 4, all completions
9 3 945 2366 0 —
11 2 10395 808 0 —
13 1 135135 84 0 —
15 0 2027025 1 0 —

The last row is included to state the finite lemma on all partial matchings; the actual canonical Q5 cut has at most 13 crossing edges.

Why this enumeration is complete

First apply the inverse in Step 2 to the two target tables B7 and B11. The latter is the permutation of B7 swapping coordinates 2 and 3. For each of the 53 table entries and each of its 14 covered vertices d, recover L, and test the other target. This gives exactly 256 near-perfect inputs (d,L) for which both fixed targets are unavailable, among all 15·135135=2027025 inputs. The case d=7 or d=11 is included: that target is unavailable by equality, and the other is tested. See a4_single_crossing_exceptions.py/.json.

For each size |P|=(15−c)/2, enumerate all subsets of the 256 seven-edge matchings L, keeping a count of how many bad completions contain each subset P. Any stall must occur in this enumeration: if every completion is bad, it is a subset of at least one bad completion. Each counted near-perfect matching has a unique free root d besides 0, so it counts exactly one of the Tc completions. A partial matching is a stall exactly when its count is Tc. No assumptions about the unenumerated Q5 matching or its crossing bijection are made.

For each stall, use the inverse of Step 2 for all eight odd targets, with all 14 possible covered roots d in each negative table entry. Count those bad near-perfect matchings containing P. If y∈X, also count the (c−2)!! completions whose root is d=y. The target is available for some completion precisely when the total bad count is less than Tc; it is available for every completion precisely when the count is zero. a4_completion_endpoint_probe.py/.json performs this accounting and records every stall, port set, and target count. For all 42 five-port and both seven-port stalls, the four listed available targets have count zero and lie outside X. These are the quantified properties used below.

4. Transfer setup in the canonical Q5 family

Split Q5 on coordinate 0. Let A be the odd integer labels, with the sole hole v=1, and B the even labels, with holes 0,14,22. Identify each face with Q4 by z↦⌊z/2⌋. In these local coordinates, v is 0 in A and the B holes are 0,7,11.

Write FA,FB for internal matchings, C for the crossing matching, and XA,XB for their local port sets. Counting either side gives

2|FA|+c=15,2|FB|+c=13,

so c=|C| is odd and 1≤c≤13. Crossing edges may be arbitrary long required edges. They define a bijection between XA and XB.

Apply the finite completion lemma to P=FA, X=XA. A completion (d,D) and an available odd target y give a path W on A⧵{v}, from local d to local y, containing FA∪D and only short new edges. Delete D, attach every original crossing edge of C at its A port, and attach the short coordinate-0 bridge between the two copies of y. The following two forms of this transfer suffice.

5. Safe transfer when y∉XB

The resulting path family has distinct endpoints XB∪{y} and disjoint interiors partitioning A⧵{v}. In particular this remains true if y∈XA⧵{d}: its incident D edge is removed from the endpoint of W, leaving an isolated A vertex; attaching its original crossing edge and the new bridge turns it into a two-edge path with distinct B endpoints. Every other component is a path as well. No cycle can be formed because the attached B endpoints are all distinct. Compress the paths to a matching R on XB∪{y}.

If y=7 or 11, it is a B hole and FB∪R has the two opposite-parity holes 0 and the other member of {7,11}. NC_4 gives a full B circle; expanding R gives the desired 31-circle.

Otherwise y is odd, is not 0,7,11, and is not in XB. It is internally covered in B. Set k=FB(y) and q=R(y). The matching

LB=(FB⧵{yk})∪(R⧵{yq})∪{kq}

has exactly the holes 0,7,11,y, of parity counts 1 and 3. Apply A4_4 avoiding y. Expand kq into the original edge ky followed by the transferred y--q path, and expand the other R edges. This restores y and all of A⧵{v}, preserving every original edge and adding only short edges. Thus the safe transfer is valid.

6. Port transfer with a prescribed root

Suppose c≥3, y∈XB, y∉XA, and a completion is available with root d equal to the A partner of the original crossing edge at the B vertex y. Its auxiliary matching D is nonempty.

The path W has endpoints d and y in A. Both are outside V(D): d was excluded in forming D, and y∉XA. Every edge of D is therefore internal to this path. Deleting a nonempty D separates its two original endpoints into different path components. After attachment, the original crossing edge at d and the new bridge at the other endpoint meet at the same B vertex y. They concatenate two DIFFERENT components and do not close a cycle. No other attached B endpoints coincide.

The resulting paths have distinct endpoints XB⧵{y} and disjoint interiors partitioning (A⧵{v})∪{y in B}. Compress them into a matching R. Then FB∪R has exactly the holes 0,7,11,y. The four holes are distinct because y∈XB, and their parities are again 1 even and 3 odd. A4_4 avoiding y yields a circle on B⧵{y}. Expanding R restores y and all of A⧵{v}, and yields the required 31-circle. Every crossing edge, including the one at d, is an original edge of F and is preserved.

7. Every canonical input admits one of these transfers

If a completion makes 7 or 11 available, choose it and that target. These vertices are B holes and hence outside XB, so Step 5 applies.

Otherwise we are in a finite stall class. For c=1 or c=3, at least four odd targets are available for some completions. At most c≤3 of them lie in XB. Choose one outside XB and a completion making it available, and use Step 5.

For c=5 or c=7, use the four-target set G supplied by the finite lemma. If some y∈G is outside XB, any completion making it available gives Step 5. Otherwise G⊆XB. Choose any y∈G, take its original crossing partner as root d, and choose ANY perfect matching D on XA⧵{d}. The universal zero-bad-count property ensures this particular root and completion admit target y. Also y∉XA and D≠∅. All hypotheses of Step 6 hold, proving the result.

There are no stalls for c≥9, so the first branch already handles them. This exhausts the canonical family and proves A4 by R1A.

Consequence for the actual P6 goal

The previously audited full six-hole reduction (SIX_HOLE_MIXED_AND_GEOMETRY.md, SIX_HOLE_COVERED_REDUCTION.md, SIX_HOLE_FREE_REDUCTION.md) has A4 as its remaining input. Once this closure proof and its finite checks are accepted, that conditional reduction becomes a proof for all six-hole short matchings of Q6 and all required free-root/opposite-target endpoint choices.

This is not the whole of P6. The 8,10,12,14,16,18-hole rooted-maximal levels are still separate unresolved obligations. The user goal must remain active.

COVERED_EIGHT_GEOMETRY_CENSUS.md — Covered-target eight-hole geometry census

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：e31b0f7403432934c4ad609bb4828ac43abd812d86555148f2664075e978af83。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json。

Covered-target eight-hole geometry census

Date: 2026-11-01. Scope: the R8-covered geometry in EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_DRAFT.md, with root 0 and covered target v=1,7,31. These normalize the three odd distances 1,3,5 under coordinate permutations. This is a geometry census only: no matching realizability assertion, no matching enumeration, and no A6/P6 closure.

review_independence: same-family; acceptance_status: provisional.

Complete domain and counts

For each target, enumerate all 3-subsets Z of the 31 nonzero even vertices, then every 4-subset W of odd vertices other than v, subject only to no short edge between Z and W. Adjacency to root 0 is allowed. Unlike the free-target census, adjacency from Z to v is allowed because v is covered.

For each coordinate, A is its face containing v and (a,b)=(|Z intersect A|,|W intersect A|). Retain a geometry if none of its six rows belongs to {(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3)}.

v All eligible geometries No good cut Orbits fixing 0 and v Stabilizer order
1 9168375 19530 278 120
7 9334641 22472 875 36
31 9347625 24125 345 120

All 66127 retained geometries are saved, without orbit reduction, in covered_eight_residual_1.bin, _7.bin, _31.bin. Each record consists of seven unsigned bytes: sorted Z[3], followed by sorted W[4]; v is in the filename. The three files contain 462889 bytes total. Every orbit representative, orbit size, six rows and splitting signature is additionally saved in covered_eight_geometry_census_independent_check.json (1498 orbits total).

Splitting Z and the missing rows

Every retained geometry has at least three coordinates with a=1 or a=2. The only bad rows on those coordinates are (1,0),(1,4),(2,0),(2,1). All four row types do occur. All eleven bad rows in the draft occur somewhere in the retained census, for every normalized target.

Every retained geometry has a coordinate with (a,b)=(2,0) or (2,1). Thus an extension handling these two rows would cover the residual geometries of this nine-row criterion, conditional on its other hypotheses. This is a geometric observation and supplies no transfer proof for either new row.

The more favorable condition "there is a (1,4) or (2,1) cut" fails on 10,20,20 geometries for v=1,7,31 respectively. All 50 exceptions have exactly the same six-row multiset: three copies of (2,0), three copies of (3,2). Their splitting coordinates therefore offer only (2,0), and none offers (1,0), (1,4), or (2,1). They form the following seven orbits under the target stabilizer:

Verification and reproduction

covered_eight_geometry_census.cpp exhaustively loops over the complete domain and writes the JSON and three residual files. Its good-row lookup is explicit and includes all nine rows. verify_covered_eight_geometry_census.py independently rechecks every retained record, duplicate exclusion, hole parities, independence, target exclusion, six rows, all summary distributions, and orbit sizes. It independently recomputes eligible-domain totals as sum over Z of binomial(number of allowed odd vertices,4), without iterating over W quadruples. The Python program does not independently rerun the entire 28-million-geometry no-good-cut selection; completeness of that selection is from the transparent exhaustive C++ loops. Orbit sets are generated under all coordinate permutations preserving v, and must partition the retained record set exactly. JSON evidence includes source and record SHA-256 hashes.

g++ -O3 -std=c++17 research/six_directions/covered_eight_geometry_census.cpp -o research/six_directions/covered_eight_geometry_census.exe
research\six_directions\covered_eight_geometry_census.exe research/six_directions

Both programs completed successfully. These results identify the remaining geometry for further proof work; they do not establish that any particular retained hole set admits a short matching or solves R8-covered.

DISTANCE_TWO_ALL_TARGETS.md — E2、E3、Z11：换切分消除单孔侧半层障碍

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：41b5514d63a43bd0e1e1fd47453532f8264dccf23f454b56623c74a82e5654a6。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_COVERED_REVIEW.json。

E2、E3、Z11：换切分消除单孔侧半层障碍

日期：2026-11-01。状态：证明草稿，待独立审计。完整 P6 未证明。

约定与依赖

顶点采用六位整数编码，坐标从 0 起。p(x) 是汉明重量模二，ei=2i。短边是超立方体边；辅助匹配可以是完整图匹配。一个面内方向 j 的半层有该面四分之一顶点数那么多条边，其端点集由除 j 外的坐标和的奇偶性决定。记端点集为 S，补集为 T。S,T 内部的短边都只沿 j；含有该半层的匹配，其全部短边因此只沿 j。同在 T 的同奇偶顶点有相同的第 j 位，异奇偶顶点则相反。

依赖已保存的 N10、Z8，以及 AVOIDED_VERTEX_TRANSFER.md 的 N11、N12、Z9。以下 E2、E3 是新的局部引理，不假设 P6。

E2：交叉坐标面的半层互斥

设 n≥4，S0 是 K(Qn) 的匹配，未覆盖 v。记 Ai 为包含 v 的第 i 坐标面。若 S0[Ai] 含方向 j≠i 的半层 H，则 S0[Aj] 不含任何半层。

证明：v 不在 H 中。H 在 Aj 中的端点恰为

U={x:xi=vi, xj=vj, p(x)≠p(v)}.

每个 x∈U 已沿 j 与 Aj 外的顶点匹配。若 S0[Aj] 含方向 k≠j 的半层 K，则 K 避开 v。对于 Aj 内与 v 异奇偶的 x，x 属于 K 的端点集当且仅当 xk=vk。若 k=i，整个 U 都是这样的点；若 i,j,k 两两不同，固定这三个坐标后，因 n≥4 还有至少一个自由坐标，可以选择奇偶使 x∈U。因此两种情况下均有 x 同时被 H,K 覆盖，却分别沿不同方向 j,k 匹配，矛盾。证毕。

E3：同侧目标的构造或刚性障碍

设 M 是 Q6 的短匹配，恰有四孔 u,z,w,t，其中 u,z 偶、w,t 奇。沿方向 i 切为 A,B，u 是 A 中唯一的原孔，z,w,t∈B。指定已覆盖奇目标 v∈A。假设

b=w⊕ei≠u,e=t⊕ei≠u.

记 h=M(v)，M*=(M⧵{vh})∪{hu}。至少有下列结论之一：

  1. Z9 的条件可满足，得到包含 M 的 Hamilton u—v 路径；
  2. MA* 含方向 j≠i 的半层 H，它避开 u,v,b,e；原 MA 的全部边都沿 j，且
    uj=wj=tj≠vj.
证明

b,e 原本均由 MA 覆盖，因为它们不是孔且其跨面邻点为孔。收缩后仍由 MA* 覆盖：若其中之一等于 h，它改由 hu 覆盖。原跨边数是正奇数，收缩保持跨边数。MA* 最多含一个半层，因为含半层迫使所有短边同方向，而同方向的两个半层会覆盖整个 A，与自由点 v 矛盾。

若跨边至少三条，且 MA* 不含半层，任取 b,e 之一删除其匹配边，便可用 N12 和 Z9。若其唯一半层覆盖 b,e 中至少一点，删除该点的匹配边同样可用 N12 和 Z9。其余情况即半层 H 避开 b,e,v。若 h∈A，同偶边 hu 不属于短半层，且不能接触其已覆盖的端点，所以 u,h∈T；若 h∈B，则 MA*=MA，其原孔 u∈T。故 H 也避开 u。

以下只有一条跨边。

若 h∈A，令 a 为唯一 A 端口。原 MA 恰漏 u,a，所以 a 奇。若 MA* 无半层，在 b,e 中选择不等于 h 的一点（也不等于 u），其伙伴 k 奇。若唯一半层覆盖某个候选，则选择该点，其伙伴 k 也奇，因为 hu 不属于半层。删除所选短边后不再有半层，加入同奇边 ak 不会形成新的短半层。取空配对 D，Z9 成立。余下只可能是半层避开 b,e,u,v。

若 h∈B，唯一原跨边为 vh，收缩后唯一端口为 u，且 LA=MA*=MA 恰漏 u,v。记两个候选压缩为

Tb=(LA⧵{bLA(b)})∪{uLA(b)},Te=(LA⧵{eLA(e)})∪{uLA(e)}.

若其中一个无半层，Z9 成立。否则第一个半层至少有七条短边来自 LA；第二次压缩最多再删除其中一条，所以第二个半层方向必须相同。它们都避开 v，因而是同一个 H。其补集 T 含 v,b,e。b,e 同偶且 LA 二部，故 bLA(b) 在 Te 中仍然保留；由 b∈T 得 k=LA(b)∈T。新增边 uk 不能属于 H，因此 H⊆LA，也避开自由点 u。

所有未构造成功的分支均产生所述 H。u,b,e 同偶且属于 T，v 奇且属于 T，故 uj=bj=ej≠vj。因 j≠i，bj=wj,ej=tj。最后，若 h∈B，MA=MA* 的短边全沿 j；若 h∈A，v,h∈T 且原 vh 是短边，所以 vh 也沿 j。其余原 MA 边仍在 MA*，因此原 MA 的全部边沿 j。证毕。

Z11：距离二且能隔离根的四孔，全部目标

设 M 为 Q6 短匹配，四孔为 u,z,w,t，u,z 同奇偶、距离二，w,t 为另一奇偶。若某坐标能将 u 与另外三个孔隔开，则对每个与 u 异奇偶的 v，均存在包含 M 的 Hamilton u—v 路径。

这去掉 Z8 中“目标必须在三孔侧”的限制，但仍要求存在所述隔离坐标。

证明

平移取 u=0。令隔离方向为 i，另一非零坐标为 l，则 z=ei+el。若 v=w,t，用 N8；若 z 邻接 w 或 t，添加该边得到避开根的近完美短匹配，用 N10。因此以下 v 已覆盖，且上述两对均不相邻。

取 A={x:xi=0}。c=z⊕ei=el 由 MA 覆盖；b=w⊕ei,e=t⊕ei 也由 MA 覆盖且均不等于 u。若 vi=1，Z8 已证明结论。设 vi=0，应用 E3。第一种结论已完成构造；否则得到方向 j 的半层，wj=tj=0,vj=1，原 MA 全沿 j。

由于 c=el 被原 MA 覆盖，若 j=l，其原伙伴必为自由点 u，矛盾。因此 j∉{i,l}，从而 zj=0。

改沿 j 切分，A′={x:xj=1} 包含 v，B′={x:xj=0} 包含 u,z,w,t。M* 的孔恰为 v,z,w,t，故 A′ 只有一个孔 v。E2 应用于同一个 M* 及原半层 H，保证 MA′* 不含半层。H 的八条边现在全部是跨边，且单孔侧的跨边数为奇数，所以至少有九条。

考虑两个桥接候选 w⊕ej,t⊕ej∈A′。它们原来由 MA′ 覆盖，因为其短跨面邻点是孔，且自身不是孔。u∈B′，收缩唯一可能使其中的 h 改为跨端口；两个候选不同，至少另一个仍由 MA′* 覆盖。选择该候选，删除其匹配边后依然无半层，且跨端口至少九个，满足 N12 和 Z9 的充分条件。Z9 给出所需原 u—v 路径。证毕。

未关闭范围

未隔离根的四孔配置、其他同奇偶距离，以及六孔以上仍须另证。本文件的局部命题不能代替完整 P6；计算实例也不能代替上述全称论证。

DISTANCE_TWO_UNBALANCED.md — Z8：两个同奇偶孔距离2的一孔/三孔切分

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：655b63481f6539aa9303984aa2dfbe95bcca9912fc74a014794812d999611f94。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：GENERAL_NEAR_PERFECT_REVIEW.json。

Z8：两个同奇偶孔距离2的一孔/三孔切分

日期：2026-11-01。状态：局部证明，独立审读记录见GENERAL_NEAR_PERFECT_REVIEW.md。完整P6仍未证明。

陈述

M为Q6短边匹配，恰不覆盖u,z,w,t；u,z同奇偶，w,t为另一奇偶，且d(u,z)=2。若存在坐标i，使u独自在一层A，z,w,t和指定异奇偶目标v全部在另一层B，则M有Hamilton u—v延拓。

不要求其他平衡切分存在；不要求层内原短边使用两个方向。

证明

通过平移令u=0，因此z偶、w,t,v奇，u_i=0而z_i=w_i=t_i=v_i=1。

若v是自由点，使用N8。以下v已覆盖。若z与w或t相邻，将该短边加入M，得到保持u自由的近完美短匹配，使用N10（或已证N3）。以下这两对孔均不相邻。

令c=z⊕e_i、d=w⊕e_i、e=t⊕e_i。c是u的短邻点。d,e不等于u：若w=e_i，则d(z,w)=1，已在上一分支处理；t同理。c,d,e都被M_A覆盖，因为其B侧邻点是孔。c与d,e距离分别等于d(z,w)、d(z,t)，均非1，所以cd,ce不属于M_A。

记C为原跨边，X_A为A侧端口。M_A的未覆盖集X_A∪{u}奇偶平衡，所以|X_A|为正奇数。

分支一：只有一条跨边

写C={ab}，a∈A、b∈B。u偶迫使a奇、b偶。M_A恰有孔u,a，Fink完美匹配圈定理加入ua再删除ua，给出Hamilton u—a路径。M_B是Q5短匹配，b未覆盖，且v奇。因此原五方向端点定理（2501.19029v1.pdf Theorem 8，其自由根分支，亦见CORE_DERIVATION.md的D5）给出包含M_B的Hamilton b—v路径。通过原跨边ab拼接，得到所需路径。

分支二：至少三条跨边

令j为原短边cM_A(c)的方向。c仅有一个1位，若j是该位，则M_A(c)=0=u，矛盾；所以c_j=u_j=0。

X_A至少含两个奇点：|X_A|≥3且奇点比偶点多1。选择奇点a∈X_A，满足a≠u⊕e_j；至多一个候选被排除。先将u与a配对，再把(X_A∪{u}){u,a}的两奇偶类任意配对，得到二部配对D。令P_A=M_A∪D。

假设P_A在端点(c,d)、(c,e)的两次压缩都含半层。由UNBALANCED_CORE_THEOREM.md的E1，两次半层必为同一方向j的同一半层H，而且H完整包含于P_A。其端点集S的补集T含c。

因为c为奇顶点且c_j=0，c去掉第j位后的坐标和为奇，故T由这一奇和条件刻画。u=0去掉第j位后的和为偶，所以u∈S。H⊆P_A迫使P_A(u)=u⊕e_j；但构造给出P_A(u)=a≠u⊕e_j，矛盾。

故至少一次压缩无半层。对应端点不属于P_A的同一条边，GNS二部完美匹配端点定理给出Hamilton c—d或c—e延拓。应用Z6，得到Hamilton u—v延拓。证毕。

边界

原五方向定理仅用于单跨边分支中的短匹配M_B，不用于含长边的转移匹配。多跨边分支允许D含长边，Z6第二层明确调用N10的完整图版本。

本命题包含Z7的几何配置，但仍要求目标与另外三个孔同处B；不处理没有根单独一侧的配置，也不处理目标在A的情形。

EIGHT_HOLE_A1B4_DRAFT.md — Eight-hole covered targets: the a=1,b=4 row

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：e71d671feabac1fd817d1111def25d2e457afd1dca863f6aeb68b5be3c941d68。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_HOLE_A1B4_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json。

Eight-hole covered targets: the a=1,b=4 row

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft; independent review pending. The new input T44_5 is proved in T44_Q5_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md and audited PASS in T44_Q5_CLOSURE_REVIEW.md/.json. Full eight-hole P6 remains open.

Claim

Let M be a short matching of Q6 with eight holes, u a free even root, and v a covered odd target. Let Z be the other three even holes and W the four odd holes. Assume Z union W is independent. Suppose some coordinate cut has, in the face A containing v, exactly one vertex z of Z and all four vertices of W. Then M extends to a Hamilton u--v path. This is precisely the previously bad row (a,b)=(1,4).

Use global parity on both faces. Let B be the other face, let delta be 1 when u belongs to A and 0 otherwise. Let M_A,M_B be internal required edges, C the original crossing matching, and X_A,X_B its endpoint sets. Every crossing edge is short, and therefore joins mirror coordinates.

Inputs
  • Q5 K4: arbitrary complete-graph matching with two holes of each parity has a Hamilton path from every free root to any opposite-parity target, including covered targets. It follows from the already audited A4/N10 results; see SIX_HOLE_MIXED_AND_GEOMETRY.md and their closure reviews.
  • Q5 T44_5: four same-parity holes, avoid any prescribed two, obtain a 30-cycle containing the matching, with only short new edges.
  • Elementary tagged endpoint closure and simultaneous two-conflict path compression, detailed below. The corresponding method was audited in EIGHT_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_REVIEW.md for the (2,1) row, but the present hole counts and parity-reversed conflicts are checked explicitly here.
1. Choose the bridges and complete the first face

Choose two distinct holes w1,w2 in W whose B mirrors y1,y2 are not u. If delta=1 no mirror equals u; if delta=0 at most one of the four mirrors equals u, so at least three candidates remain. The mirrors are even. They cannot be other original holes: a nonroot even hole adjacent to a member of W would contradict independence. They cannot be crossing ports either: their unique short A neighbor is the original hole wj. Thus both yj are internally covered by M_B, with distinct odd partners kj.

Since M_A is bipartite, the even-minus-odd port count in A equals the odd-minus-even ORIGINAL hole count. Hence

|X_A intersect E| - |X_A intersect O| = 4-(1+delta)=3-delta.

If delta=1, c=|C| is even and at least two. Pair X_A union {w1,w2} arbitrarily into an artificial matching D and put r=u. The matching L_A=M_A union D has precisely four holes: u,z even, and the two members of W other than w1,w2 odd. D is nonempty and avoids r.

If delta=0, c is odd and at least three. Choose any even port r in X_A; one exists by the displayed surplus. Pair (X_A minus {r}) union {w1,w2} into D. Now L_A has four holes r,z even and the other two members of W odd. D is again nonempty and avoids r.

K4 supplies a Hamilton r--v path P_A in A containing L_A. Its other new edges are short. This invocation permits v to be internally covered or to be a port covered by D; r is even, so r != v.

2. Transfer all original crossings and both bridges

Delete D from P_A, attach every original crossing edge, and add the two short bridges wj-yj. Every added B attachment is at a distinct vertex: the ports X_B, y1,y2 are disjoint. Therefore the result is a path forest.

All A vertices now have degree two except the global endpoints lying in A. For delta=1, r=u keeps degree one. For delta=0, r is a crossing port and its original crossing restores its degree to two. The holes wj were covered by D; removing their D edge reduces degree by one and their new bridges restore it. Other ports lose a D edge and gain a crossing edge. If v is a port, its sole path edge belongs to D: deletion temporarily isolates v, and its original crossing restores degree one. If v is internally matched, its endpoint degree was unchanged.

For delta=1 the nonempty D separates u and v into different path components, giving two distinct terminal segments to B. For delta=0 there is one terminal segment from v to B and u is an original free B vertex. Temporarily add a tagged artificial edge uv. In the former case it joins the two terminal segments into a B-to-B path; in the latter it extends the terminal segment to the distinct B endpoint u. It creates no cycle at this stage. Compress all resulting B-to-B paths into a matching T, recording each expansion and the unique edge carrying the tag.

For delta=1 the endpoint set of T is X_B union Y; for delta=0 it is X_B union Y union {u}, where Y={y1,y2}. Every A vertex occurs once in the interiors of these transferred paths. The only overlap between vertices covered by T and M_B is Y.

3. Suppress the two conflicts and invoke T44_5

Each yj has the original M_B edge yj-kj, with kj odd. The kj are distinct, internally covered, and outside the endpoint set of T. In particular no original matching edge joins y1 and y2, since both are even.

In M_B union T, the only degree-two vertices are y1,y2. Every component meeting Y is a path: its original matching edge reaches a degree-one vertex kj. If T joins y1,y2, the component is k1-y1-y2-k2; otherwise there are two distinct paths. Suppress Y along these paths to produce a matching L of K(B), retaining all expansion data and the tag.

If delta=1, the original B holes are the two even members of Z outside A. After the port transfer and suppression, L has precisely those two holes together with y1,y2, hence four even holes.

If delta=0, the original B holes are u and the two even members of Z outside A. The tagged closure consumes u, while suppression exposes y1,y2. The final four holes are again (Z minus {z}) union {y1,y2}, all even.

Apply T44_5 to L, avoiding exactly y1,y2. It gives a single 30-vertex circle in B minus Y containing all required compressed edges. Undo every suppression and path compression. This restores both avoided bridge vertices and all 32 A vertices, each once, to give a single 64-vertex circle containing every original edge of M and the tagged uv edge. Delete the tagged edge to get the desired Hamilton u--v path.

Every surviving edge outside M is either a local short edge supplied by K4/T44_5 or one of the two short bridges. All artificial D edges were deleted; all compressed edges were expanded; the possibly long tag uv was removed. This proves the claimed row for every original matching.

Scope and geometric accounting

For the earlier R8-covered domain, all its 66127 normalized hole geometries are listed in covered_eight_residual_1/7/31.bin. Of these, 24669 have at least one (1,4) cut: 7535,8319,8815 for the three targets. The new row therefore closes every realizing matching for those geometries. The remaining geometry counts are 11995,14153,15310, totaling 41458. Of these 41408 have an a2b1 cut, while 50 have none (the previously identified seven exceptional orbits). These are hole-geometry counts, not counts of matchings or a claim that every geometry is realizable.

The remaining (2,1) route still needs nonadjacent Q5 T15, and the last 50 geometries still need another argument such as a proved EP0 cut selection. Full eight-hole P6, the higher layers, and full P6 remain open.

EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_DRAFT.md — Eight-hole reduction: complete free-target branch and exact covered residual

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：39a5632be39ab0ac6a6ea5e1ee3125ad2cb049edf72f819972e21b31eee1d88b。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json, Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json, Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json, TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json。

Eight-hole reduction: complete free-target branch and exact covered residual

Date: 2026-11-01. Authoring route: ARIS proof-writer. Independent proof-checker review is still required. This document does not close eight holes or full P6.

Claim

Let M⊆E(Q6) have exactly eight holes, let u be a free root, and let v have the opposite parity. The original objective is a Hamilton u--v path containing M.

The claims proved here are:

  1. Assuming Q5 A6, the objective holds for every free target v.
  2. Assuming Q5 A6, it holds for every covered target satisfying the explicit nine-row cut criterion below, or the preliminary augmentation.
  3. Assuming Q5 A6, full eight-hole P6 is equivalent to the additional universal residual obligation R8-covered stated in Section 7.

The third statement is a complete domain partition, not a claim that A6 already implies R8-covered. R8-covered is nonempty, even among realizable short-matchings, as witnessed in Section 8.

Status

PROVABLE AFTER EXTRA ASSUMPTION, for claims 1--3, relative to the explicit imports and the exhaustive geometry certificate below. NOT CURRENTLY JUSTIFIED, for the implication A6 alone implies full eight-hole P6. No such implication is asserted.

Assumptions and notation

Import full six-hole Q6 P6 from SIX_HOLE_CLOSED.md, full Q5 A4 from CANONICAL_A4_CLOSURE.md, and Q5 N10/N14/K4 from their recorded proofs. The A4 closure audit is CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.json; its PASS is relative to imported theorems and finite certificates, with same-family, provisional assurance. Older six-hole proof files retain historical open-A4 wording; this document uses the later closure, not that historical status. Import the established five-direction free-root endpoint theorem.

A6, the only new auxiliary assumption, says that every matching of K(Q5) with hole counts 2,4 extends, using only short new edges, to a circle covering exactly Q5−v for each specified majority-parity hole v. The matching edges may be arbitrary, including long same-parity edges.

Use a cube automorphism to put u=0 and hence make u even. Write the other even holes as Z={z1,z2,z3} and all odd holes as W, |W|=4. The target v is odd and may or may not belong to W. For a coordinate i, let A be the face containing v, and B the other. Set

a=|Z∩A|,b=|W∩A|,δ=1[u∈A].

Thus the original hole counts in A are (a+δ,b) and those in B are (4−a−δ,4−b), in the order even/odd. Let MA,MB be internal matching edges, let C be the matching edges crossing the cut, and let XA,XB be their endpoint sets. Put c=|C|.

Dependency map
  1. A6 plus A4/N14/K4/N10 gives the general local endpoint lemma in Section 1.
  2. That lemma gives all nine-row cut transfers in Sections 3--5.
  3. A finite complete hole-geometry check gives every free-target input one of these cuts; Section 6 handles its one root-bridge boundary case.
  4. Covered inputs outside these reductions are exactly R8-covered.
Proof
1. General local endpoint lemma

For a vertex x, write ϵ(x)=1 for even and −1 for odd. Let F⊆K(Q5) have 2t holes, 1≤t≤3, with even-minus-odd hole count h∈{−2,0,2}. If r is free and y≠r satisfies

ϵ(r)+ϵ(y)=h,

then F has a Hamilton r--y extension with only short new edges. For h=0 this includes arbitrary opposite-parity targets. For h=±2 both endpoints have the majority hole parity.

If y is free, add the auxiliary edge ry. The remaining holes are balanced and number 2t−2∈{0,2,4}. A full circle extension follows respectively from the perfect-matching theorem, N10, or K4. Delete ry. If y is covered, put k=F(y) and F′=F−yk+kr. Its hole imbalance is 2ϵ(y): this follows by subtracting the free root and adding the new free target to the old holes. Its total hole count remains 2t. Apply N14, A4, or A6 for t=1,2,3, avoiding y. Delete kr and append the original edge ky. Every introduced long edge has been deleted.

In particular, balanced matchings with 2,4,6 holes have full circle extensions: take any free root and a short neighbor as target in this lemma, and close the resulting Hamilton path. The edge between the two ends is not already in a path on 32 vertices. All these statements allow arbitrary required matching edges, so they apply to compressed transfers.

2. Preprocessing and forest bookkeeping

If any two vertices of Z∪W are adjacent, add their short edge to M. This preserves the free root and yields six holes. Full six-hole P6 solves the original endpoint problem. Hence assume Z∪W independent.

If v∈W and uv is short, add uv to M and apply six-hole P6 to obtain a full circle containing this enlarged matching: use any remaining free root, a short neighbor as its target, and close the Hamilton path. Delete uv. Thus in the free-target census d(u,v) is 3 or 5.

If c=0 for any selected cut, all original matching edges use at most five directions. The imported five-direction theorem solves the original endpoint problem. Below c>0.

In each transfer choose an artificial matching D in A. A Hamilton path PA supplied by Section 1 contains MA+D. When u∈A, its ends are u,v; when u∈B, its ends are an even port p∈XA and v. Delete D, attach all real crossedges, and optionally one bridge xy from an original hole x∈A to its mirror y∈B.

The resulting graph is a path forest. Each newly attached B vertex is distinct and attached once. If the covered target v belongs to XA, deleting its incident D edge can isolate it, but attaching its original crossedge immediately gives its terminal segment. All other artificial edges avoid path endpoints. The degrees in A become two except for the actual endpoints u,v that lie there.

For δ=1, D is nonempty, so there are two distinct terminal segments u--r and s--v, with r,s∈B; compress the other segments into a matching R. For δ=0, there is one terminal segment r--v; compress the others into R. If a bridge is present, these B segment endpoints are in XB∪{y}; otherwise in XB.

An internal bridge endpoint y is internally matched by MB. If it belongs to R, it produces exactly one conflict. With k=MB(y) and d=R(y) replace the two edges by

FB=(MB−yk)∪(R−yd)∪{kd}.

This is a matching because k is internally covered and d is a different crossport. Ultimately expand kd to the original ky followed by the corresponding y--d transfer segment. This restores y once. Other compressed edges expand into their disjoint segments.

3. Zero bridges: b=a+1, a∈{0,1,2}

If δ=1, pair all of XA into D. Its size is even: internal short edges give |XA∩E|−|XA∩O|=b−a−1=0. Since c>0, D is nonempty. The holes of MA+D are balanced, (a+1,a+1), so Section 1 gives the u--v path in A. After transfer MB+R+rs is a matching with balanced holes (3−a,3−a). Use its full circle, delete rs, expand and attach the two terminal segments.

If δ=0, the same port difference is b−a=1, so an even port p exists. Pair XA−{p} into D. The holes become balanced (a+1,a+1); use the p--v path. Now MB+R+ur has balanced holes (3−a,3−a): the extra free B root u is consumed by ur. Its circle, with ur deleted, expands to the required path.

The values a=0,1,2 ensure all the local balanced matchings have at most six holes. Artificial rs or ur joins distinct free vertices.

4. One even hole consumed: b=a, a∈{1,2,3}

Choose x∈Z∩A, and let y=x⊕ei in B. Independence of Z∪W implies y∉W. It cannot equal even root u. As its cross-cut neighbor is the free vertex x, y is internally covered by MB. The bridge xy is short and y is odd.

If δ=1, pair XA∪{x} into D; the port difference is −1, so c is odd. If δ=0, the port classes are equal and c>0, so choose an even port p and pair (XA−{p})∪{x} into D. In both cases D is nonempty, and the resulting holes in A are balanced (a,a). Section 1 applies.

If y is not a terminal segment endpoint, perform the single-conflict compression and add rs (δ=1) or ur (δ=0). The holes are exactly (3−a,5−a) and include y in the odd majority. Apply A6/A4/N14 for a=1/2/3, avoiding y, then delete the auxiliary endpoint edge and expand the conflict to restore y.

If y is a terminal endpoint and δ=1, write q for the other terminal endpoint. The matching L=MB+R has original B holes (3−a,4−a) plus q, while y is covered. Its total hole count is 8−2a≤6. The imbalance is 0 when q is even and −2 when q is odd; Section 1 gives a q--y path in either case. If δ=0 and y is the terminal endpoint, L=MB+R has balanced holes (4−a,4−a), also at most six, and Section 1 gives u--y. Expand and attach the terminal segment(s). These are all possible positions of y.

5. One odd hole consumed: b=a+2, a∈{0,1,2}

Choose x∈W∩A different from v if v is free, such that y=x⊕ei≠u. Independence implies y∉Z; because x is free its mirror y is internally covered by MB. Thus y is even. For a covered target there are at least two choices of x, at most one with mirror u. For a free target and a≥1 there are again at least two choices after excluding v. For a=0, the only failure of this choice is treated separately in Section 6.

If δ=1, pair XA∪{x} into D. The port difference is 1, so c is positive odd and D is nonempty. If δ=0, port difference is 2; choose an even port p and pair (XA−{p})∪{x} into D. In both cases the A holes are balanced (a+1,a+1); Section 1 supplies the required path.

If y is not terminal, conflict compression followed by rs or ur leaves exactly (4−a,2−a) holes, with y in the even majority. Apply A6/A4/N14 for a=0/1/2, avoiding y, delete the auxiliary endpoint edge, and expand to restore y.

If y is terminal and δ=1, the matching L=MB+R has holes (3−a,2−a) plus the other terminal endpoint q. Its total hole count is 6−2a. The imbalance is 2 for even q and 0 for odd q; Section 1 gives a q--y path. For δ=0 and terminal y, L=MB+R has holes (4−a,2−a) and Section 1 gives u--y. Expand and attach the terminal segments.

Thus the good cut rows proved in Sections 3--5 are precisely

a allowed b
0 1,2
1 1,2,3
2 2,3,4
3 3

In every branch all added edges remaining after expansion are short. The forest followed by a single local path gives one global Hamilton path, rather than merely satisfying the required vertex degrees.

6. Free targets: exceptional root bridge and exhaustive geometry

The bridge-choice exception from Section 5 has a=0,b=2,δ=0, W∩A={v,x}, and x⊕ei=u. Here use a different first path: pair all XA into D. The holes in MA+D are exactly x,v, both odd. N10 gives a Hamilton x--v path. The port imbalance is 2, so c≥2 is even and D is nonempty. Delete D, attach the crossedges, and attach ux. There are two distinct terminal segments u--r and s--v, and a matching R on all other crossports. Now

LB=MB+R+rs

has exactly four even holes, including u, and two odd holes. A6 avoiding u gives a circle on B−u. Delete rs, expand R, and attach the two terminal segments, the first of which restores u via its bridge. This covers all vertices once and preserves M.

It remains a pure geometry statement that a good cut always exists for free targets after preprocessing. The executable certificate is eight_hole_free_cut_census.cpp. Normalize u=0. An odd free target at distance 1 was settled in Section 2. Permuting coordinates sends every distance-3 target to v=7 and every distance-5 target to v=31. For each of these two targets the certificate enumerates:

  1. Every unordered triple of distinct nonzero even vertices Z, none adjacent to v.
  2. Every unordered triple of odd vertices different from v and nonadjacent to every member of Z; adding v forms W.
  3. Every one of the six cuts, testing membership in the displayed table.

No root-other-hole adjacency is excluded. Same-parity pairs cannot be adjacent, so these loops enumerate exactly every geometry remaining after Section 2, with no realizability assumption or missing matching quantifier. In particular they may include geometries admitting no short matching, which only strengthens the coverage assertion.

Compiled using g++ -O3 -std=c++17; observed output:

v=7 total=1300674 bad=0
v=31 total=1287690 bad=0

The census certifies a cut property only. The transfer proofs work for every short matching realizing the holes, without enumerating matchings. They also handle the exceptional root bridge just proved. Therefore A6 implies the original eight-hole statement for all free targets.

7. Exact residual covered-target obligation

Define R8-covered as follows. For every M⊆E(Q6) with holes {0}∪Z∪W, where Z consists of three distinct nonzero even vertices, W consists of four odd vertices, and Z∪W is independent, and every odd covered target v∉W, assume that for every coordinate i, the counts in the face containing v obey

(ai,bi)∈B={(0,0),(0,3),(0,4),(1,0),(1,4),(2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1),(3,2),(3,4)}.

Then require a Hamilton 0--v path containing M. One may additionally assume that M uses all six directions; the five-direction theorem already handles the others.

The set B is the exact complement of the nine good rows inside {0,1,2,3}×{0,1,2,3,4}. Thus every eight-hole input is covered by exactly the following exhaustive decision:

  • a nonroot adjacent hole pair: six-hole reduction;
  • a free target: Section 6;
  • a covered target with at least one good cut: Sections 3--5;
  • a covered target with no good cut: R8-covered.

Consequently A6 plus R8-covered suffices for full eight-hole P6. Conversely, full eight-hole P6 implies R8-covered just by specialization. This is the claimed exact additional obligation for this reduction scheme; it is not a proof that R8-covered is logically independent of A6.

8. Realizable obstruction to completeness of the nine-row transfer

Let u=0, Z={6,17,53}, W={11,35,41,47}, and v=4. The six rows (ai,bi), in bit order i=0,…,5, are

(1,0),(2,1),(2,1),(3,1),(1,4),(2,1).

All belong to B, and Z∪W is independent. These holes are realized by the following short 28-edge matching (each pair has Hamming distance one):

(3,1) (5,4) (9,13) (10,2) (12,14) (15,31) (18,16)
(20,21) (23,22) (24,26) (27,19) (29,25) (30,28) (33,49)
(34,32) (36,38) (39,7) (40,8) (43,42) (45,37) (46,44)
(48,50) (51,55) (54,52) (57,56) (58,59) (60,61) (63,62)

Thus it would be false to say that the nine-row cut argument by itself covers all eight-hole inputs. This is an obstruction to that argument, not a counterexample to P6 or to the possible sufficiency of A6.

Corrections or missing assumptions

A6 is still open. R8-covered is not proved here. The available proofs establish full free-target coverage conditional on A6 and a precise nonempty residual for covered targets; they do not establish an A6-only reduction for every covered target.

Open risks
  • This is an unaudited draft; the complete geometry certificate needs an independent domain-coverage and implementation review.
  • Imported closure results retain their documented assurance scope.
  • Eight-hole closure would still leave the 10--18-hole levels of P6.
