原件：打开文件。SHA-256：c0842d977f047171456d1284c58468eab8437458c3864d8f922a131bd7934f1e。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_ALL_EP0_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json。

Eight-hole covered endpoints: a two-bridge core and an exposed-port reduction

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer working draft; independent review pending. This file changes no earlier proof or main research state.

Claim and status

The original objective remains the Hamilton path from a free even root u to a covered odd target v containing an arbitrary eight-hole short matching of Q6. NOT CURRENTLY JUSTIFIED for all covered targets, even with A6 available.

The new conditional results proved below are:

  1. Any cut with (a,b)=(2,1) is solved by the explicit Q5 core T15 defined below.
  2. Any cut with (a,b)=(2,0) is solved by T15 plus the explicitly quantified exposed-port path condition EP0 at that cut.
  3. The endpoint-position branches in both transfers can be handled by one tagged closure and simultaneous path compression. No unproved terminal-mirror shortcut is needed.
  4. EP0 cannot be justified merely by choosing an arbitrary (2,0) cut: for each of 21 cuts of seven listed exceptional geometries, an explicit realizing short matching has no eligible exposed-port edge at all. Across all three cuts of each of those seven geometries, however, at least one eligible edge always exists. The latter is certified by explicit Hall obstructions, not a Hamilton sample.

Results 1--2 have status PROVABLE AFTER EXTRA ASSUMPTION, namely T15 and, for result 2, EP0. Neither new core is claimed proved. The combinatorial transfer proof below uses N10 and elementary compression; it does not use A6. A6 is available for the previously established nine good rows and free-target theorem.

1. Imports, notation and exact new obligations

Use the eight-hole notation of EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_DRAFT.md: u=0, three other even holes Z, four odd holes W, and Z∪W independent. The target v is odd and covered. In cut coordinate i, let A contain v, let B be the opposite face, and put a=|Z∩A|, b=|W∩A|, δ=1[u∈A]. Let MA,MB be internal matching edges and XA,XB the crossing-port sets. Write x¯=x⊕ei for the short mirror. All crossing edges are short, so each crossing port is matched to its mirror.

Import N10 from GENERAL_NEAR_PERFECT.md: an arbitrary matching of K(Q5) with holes r,q has a Hamilton r--v extension with short new edges whenever v≠r has the parity of q. Long and same-parity edges of an artificial completion matching are allowed. Import the established five-direction free-root endpoint theorem to dispose of c=0. Full A6, if used outside this file, retains its separate audit and dependency scope.

T15, an unproved Q5 two-avoidance core. For every matching L of K(Q5) with exactly one even and five odd holes, and every specified pair of distinct odd holes y1,y2, require a cycle through exactly V(Q5)⧵{y1,y2} containing L, with short new edges. The assertion includes its parity reversal. This is a 30-vertex cycle assertion. It does not follow from A6 by merely changing the omitted-hole count.

For an (a,b)=(2,0) cut write Z∩A={z1,z2} and S={w¯:w∈W}⊂A. Each s∈S is even; independence gives S∩{z1,z2}=∅. Since its mirror is an original free vertex, s is not a crossing port. It is internally covered by MA, except that s=u is possible when δ=1.

EP0, a local sufficient condition, not an established universal lemma. Choose r=u if δ=1; if δ=0, choose either member of {z1,z2} as r. Require the existence, in this order, of

q∈XA∩O,D a perfect matching on (XA⧵{q})∪({z1,z2}⧵{r}),

and a Hamilton r--v path P containing MA∪D, with short new edges, such that qs∈E(P) for some s∈S. All quantifiers are existential after the cut and original matching are fixed. The formula removes r from {z1,z2} only when it belongs to that set. The port q may equal v when v is a crossing port. The vertex s may equal u when δ=1.

The matching MA∪D has exactly the holes r,q. Thus N10 guarantees some such r--v path, for every admissible choice of q,D; it does not guarantee the additional edge qs. The existential edge requirement is precisely the unproved part of EP0. In particular XA∩O merely containing a neighbor of S is weaker than EP0.

Dependency map: N10 plus the selected completions -> first A path; a short bridge at each consumed nonroot even hole -> two odd internally covered mirrors in B; tagged terminal closure plus two-vertex compression -> an arbitrary K(Q5) matching with hole counts (1,5); T15 -> final global path. EP0 adds one optional edge deletion and a bridge to an original B hole, which preserves the same final hole counts in the (2,0) row.

2. A unified closure and two-conflict compression

The constructions below start from an A path, delete artificial edges, and attach each real crossing edge plus specified bridges. Their attached B vertices are all distinct. They therefore form a path forest, whose A interiors are disjoint and cover A. Every A vertex has degree two except the specified global endpoints that lie in A. The covered target v may belong to XA: removing its D edge can isolate it, after which attaching its real crossing edge gives its terminal segment.

When δ=1, there are two different terminal segments, from u and v to B; removing a nonempty D from the first A path separates the original endpoints. When δ=0, there is one terminal segment from v to B; u is still a free B vertex. Temporarily join the global endpoints by a tagged artificial edge uv. For δ=1 this joins the two terminal segments into a B-to-B path; for δ=0 it extends the terminal segment to the B endpoint u. Compress this tagged path and all other B-to-B segments. They give a matching T on their distinct B endpoints. The tag belongs to exactly one compressed edge. This is a proof device: uv is removed at the end, so its length is immaterial.

In both applications the only overlap of covered vertices between T and MB is the set Y={y1,y2} of the two odd bridge mirrors. Each yj is internally covered by an original edge yjkj, where kj is an even internally covered B vertex outside the endpoint set of T. The two kj are distinct. Since Y has one parity and MB is short, no MB edge joins the two members of Y.

The union MB∪T thus has degree two exactly on Y, and degree at most one elsewhere. Every component containing a member of Y is a path: it has the degree-one neighbor kj at the end of its M_B edge. If T pairs y1 with y2, the component is k1−y1−y2−k2. Otherwise each conflict gives its own three-vertex path, or a path with its T segment already compressed. Compress all these paths, removing Y from the local vertex set, into single edges. The resulting edge family L is a matching of K(B), with both yj as holes. Any original M_B edge in such a path is recorded for expansion. If a compressed edge carries the tag, its expansion preserves the tag.

T15 gives a single circle on B⧵Y containing L. Expand its recorded paths and then every original transferred segment. This restores Y once and all A vertices once, retaining every original edge. The result is a single 64-vertex circle with the tagged uv edge. Deleting that edge gives the required Hamilton u--v path. Every surviving new edge is short.

This proof covers terminal and nonterminal bridge mirrors at once. No application of a local endpoint theorem at a covered mirror is concealed in it.

3. The (2,1) row reduces to T15

Let Z∩A={z1,z2} and let w be the sole member of W∩A. For each j bridge zj to yj=z¯j. The mirrors are odd and distinct. They are not W holes by independence, cannot be the even root, and cannot be crossing ports because zj is free. Thus both are internally covered by MB.

If δ=1, set r=u and choose D to pair XA∪{z1,z2}. The original A holes are u,z1,z2,w, so the number c of crossing ports is even. The set paired by D has positive even size. The holes of MA∪D are exactly r,w.

If δ=0, set r=z1 and choose D to pair XA∪{z2}. Here the original A holes are z1,z2,w, so c is odd and positive; D is nonempty. Its completed matching again has exactly the opposite-parity holes r,w. This choice needs no even crossing port.

In either case N10 gives a Hamilton r--v path containing MA∪D. Delete D, attach all real crossedges, and attach both short bridges zjyj. For δ=0 the bridge at r=z1 attaches to the initial path endpoint; its degree becomes two, as required because it is not the global root. For δ=1 the global root retains degree one. All other degree and forest requirements of Section 2 follow from distinct B attachments.

For δ=1, the original B holes have counts (1,3). The matching T consumes all crossing ports and covers both internally matched yj. After conflict compression its holes are the original B holes together with Y, hence (1,5). For δ=0, the original B holes have counts (2,3) and include u. The tagged closure consumes u, while the two conflict compressions expose Y. Thus the new holes are (HB⧵{u})∪Y, again (1,5). T15 avoiding Y applies, and Section 2 completes the path.

4. The (2,0) row reduces to T15 under EP0

Suppose EP0 supplies r,q,D,P,s, and set t=s¯∈W⊂B. The odd crossing-port surplus is 2+δ, so such ports exist. For δ=1, c is odd and at least three, and D has size (c+1)/2. For δ=0, c is even and at least two, and D has size c/2. In both cases D is nonempty, avoids r,q, and MA∪D has holes r,q.

Delete D and the short new edge qs from P. Attach all real crossing edges; attach both bridges zjyj as in Section 3; and attach the short bridge st. The vertex s is outside XA∪{z1,z2}, so this extra deletion does not interact with D or a preexisting bridge at s.

If q≠v, it loses one of its two new path edges and gains its real crossing edge, so its degree remains two. If q=v, deletion isolates the path endpoint, and its real crossing edge gives it degree one. If s≠u, it is internally covered by MA, loses one new edge, and gains st, so it retains degree two. If s=u (only possible for δ=1), it loses its unique path edge and gains ut, retaining degree one. These include all endpoint boundaries.

The new B endpoint t is an original odd hole, distinct from XB and from Y. It is distinct from Y because a coincidence would give an edge between a nonroot even hole and a member of W. Attachments therefore remain distinct, and Section 2's tagged closure and conflict compression apply.

For δ=1, original B hole counts are (1,4). The transfer consumes the odd hole t and the conflicts expose Y: the final hole set is (HB⧵{t})∪Y, with counts (1,5). For δ=0, original B hole counts are (2,4); the closure also consumes u. The final hole set is (HB⧵{u,t})∪Y, again (1,5). T15 avoids precisely Y, and expansion completes the required global path.

5. What finite probes establish, and what they do not

The independent geometry work in COVERED_EIGHT_GEOMETRY_CENSUS.md reports that each residual has a (2,0) or (2,1) cut. That complete geometric classification is an external input to any future global use of this draft; this file does not recertify it. In particular there are 50 normalized geometries, represented by seven target-preserving permutation orbits, whose splitting cuts are all (2,0).

The diagnostic script eight_hole_covered_next_probe.py constructs actual short matchings on the covered vertices of the following seven representatives. For each of their three (2,0) cuts separately, it finds a 28-edge matching such that

E(Q5)∩((XA∩O)×S)=∅.

Every such output is verified directly as a matching with the exact eight holes. There are 21 such positive witnesses, fully recorded in the JSON. Consequently EP0 fails for arbitrary fixed cuts; it cannot be universally asserted in that form.

There is a useful weaker selection fact across cuts. In each representative, simultaneously delete every short edge that would create an eligible q--s adjacency in any of its three cuts. The resulting graph of covered vertices has the isolated even vertices listed in the last column. Each such vertex is covered in any realizing matching, so a realizing matching must contain a deleted edge. That edge gives an eligible adjacency at at least one of the three cuts.

v Z W (2,0) coordinates isolated even vertices after all deletions
1 3,5,9 14,31,47,62 1,2,3 15,30,46,63
7 3,5,6 8,16,32,56 0,1,2 24,40,48
7 3,5,15 8,25,41,56 1,2,3 9,24,40,57
7 3,15,23 25,26,56,59 2,3,4 24,27,57,58
7 15,23,39 56,59,61,62 3,4,5 57,58,60,63
31 15,23,27 1,2,32,35 2,3,4 3,33,34
31 15,23,63 32,35,37,38 3,4,5 33,34,36,39

Coordinates are numbered from zero. The script explicitly verifies the full neighbor set of each listed Hall subset is empty in the deletion graph. This proves the adjacency fact for all realizing matchings of each listed geometry, and cube symmetries give it for their images. It is not a sample-based Hamilton assertion. It still does not prove that the N10 path can contain that eligible edge. That optional-edge prescription is the present barrier.

The parent agent separately verified all 21 positive matching witnesses and all seven Hall certificates using the solver-free checker verify_eight_exposure_obstructions.py; its result is recorded in eight_exposure_obstructions_verification.json. This independent finite check does not constitute semantic acceptance of the transfer draft or of either core.

The Q4 analogue of T15 must not be imported without qualification: prior diagnostic files q4_six_hole_two_avoided.cpp and q4_six_two_avoided_results.json report actual negative instances for some pairs of prescribed avoided majority holes. The Q5 statement T15 remains a separate conjectural core in this document.

6. Remaining exact research obligations

T15 is a standalone unproved complete-graph-matching extension theorem. EP0 is a genuine extra path-edge condition. A global route through these reductions requires a proved choice of cut satisfying (2,1) or satisfying (2,0) together with EP0; mere availability of a (2,0) cut is insufficient. The seven-orbit exceptional incidence check supplies an eligible edge in some cut, but not EP0.

No conclusion here closes R8-covered. Closing T15 alone would nevertheless close all (2,1)-cut inputs, regardless of the other cut rows, via the full quantified transfer in Section 3. Independent proof-checker review of this draft is still needed.

Rank reduction when an included hole forces a cherry

2026-11-01. A structural lemma for future marked multiple-omission inputs; not an accepted new P6 branch.

Suppose an included free vertex h has exactly two available short neighbors p,q after the specified omissions. Every short-complement forest must contain ph,hq, hence its endpoint matching contains pq. In the actual application p,q are covered vertices; this assumption must be checked, not inferred from the degree count alone.

If the required matching F contains pq, the three edges ph,hq,pq form an isolated triangle in every cycle extension: all three vertices already have degree two. If other retained vertices exist, the desired spanning cycle is impossible. This is an explicit obstruction.

If pq∉F, put a=F(p) and b=F(q). The four endpoints are distinct. Replace the two required edges pa,qb by ab, giving a perfect matching F′ on K⧵{p,q}. For each admissible forest with endpoint matching P, remove pq to obtain P′ on that same set. Then F+P is one alternating cycle if and only if F′+P′ is one alternating cycle: the path a−p−q−b is suppressed or expanded.

Thus full rank 2(|K|−2)/2−1 for these shortened endpoint pairings is a sufficient certificate for every required matching avoiding pq. It need not be possible to attain the larger rank for the original |K| endpoints. A reduced-rank certificate plus the forced triangle would yield an exact local classification.

For Q5 one-versus-seven holes with three majority holes omitted, a minority free hole whose three neighbors are precisely the omissions has this form if the other two neighbors are covered. In a Q6 transfer, the original internal matching is short and cannot contain the same-parity edge pq. The compressed matching may contain it, however; one must still prove that the completion and transfer can avoid creating it. A rank certificate alone does not discharge that transfer obligation.

Fourteen-hole residual: cached-positive candidate reuse and exact greedy subset

2026-11-02. Producer-only computational/proof preparation by /root/higher_forced_cherry_review. No new local input or actual application is independently accepted by this document. The old source/registry files and the frozen FOURTEEN_REUSE package remain unchanged. This is not full fourteen holes; the source reduction still depends on complete twelve-hole Q6, which is not asserted here.

Exact source and candidate result

The six frozen FOURTEEN_REUSE_remaining_h14_v{1,7,31}_{covered,free}.bin files contain48211 original-label13-byte records (Z6 followed by W7), with free root0 and the named odd target. Their first-stage producer source gate is FOURTEEN_REUSE_MANIFEST.json; that application's fresh independent acceptance is a separate pending gate. No matching-realizability exclusion is used.

Actual source/cut predicate

For every original record, try all six target-facing cuts and every legal source subset of the actual type. With k=7, even consumption has s=a+1-b, minority6-a and majority7-b+s, with sources among A Z holes and b>=1. Odd consumption has s=b-a-1, minority7-b and majority6-a+s, with sources among A W holes excluding root mirror and a free target. The code explicitly checks source counts/pool and rejects any mirror which is an original hole/root.

Delete only the outer coordinate, then transform actual minority, majority and marked mirror omissions together. A minority anchor is used when present, otherwise an omission anchor. For each cached canonical row every corresponding source anchor and every coordinate permutation is included. A hit is tied to a named exact cache row/prefix, not just to a type or unmarked hole count.

The scan examines1434085 legal source projections in about0.934 seconds. It retains one witness per source record/candidate orbit rather than stopping at the first orbit. Exactly278524 such distinct hits occur, across161 of the403 candidate rows. Thus the complete candidate union is defined by source-index sets, not by adding overlapping orbit counts.

Each per-status FOURTEEN_CACHED_all_hits_h14_v{v}_{status}.bin record has28 little-endian bytes: original13-byte-source index uint32; family uint8 (30=NEW cache,31=EXTRA cache); cut uint8; exact local ID uint16; original-label source mask uint64; actual projected minority, majority and omission masks (three uint32). The target and free/covered status come from the filename.

Greedy sufficient registry: only twenty new local obligations

Greedy selection repeatedly chooses the candidate row with largest uncovered source-record gain, breaking ties by its numerical code (NEW index, EXTRA1000+index). This is a convenient deterministic selection, not a minimum-cardinality theorem. The selected twenty rows have exactly the same source-record union as all403 candidates. A chosen selected witness is stored per covered source record; all other source records are copied unchanged in original order to the six FOURTEEN_CACHED_remaining_h14_v{v}_{status}.bin files. Monotone lift, including the actual target-cross cases

Let 31h be the original target matching edge. If it is internal A, remove it and insert the auxiliary edge wh internally in A. If it crosses, then h=63; replace it by the auxiliary crossing edge w63. Let X′ be this domain's vertices unmatched by L′. Their incident original or virtual cross edges are retained as ports.

The submatching inclusion L′⊆L*′ holds in all three cases:

Writing δ=1 when u∈A, completion parity and sizes give

Any cycle in the ACTUAL compressed matching L plus R would lie wholly in the common parity class of the obstruction endpoints. Original internal short edges and suppressed mirror-mate edges leave that class; an edge to the root cannot be in the cycle because the root is excluded. Every edge of that cycle belonging to L must therefore be a direct transfer pair between two original ports. Lift its transferred paths to A and replace its JB edges by their prescribed JA pairs. This would make a cycle in the tagged A cycle with D⧵JA deleted when the root is in A, or in a subgraph of the original A path when the root is in B. The former is a forest because d>j; the latter is a forest as a subgraph of a path. The lifted paths have disjoint interiors, so a cycle, not merely a repeated-vertex closed walk, would result. With root in B, attachments are distinct B leaves, including its tag leaf. The covered target-port boundary is allowed: deletion can isolate target v in A, but crossing and tag restore degree two. A free target cannot lie in D.

Each y in Y is originally internally B-covered: its free A mirror excludes crossing coverage, nonroot independence excludes another original hole, and legal sources exclude the root. Its distinct original short mate has parity opposite Y, outside Y/ports/free root. Only those pendant conflicts occur, so simultaneous suppression cannot make a conflict cycle. The actual L is a perfect matching on B minus H_, H_=(H intersect B minus root) union Y. This proves the marked counts and sets used by the scanner. Applying an accepted universal local cycle on exactly B minus Y, expanding all paths and deleting the tag gives the specified Hamilton path, preserving every original edge and only short new physical edges.

The argument is the accepted general source transfer with the already accepted full balanced Q5 input. It does not import an unproved thirteen/fourteen-hole endpoint theorem or full twelve-hole closure into the local construction. The latter is a separate conditional predecessor gate only for reducing arbitrary original fourteen-hole geometries to this source domain.

Forced-classification hypothesis discharge

Each forced registry row supplies a single actual pair pq of covered B vertices with parity Y, and local cycle existence iff that pair is absent from arbitrary L. Its source count is3 or4, within the accepted generic forced-cherry theorem's s>=3 scope. The scanner transports pq with the same automorphism as the marked sets and rejects root-in-obstruction witnesses. Root0 is in B exactly when the target's cut bit is1; its projection then is0, so the actual forced mask must omit bit0 in that case.

Consequently the generic root-not-OB theorem applies to every actual original matching: an unchanged internal pair cannot produce the same-parity obstruction; suppressed source mates have the opposite parity; if both obstruction endpoints are ports, prescribe their actual A crossing-partner pair inside D and keep the automatic spare deletion gap. This excludes pq from the actual compressed L, not just original M_B. The unknown target mate is never chosen favorably. Root-in-pair records are not accepted through this forced route even if a different proof might solve them.

The new root-mirror-omitted author transfer and A mixed-opening ideas are not used. STAR_B10 is used solely as its accepted local forced classification and combined with the already accepted generic root-not-OB transfer in this different14-hole application.

Computation, selected witnesses and producer sanity

Reproduction:

python FOURTEEN_REUSE_prepare.py
g++ -std=c++17 -O3 FOURTEEN_REUSE_scan.cpp -o FOURTEEN_REUSE_scan.exe
./FOURTEEN_REUSE_scan.exe full
g++ -std=c++17 -O3 FOURTEEN_REUSE_sanity.cpp -o FOURTEEN_REUSE_sanity.exe
./FOURTEEN_REUSE_sanity.exe

A separately named benchmark processed494182 source records in about2.7 seconds, forecasting aboutone minute. The full scan took 53.8711 seconds for9484443 records and evaluated55607272 actual legal source projections before first sufficient hits or exhaustion. It tries all six target-facing cuts and every legal source subset whose exact shape can enter the accepted registry. On success it keeps the first valid witness; rejected records exhaust all eligible choices. No claim about optimal witness tie-breaking or all per-orbit hit sets is made.

Each FOURTEEN_REUSE_witness_h14_v{v}_{status}.bin record is32 bytes, little-endian:

Field Bytes

outer coordinate cut 1
family code 1
exact local ID (zero for legacy membership predicates) 2

actual projected minority mask 4
actual projected majority mask 4

The target/status come from the filename. Source indices refer to the original thirteen-byte input, not a filtered array. Selected witnesses occupy about288 MiB. The six new thirteen-byte residual files occupy about0.60 MiB total and retain exact original labels and source order.

The producer replay independently reads all witnesses and source records again, checks indices/order/alignment, reconstructs source legality and actual marked masks, replays exact family membership and forced-root exclusion, and compares every missing source record to the next residual record byte-for-byte. All9436232 positive witnesses and48211 residual records pass. This uses shared producer predicate helpers and is explicitly producer sanity, not independent application acceptance. A fresh reviewer should rebuild the relevant registries/source predicates independently and verify all positive witnesses plus exact complement/no-hit conditions on the small48211 residual domain.

FOURTEEN_REUSE_MANIFEST.json binds all input review gates, source bytes, accepted lookup versions, producer code/catalog/registry, report, selected witnesses, raw residuals and sanity result. Only new FOURTEEN_REUSE-prefixed files were written. This package does not modify any predecessor state or claim a full layer has closed.

HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_TRANSFER.md — Uniform transfer through one or several forced cherries

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：a5030f66772259eeb32402c25f92a77761acb454e70696b2d370c652037fbea4。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：FOURTEEN_FINAL25_REVIEW.json, FOURTEEN_FORCED_REVIEW.json, FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json, HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_REVIEW.json, HIGHER_Q5_FULL_T37_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json, SIXTEEN_LOCAL_REVIEW.json, SIXTEEN_SMALLCUT_REVIEW.json, SIXTEEN_STAR_REVIEW.json, TWELVE_EXTRA_FORCED_REVIEW.json, TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json, TWELVE_NEW_FORCED_HALL_REVIEW.json, TWELVE_STAR_B_REVIEW.json。

Uniform transfer through one or several forced cherries

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer candidate. Status: PROVABLE AS STATED relative to the explicit local inputs below; fresh independent review is required. This is a sufficient-route theorem, not a closure of any higher hole layer or unrestricted local geometry.

Claim and assumptions

Let M be any short matching in Q6 with holes H={u}∪Z∪W, where u is even and free, |Z|=k−1, |W|=k, Z is even, W is odd, and Z∪W is independent. Let v be any odd target, covered or free. Choose a coordinate cut A,B with v∈A; put a=|Z∩A|, b=|W∩A|, δ=1[u∈A]. Let C be the original crossing matching, c=|C|, and XA,XB its port sets.

Consider either of the following branches with s≥3:

  • Even consumption: b≥1, s=a+1−b, and choose any S⊂Z∩A of size s.
  • Odd consumption: s=b−a−1, and choose S⊂(W∩A)⧵{v,u¯} of size s. The exclusion of v matters only when v is free, and that of u¯ only when u∈B. Existence of this precise S is a hypothesis.

Here x¯ means the mirror across the cut and Y={x¯:x∈S}. The intended B matching has hole set H*=(H∩B)⧵{u} ∪Y and covered set K=B⧵H*. In even consumption its hole counts (global even,odd) are (k−a−1,k−b+s); in odd consumption they are (k−a−1+s,k−b). It must admit a local cycle on precisely B⧵Y.

Single-cherry hypothesis. Suppose p,q∈K are distinct, have the same global parity as Y, and u∉{p,q}. Suppose the actual marked B geometry has the local classification: for every arbitrary perfect matching F on K, it has a cycle on B⧵Y containing F, with only short new edges, if and only if pq∉F. Then M has a Hamilton u--v extension with only short new edges.

This statement holds for every feasible k, in particular k=6,7,8,9 (twelve through eighteen holes); it does not supply the assumed marked local classification or the existence of a useful cut.

The multi-cherry version and a precise rank criterion supplying its local classification are proved in Sections5--6. All graph unions retain edge labels: a common matching pair is a two-edge cycle, not a single edge.

Imports and strategy

Import the accepted balanced-hole Q5 endpoint theorem for arbitrary complete-graph matching edges and every feasible balanced hole count: any free root and opposite-parity covered or free target have a Hamilton path through that matching, with only short new edges. The full A10 assembly and Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json accept the consequences of Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION.md, together with full A8 and the named earlier inputs. Thus the old uniform transfer's small balanced-hole range need not restrict a,b here. Global parity is restricted to a face; choosing face coordinates may reverse both parity names, which the import allows.

Import the established five-direction free-root endpoint theorem for c=0, exactly as in HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER.md. For c>0 we prove the forest construction directly. Its degree accounting, tag and simultaneous suppression agree with that accepted uniform transfer. The single-cherry avoidance extends the accepted Q5_T17_RANK_ROOT_NOT_OB_TRANSFER.md; that frozen text is not modified.

Dependency map: all-balanced Q5 endpoints -> A Hamilton path -> controlled deletion forest -> actual compressed B matching avoids the local obstruction -> assumed B classification -> expansion. In Section5 the optional local input is obtained from independently verified forest ranks and the generic complete-graph matching-connectivity rank upper bound. No Q6 higher layer is an input to this proof.

1. Legal completions and uniform gap lower bounds

If c=0, invoke the explicit five-direction import and finish. Assume c>0. Shortness of the internal matching MA gives

|XA∩E|−|XA∩O|=b−a−δ,c≡a+b+δ(mod2).

Choose root r and the set VD to be paired as follows:

Branch Root face r VD A holes after completion
even δ=1 u XA∪S (b,b)
even δ=0 any member of S XA∪(S⧵{r}) (b,b)
odd δ=1 u XA∪S (a+1,a+1)
odd δ=0 any even port (XA⧵{r})∪S (a+1,a+1)

For the last row the even-port surplus is b−a=s+1, so such a port exists and c≥s+1. Every VD has even cardinality by the congruence above. Its vertices are free for MA, distinct from r, and do not include a free target v by the source exclusions. A covered target can belong to VD only when it is a crossing port.

Let D be any perfect pairing of VD for now, and write d=|D|. When δ=1, d=(c+s)/2≥2 since c≥1, s≥3. When δ=0, d=(c+s−1)/2. In even consumption c+s−1≥3 and is even, hence d≥2. In odd consumption c≥s+1 gives d≥s≥3.

The A matching MA+D has exactly the balanced hole counts in the table, with r free and even and v an odd legal target. Apply the all-balanced endpoint import to obtain a simple Hamilton r--v path PA containing every edge of MA+D. Artificial D edges may be long or same-parity; all other new local edges are short.

2. Actual transfer and suppression

Each y∈Y is originally internally matched in B. Indeed its source mirror is originally free, so it cannot be a crossing port; independence of Z∪W excludes any original nonroot hole at y; and y≠u by parity in even consumption and the explicit root-mirror exclusion in odd consumption. Put hy=MB(y). These mates are distinct and have parity opposite to Y. Being internally covered, they are not ports or the root; their parity also puts them outside Y.

Delete D from PA, attach every original crossing and all short bridges xx¯ for x∈S, and add tagged edge uv. If u∈A, one can equivalently first add uv to PA, obtaining one simple32-cycle, then delete D. Its endpoint edge was not already on PA. Since d≥2, at least one cycle edge was removed and the result is a forest. If u∈B, start with a path forest; all attachments, including the previously free root at v, are distinct B leaves and create no cycle.

Degree accounting leaves all A vertices with degree two: the missing degree at r is supplied by its source bridge or crossing when r≠u; the tag supplies the true endpoint degree at v and at u when u∈A. Each deleted D endpoint receives one attachment. If a covered target is a port and loses its only A path edge, its crossing and tag restore degree two. A free target is not in D and keeps its A path edge plus the tag. Thus compression gives a perfect matching T on XB∪Y∪({u}∩B), with exactly one tag-carrying path.

The only degree conflicts in T+MB are at Y, with the distinct pendant mates hy described above. A conflict component contains one T edge and at most one pendant original edge at each endpoint. It cannot be a cycle. Suppress Y in every such component and carry along the actual paths and tag. The result is a perfect matching L on K, with hole set exactly H*, including Y as omitted holes. It may have arbitrary long or same-parity edges; its precise edges, not just MB, must satisfy the B input.

3. One cherry: preventing the actual compressed pair

Both p,q are originally covered: they are outside H* and Y, and the only original hole removed from H∩B was u, which is excluded. They have Y's parity. Consequently pq∉MB by shortness.

If an obstruction endpoint is not a port, it is not a T endpoint either: it is outside Y and the root. Its original internal matching edge stays unchanged. Its opposite-parity mate is not in Y, cannot be a port or free root, and is not the other obstruction endpoint. If a T edge ends in Y, suppression moves that end to hy of opposite parity, and a Y--Y edge becomes an edge between two such mates. An edge to u remains incident with that distinct root. These cases prove

pq∈L ⟹ p,q∈XB and pq∈T.

If either vertex is not a port, any legal D therefore works. Otherwise let p′,q′ be their actual original A crossing partners and prescribe p′q′∈D. This is legal: in even consumption r is the originally free root or a source hole, never a port. In odd consumption with δ=0, the B obstruction endpoints are even, their crossing partners are odd, and r was chosen even. For δ=1, r=u is originally free. The prescribed endpoints are distinct from all source holes, so the remaining even number of vertices in VD can be paired arbitrarily.

For δ=1, the tagged A cycle loses p′q′ and at least one other D edge. Its direct p′--q′ arc and its complementary arc are both cut. Hence p′,q′ lie in different remaining A components. B leaf attachments cannot merge those components, so p,q are not one T pair. For δ=0, deleting p′q′ from a simple A path already separates its endpoints. Further deletions and distinct B leaf attachments cannot reconnect them. Thus again pq∉T, and hence pq∉L.

The covered target-port boundary is included: if v is incident with the prescribed D edge, deletion may isolate v in the A path. For δ=1 the retained tag is part of the tagged-cycle proof. For δ=0 the segment is u−v−v¯, which cannot have endpoints p,q because the root is excluded. For a free target this degeneracy cannot occur because v∉VD.

Apply the assumed B classification to the actual L. Expand its cycle through the suppressed mirrors Y and transferred A paths. These paths are disjoint except for their prescribed cycle endpoints; no physical edge is reused. Expansion gives a tagged spanning64-cycle containing all original M edges. Delete the tag. All D edges had been deleted, all compressed edges were expanded, and every remaining new edge is a local cube edge or selected short bridge. This proves the single-cherry theorem.

4. Source existence for free targets

In even consumption b≥1 implies s=a+1−b≤a; sources exist and cannot be the odd target. In odd consumption the exact existence condition is

b−|(W∩A)∩{v,u¯}|≥s=b−a−1.

For covered targets at most the root mirror is excluded, so this always holds. For free targets with a≥1 at most two holes are excluded and it also holds. With a free target and a=0, two distinct excluded holes can leave too few sources; Z∪W independence alone does not remove this possibility. No route is claimed without legal sources.

If the full original hole set H={u}∪Z∪W is independent, then u¯∉W, so at most v is excluded; the odd source set exists even when a=0. This is a useful free-target corollary under a declared stronger geometry hypothesis. It is not silently inferred from Z∪W independence, nor from an unproved predecessor hole layer.

5. Several cherries: exact local rank criterion

This section is a general local lemma on one Q5 face. Let H* be its holes, Y⊂H* its specified omissions, and K its 2n covered terminals. Assume n≥2. A legal short-complement forest has degree zero on Y, two on H*⧵Y, one on K, and consists of paths whose endpoints partition K. Write P for its endpoint perfect matching.

Let R be a fixed matching of r pairs on K, with 1≤r<n. Suppose every legal short-complement forest has endpoint pairing containing R. To prove the positive direction it suffices to supply a selected family of such forests whose reduced pairings P−=P⧵R, on K−=K⧵V(R), have rank 2n−r−1 against any supplied perfect-matching columns in the connectivity matrix on these 2(n−r) labels. The generic upper bound for that matrix is the only rank import.

Then, for every arbitrary perfect matching F on K,

a required local cycle exists⟺F+R has no labeled cycle.

Necessity. Any local cycle through F, after deleting F, gives one of the legal complement forests and hence a pairing containing R. A cycle in F+R is a full component of F+P, because all its vertices already have one F and one R edge. It misses the nonempty set K−, so F+P cannot be a single alternating cycle. This contradiction proves necessity; a common pair F∩R is included as a two-edge obstruction.

Sufficiency. If F+R has no cycle, it is a disjoint union of paths. Every vertex of V(R) has degree two and every other vertex of K has degree one, so its path endpoints are exactly K−. Suppressing all internal V(R) vertices produces an arbitrary perfect matching F− on K−. For any selected P=R∪P−, replacing those internally disjoint F/R paths by single edges preserves connectedness of the labeled unions:

F+P is one alternating cycle⟺F−+P− is one alternating cycle.

The verified reduced rank and upper bound make the selected rows span the full connectivity row space. The column of every F− is nonzero: cyclically join consecutive F-minus edges; for two residual terminals use the labeled double-edge cycle convention. Some selected row connects it. Undo the suppressions and expand the selected short forest to obtain the required local cycle. Since the original full terminal domain has at least four vertices, a shared physical F/forest edge would form a proper two-edge component and could not have passed connectedness.

For r=1, acyclicity of F+R is exactly absence of that one pair in F. For r≥2, absence of the individual R edges is insufficient. For example R={01,23} and F={12,30,45} have no common pair but contain the alternating cycle 0−1−2−3−0. The other endpoints ensure it is a proper component. The case r=n is deliberately excluded: there are no residual endpoints, F+R always has cycles, and the stated necessity argument would not exclude one Hamilton alternating component.

6. Multi-cherry transfer: the extra gap is automatic

Return to the global setup, with the same legal sources and s≥3. Let R be a matching of local covered B vertices, all of whose endpoints have the parity of Y, lie outside Y, and exclude u. Assume the actual marked B geometry has the local classification

cycle on B⧵Y through arbitrary F⟺F+R is acyclic.

Section5 is one sufficient way to establish this input; a fresh audited alternative proof is also allowed. Let

JB={pq∈R:p,q∈XB},j=|JB|,

and let JA be the matching of their actual crossing partners in A. These j edges are pairwise disjoint and are all legal completion pairs by the same parity/root argument as in Section3. Prescribe JA⊂D and pair the rest of VD arbitrarily.

Under precisely the stated hypotheses a Hamilton u--v extension exists. No additional bound on |R| and no matching-dependent extra-gap hypothesis are needed. Because R is a matching, every edge of JB consumes two distinct ports, and therefore

j≤⌊c/2⌋.

For δ=1, d=(c+s)/2>⌊c/2⌋; for δ=0, d=(c+s−1)/2>⌊c/2⌋. Both strict inequalities follow from s≥3. Thus d>j holds automatically in both root faces, and at least one D edge remains outside the prescribed set JA. The actual bound is on both-port obstruction pairs, not on the total number of cherries.

To prove the claim, every cycle in L+R would alternate L and R edges, and all its vertices would belong to V(R), which has Y's parity. Section3's suppression analysis now applies to each possible L edge within V(R): such an edge can only be an unchanged direct T pairing between two ports. Original internal edges and suppressed bridge-mate edges end outside this parity class. An edge to the root cannot belong to the cycle because u∉V(R). Thus the putative cycle lies in T+JB.

Lift every T edge of that cycle to its actual transferred A path and the crossing attachments at its port endpoints. Replace every J-B edge by its prescribed A pair in JA, deleting the now-superfluous B port leaves and crossings along this cycle. This gives a cycle in the graph obtained from the tagged A graph by deleting D and restoring JA. The lifted paths are internally disjoint, so this operation does not create a merely closed walk with repeated interior vertices.

If δ=1, write Q=PA+uv, a simple cycle. The graph in question is

Q−(D⧵JA).

Since d>j, it is a proper edge-deleted subgraph of a simple cycle, and therefore a forest. If δ=0, ignore the tag's root leaf, which cannot participate in the putative cycle. The graph in question is

PA−(D⧵JA),

a subgraph of a simple path, hence a forest even when D=JA. Both conclusions contradict the lifted cycle. Consequently L+R is acyclic and the assumed local classification and tagged expansion finish. The argument includes a covered target port isolated after deleting D; the tag either belongs to Q or has the excluded root as a leaf.

The extra-gap distinction is real for the abstract graph argument. If δ=1 and D=JA, restoring all prescribed pairs restores the entire tagged A cycle. Upon path compression this can produce a full alternating T+JB cycle even though no individual R pair is a T edge. This is a failure of this prescription argument, not a counterexample to the global endpoint theorem. The port count excludes this event under the present hypotheses. Outside those hypotheses no claim is made that a different D or cut cannot work. In the δ=0 path case restoration of all D edges would still be acyclic, providing a stronger abstract fact than the uniform extra-gap bound used here.

Boundaries and outstanding work

The new results are complete conditional proofs, submitted for fresh review. Higher marked local rank certificates, actual useful cut/source coverage, and whole twelve-to-eighteen-hole closure are not provided. Root-in-obstruction cases, mixed-parity obstruction endpoints, and transfers outside the declared source/consumption hypotheses are not covered. In particular, general tagged-cycle prescriptions without any unprescribed gap are not justified by this argument; the present port bound guarantees that gap. Source shortage for a free target under only nonroot independence must be handled by another route or an explicit stronger hypothesis. No unconditional predecessor induction is introduced. The proposed single-cherry result specializes to the accepted ten-hole two-row lemma, and the multi-cherry result strictly tracks cycles of the whole F+R union, not just membership of individual pairs.

Author sanity evidence, not independent acceptance

HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_author_check.py exhausts all perfect F matchings on four, six, eight and ten terminals for every nonempty fixed partial R with at least two residual terminals. It compares119238 full/reduced connectivity instances and checks both directions of the contraction criterion. It also checks8640 integer port/gap parameter cases and the two explicit alternating-cycle boundary examples above. All pass. These finite checks support the argument but do not prove its universal quantifiers or replace the requested fresh proof review.

A uniform cut transfer for the remaining P6 layers

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Proposed proof relative to explicit imports; independent review pending. Full P6 and the 10--18-hole layers remain open.

Claim, assumptions, and notation

Let M be a short matching in Q6 with 2k holes, let u be a free even root, and let v be any odd target, covered or free. Write the holes as {u}∪Z∪W, where |Z|=k−1, |W|=k, all members of Z are even and all members of W are odd. Assume Z∪W is independent. This assumption is a legitimate induction reduction only after the (2k−2)-hole theorem is available; it is not currently a proof of that predecessor theorem for k≥6.

Choose a coordinate cut A,B with v∈A. Put a=|Z∩A|, b=|W∩A|, and δ=1 if u∈A, otherwise 0. Let C be the original crossing matching, c=|C|, XA,XB its port sets, and MA,MB the internal matching restrictions. The mirror of a vertex across this coordinate is denoted by x¯.

Import the established five-direction free-root endpoint theorem for c=0. For c>0, import the full Q5 local endpoint lemma for arbitrary complete- graph matchings with balanced 2,4,6 holes: any free even root and any odd target have a spanning path containing the matching with only short new edges. Import full-cycle extensions for balanced 0,2,4,6 holes; omit-one extensions for hole counts (j,j+2), j=0,1,2, at every specified majority hole; and T44_5 for four same-parity holes, omitting any specified two. These are the accepted A6/N14/A4, perfect-matching, and T44_5 consequences in EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_DRAFT.md Section 1 and the final reviews cited by EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_CLOSURE.md. No higher-hole P6 theorem is imported.

The following transfer is conditional on the exact B-side cycle theorem specified below. In the corollary table all its local inputs are already proved, so those cut classes are unconditional relative to the imports.

1. Excess even holes in A

Suppose 1≤b≤3 and s=a+1−b≥0. Choose any s members S of Z∩A; this is possible because b≥1. The desired B-side input is the cycle-extension theorem for hole counts

(k−a−1, k−b+s),

omitting exactly the s odd holes Y={x¯:x∈S}. This input must hold for the actual marked hole geometry and every arbitrary complete-graph matching on its complement.

If δ=1, pair XA∪S arbitrarily into a matching D and take r=u. The holes of MA+D are (b,b) and include r. Indeed c+s is even, since c≡a+1+b(mod2).

If δ=0 and s≥1, choose r∈S and pair XA∪(S⧵{r}) into D. Its cardinality is even since c≡a+b(mod2). The holes are again (b,b) and include r. There is no requirement for an even crossing port in this case.

If δ=0 and s=0, then b=a+1. Shortness of MA gives |XA∩E|−|XA∩O|=b−a=1. Choose an even port r and pair XA⧵{r} into D. The completed holes are (b,b).

Use the imported endpoint theorem for a spanning r--v path in A. Delete D, attach every original crossing edge, and attach the short bridges xx¯ for all x∈S. If r∈S, its bridge makes it an interior vertex; if r∈XA, its original crossing edge does so. If r=u, it remains the true global endpoint. The other endpoint is v. This remains true when v is a crossing port or a free vertex.

Every y∈Y is internally covered by MB: independence excludes an original odd hole at y, its even mirror x is free so it is not a crossing port, and y≠u by parity. The bridges are mutually distinct.

2. Excess odd holes in A

Suppose 0≤a≤2 and t=b−a−1≥1. Choose a set S⊂W∩A of size t that excludes v (if free) and excludes the vertex u¯ (if it lies in A). This existence is an explicit hypothesis of this branch. It always holds for covered targets, since b−t=a+1≥1; it also always holds for free targets when a≥1, since at most two vertices are excluded.

The required B-side cycle input has hole counts

(k−a−1+t, k−b),

and omits exactly the t even holes Y={x¯:x∈S}.

For δ=1, take r=u and pair XA∪S into D. For δ=0, the port difference is b−a=t+1>0, so choose an even port r and pair (XA⧵{r})∪S into D. The parity identities above show these sets have even size. The holes of MA+D are (a+1,a+1); r is free, and v remains a legal odd target. Apply the local endpoint theorem, delete D, and attach crossings and all bridges at S as in Section 1.

Each y∈Y is internally covered by MB: independence excludes Z, the choice of S excludes u, and a free mirror excludes crossing ports. All bridge conflicts now have even parity.

3. Tagged closure and simultaneous conflict compression

In both branches all A vertices have their intended final degrees. Deleting D from one A path leaves a path forest; all attachments are at distinct B vertices. If u∈A, D is nonempty (c>0, and the pairing set has positive even size), so the two true endpoint segments are distinct. If u∈B, it has not been attached. Add a tagged artificial edge uv. For u∈A this joins the two different terminal segments; for u∈B it extends the single terminal segment to u. The result remains a forest. Compress all A-interior paths into a matching T on distinct B endpoints. Exactly one edge of T carries the tag.

The only degree conflicts in T∪MB occur at Y. Each y∈Y has a distinct original mate hy of the opposite parity. Every hy is outside the endpoints of T: it is internally covered, is not a crossing port or the free root, and cannot be in the same-parity set Y. Thus the conflict components are paths, each with an original pendant endpoint hy; they cannot be cycles. Suppress every y∈Y in these components, recording the paths and any tag, to obtain an arbitrary matching L on B.

The endpoints of T are exactly XB∪Y and additionally u when u∈B. Consequently the holes of L are precisely

(HB⧵{u})∪Y,

where u is removed only when it belongs to B. These give the counts in Sections 1--2. Applying the specified B theorem produces a single cycle on B⧵Y containing L. Expand each suppressed conflict path, then each transferred A path. The result is one spanning cycle on Q6 containing the tag and every original matching edge. Delete the tagged uv edge to obtain the required Hamilton u--v path. All remaining new edges are short: artificial completion edges were deleted, and all compressed edges were expanded. This proves the conditional transfer.

4. Already available cut classes for ten and twelve holes

The following rows work for both free and covered odd targets. All odd-consumption rows have a≥1, so their selection condition holds. The zero-crossing case is handled by the five-direction import.

total holes (a,b) A balanced holes B hole counts; omitted holes input
10 (1,2) (2,2) (3,3); none balanced six-hole cycle
10 (2,3) (3,3) (2,2); none balanced four-hole cycle
10 (2,2) (2,2) (2,4); one odd A6
10 (3,3) (3,3) (1,3); one odd A4
10 (1,3) (2,2) (4,2); one even A6 reversed
10 (2,4) (3,3) (3,1); one even A4 reversed
10 (4,3) (3,3) (0,4); two odd T44_5
10 (2,5) (3,3) (4,0); two even T44_5 reversed
12 (2,3) (3,3) (3,3); none balanced six-hole cycle
12 (3,3) (3,3) (2,4); one odd A6
12 (2,4) (3,3) (4,2); one even A6 reversed

The marked T15 cases provide further conditional geometric entries: ten holes (3,2) or (1,4), and twelve holes (4,3) or (2,5). Their A hole counts are respectively (2,2) or (3,3) and the B counts are (1,5) or (5,1), omitting two majority holes. Only the already audited marked T15 geometries may be used; unrestricted T15 is not proved.

5. Remaining obligations and scope

No assertion is made that every ten- or twelve-hole geometry has a row in this table. A complete census must account for all free/covered targets, and any further T15 use must track the actual marked omissions. For 14--18 holes this particular table supplies no complete route. The original full P6 objective is unchanged, and the proven eight-hole package is not edited.

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：FOURTEEN_HALL_REVIEW.json, FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json, HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REVIEW.json, TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json。

Full Q5 local inputs: near-balanced cuts for the 12--18-hole layers

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer producer package. The row proof is relative to accepted local imports; the new exact census is producer evidence pending independent review. Full 12--18-hole Q6 and full P6 remain OPEN.

Exact row theorem

Let M be a short matching of Q6 with 2k holes, 6<=k<=9. Fix a free root u and any opposite-parity target v, free or covered. Normalize u=0 even, write its other even holes as Z (size k-1) and odd holes as W (size k), and assume Z union W is independent. Choose a coordinate face A containing v, let B be the other face, and put a=|Z intersect A|, b=|W intersect A|.

The following cut rows suffice for a Hamilton u--v path through M with all new edges short, relative to the stated accepted local inputs:

  1. b=a with b>=1;
  2. b=a+1;
  3. b=a+2, provided an odd source in W intersect A exists that is neither the free target v nor the mirror of u across the cut.

For a covered target row3 always has a source because b>=2 and only the root mirror can be excluded. For a free target it always has a source if the entire hole set {u} union Z union W is independent; the root mirror then is not a hole and only v must be excluded. Without that stronger independence assumption one must check the source condition explicitly: a=0,b=2 can have two different forbidden sources and is not automatic. The row a=b=0 is deliberately excluded: its even bridge source does not exist. No matching feasibility assumption or sampled matching is used.

Accepted imports and their ranges

Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW accepts every arbitrary K(Q5) matching with balanced m:m holes, m=1,...,16, from any free root to any opposite-parity target, covered or free, with only short new edges. It accepts full cycles for m=0,...,16. It also accepts every feasible imbalance-two avoid-one input with holes (t-1,t+1), t=1,...,15, for every marked majority hole and both parity orientations. Required local matching edges may be long or join equal parities. All these ranges are part of the reviewed consequence statement, not an extrapolation from small cases.

Use the accepted uniform-transfer construction and its explicit five-direction free-root endpoint input for zero original crossings. Its old numerical restrictions b<=3 or a<=2 served the former limited A endpoint imports. The construction is replayed below with the new full balanced-hole theorem. No complete higher-hole Q6 theorem is used to obtain these local Q5 inputs.

Completion, endpoint and hole-count proof

Let C be the actual original crossing matching, c=|C|, and X_A,X_B its distinct endpoint sets. If c=0, apply the accepted five-direction theorem. For c>0 write delta=1 if u belongs to A, and 0 otherwise.

In row1, select one even source z from Z intersect A; in row2 select no source. Equivalently s=a+1-b is one or zero. If delta=1, take r=u and pair X_A plus the s sources into a matching D. If delta=0 and s=1, let r be the source and pair X_A. If delta=0 and s=0, shortness of the original internal matching gives one more even than odd crossing port; choose an even port r and pair all other A ports. The endpoint pairing sets are even by 2|M_A|+c=32-|H_A|. The completed A matching M_A union D has exactly b holes of each parity, and r is free. In row1 b>=1, and in row2 b=a+1>=1, so the full local endpoint theorem applies. Its odd target v is legal whether covered or free; even consumption never consumes v.

After the accepted transfer and tagging, the B matching has hole counts (k-a-1,k-b+s). In row1 these are (k-a-1,k-a+1), and exactly the source mirror is omitted; it lies in the majority class. The full Q5 imbalance- two avoid-one theorem applies. In row2 both counts equal k-a-1; the full balanced-cycle theorem applies, including zero holes/perfect matching.

In row3 choose the one legal odd source w specified in the theorem. If delta=1 take r=u and pair X_A union {w}. If delta=0, shortness gives two more even than odd crossing ports; choose an even port r and pair (X_A minus {r}) union {w}. The completed A matching has a+1 holes of each parity, includes the free even r, and still permits target v. Use its full local endpoint theorem. The transferred B holes are (k-a,k-a-2), with the even source mirror as the sole prescribed majority omission. The reversed imbalance-two theorem applies. All declared B counts are nonnegative and feasible for an actually constructed matching. The A balanced parameter is at least one in every branch.

Forest, conflict and artificial-edge bookkeeping

Every selected source is originally free. Its mirror cannot be a crossing port, because a crossing edge at that B vertex would have to use its actual short mirror as partner in the original short M. Independence excludes its being an original hole of the opposite parity. Even-source mirrors have odd parity and cannot be u; the odd-source hypothesis excludes u explicitly. Thus every mirror is internally B-covered.

Apply the local A path, delete D, attach all original crossings and the one bridge if present. Distinct physical attachments preserve a path forest, including a temporarily isolated crossing target. The artificial tag uv joins the true endpoint segments when u is in A, or extends the v segment to the previously unattached u in B. For u in A the parity identities and c>0 make D nonempty; for u in B the D-empty boundary is already included in the accepted tagged construction. Compress A paths.

The only B conflict is the single internally covered bridge mirror y. Its original mate is outside every transferred endpoint: it is internally covered, not a crossing port or free root, and has opposite parity to y. It is a pendant endpoint in the conflict path, so no cycle is formed. Suppress y, retaining its path and any tag. The resulting B matching has the exact hole counts stated above, namely (H_B minus {u}) union {y} when a bridge is present, or H_B minus {u} otherwise. Its marked y is omitted by the B cycle theorem and restored once on expansion.

Expand every suppressed edge and transferred path and delete the unique tag. The global graph is one Hamilton u--v path preserving every original edge. All completion edges D were deleted, all compression edges expanded, and the tag removed; every surviving newly introduced physical edge is short. This proves the row theorem without the old local endpoint bounds.

Conditional predecessor reduction, especially free targets

Let P(k-1) be the COMPLETE preceding 2k-2-hole endpoint theorem for every short matching, every free root of either parity and every opposite- parity target, free or covered. The following reductions require P(k-1).

For a covered target, any short Z--W hole edge can be added without covering u or v, and P(k-1) applies. Thus the remaining reduced domain may assume Z union W independent; root--W adjacency is still allowed.

For a free target, suppose ANY two original holes x,y form a short edge. If xy differs from uv, adding xy leaves at least one of u,v free. Apply P(k-1) using that remaining free endpoint as root and the other as target, reversing the resulting path if needed. It contains M union {xy}; the extra xy edge is short relative to M. If xy=uv, add uv, choose a different remaining free root r (there are at least 2k-2 free holes), and any short neighbor s of r. P(k-1) gives a Hamilton r--s path containing the added uv. Its endpoints are opposite-parity, and r was free in the augmented matching. Add the short rs edge to obtain a Hamilton cycle; a path with 64 vertices cannot already contain an edge joining its two endpoints. Delete the added uv to obtain the required Hamilton u--v path through M. The artificial uv is not an original edge because both endpoints were originally free. No original required edge was deleted.

Consequently the free-target reduced domain may assume the ENTIRE hole set independent. In particular mirror(u) is never an odd source hole, so the source exception in row3 is automatically discharged there.

The complete preceding ten-hole theorem is now final PASS in TEN_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, fixed SHA-256 72c6f693b4f8bee6376edcbd132235d7985436f6ebbad8a19dade0d5326f643d. Thus these predecessor reductions are available unconditionally relative to accepted imports for the twelve-hole layer. For fourteen, sixteen and eighteen holes they remain CONDITIONAL on the corresponding preceding complete layer. Neither the census nor the row proof proves that missing predecessor. The cut theorem itself holds for its explicitly independent input geometries regardless of predecessor status.

Exact new producer census and raw remaining domains

HIGHER_Q5_FULL_census.cpp is a new source, leaving the old census frozen. It enumerates every nonzero even Z of size k-1 and every odd W of size k nonadjacent to Z, retaining root adjacency. For each normalized odd target v=1,7,31 it separates free/covered status. Coordinate permutations fixing root0 normalize all opposite-parity targets to these weights1,3,5. For free targets, any unit vertex in W is recorded as the conditional root-adjacent-to-predecessor branch BEFORE cut tests; all remaining free records have fully independent holes. Then all SIX actual target-oriented cuts are tested for b-a in {0,1,2}, excluding a=b=0. Only genuinely unhit records are written as raw original labels, with sorted Z followed by W.

The old k>=7 eligible-only shortcut is removed. Every k=6,...,9 runs the actual cut tests and writes all six residual files, including empty files. The program performs no matching-realizability exclusion. Each record has 2k-1 bytes. These are hole-geometry counts, not matching counts or automorphism-orbit counts. A hole geometry need not be realizable by a short original matching; no such restriction is used in this exhaustive over-domain.

All eligible counts agree exactly with the old independent-domain census, while the k>=7 cut filtering is new. All raw file lengths equal the stated residual count times 2k-1. These are producer consistency checks, not a substitute for an independent census/domain audit.

The eighteen-hole free residual being empty is a conditional statement about this reduced domain; it is NOT a full eighteen-hole theorem while the sixteen-hole predecessor is unproved. All four layers remain open.

Next shared inputs and limits

The frozen raw file naming is HIGHER_Q5_FULL_residual_h{12,14,16,18}_v{1,7,31}_{covered,free}.bin. Their SHA-256 pins, source, proof and accepted import/review hashes are recorded in the new manifest. Counts are only the initial near-balanced filter, before lookup of existing marked rank registries, accepted T63 split, T44 and other local inputs. They must not be described as the final number of difficult or unproved matching cases.

For example twelve-hole rows(2,1),(0,3) require marked Q5 T37 inputs: three minority plus seven majority holes, omitting two majority holes. Their complement has22 endpoints, so the same matching-connectivity rank method would require1024 legal short forests rather than2048. Actual included holes come from original Z union W and are independent. First reuse already accepted actual marked T26/T15/T17/T63 registries where applicable; new T37 geometries must have their own profile and positive certificates. No unprofiled universal local input is assumed.

Exact general source-transfer theorem

Let M be a short Q6 matching with twelve holes, free even root u=0 and any opposite-parity target v, free or covered. Its other even holes Z have size5, its odd holes W size6, and Z union W is independent. Choose a coordinate face A containing v, with a=|Z intersect A|, b=|W intersect A|. Either construction suffices when the actual marked B geometry is an accepted universal local matching input in the table below:

  • Even consumption: b>=1 and s=a+1-b>=0. Choose s sources S from Z intersect A. B minority holes are Z intersect B, majority holes are (W intersect B) union Y, with Y the s short source mirrors; omit Y.
  • Odd consumption: t=b-a-1>=1. Choose t sources S from W intersect A excluding v when free and excluding the root mirror. B minority holes are W intersect B, majority holes are (Z intersect B) union Y; omit Y.

The selected source set must exist. This is a statement for every original matching realizing the geometry; it is not a favorable-matching search.

Replay with full balanced Q5 endpoint inputs

For zero original crossings use the accepted five-direction theorem. Otherwise let X_A,X_B be actual distinct ports and delta indicate u in A. In even consumption, if delta=1 choose r=u and pair X_A union S into D. If delta=0 and s>=1 choose r in S and pair X_A union (S minus {r}). If delta=0 and s=0, shortness gives even-port surplus1; choose an even port r and pair the rest. The completed A matching has exactly b holes per parity with free r. Since b>=1, the accepted FULL balanced Q5 endpoint theorem applies, with covered or free odd target v. Even sources cannot consume v. The old b<=3 restriction served only the old endpoint import.

In odd consumption, choose r=u and pair X_A union S when delta=1. When delta=0 the even-port surplus is t+1>0; choose an even port r and pair (X_A minus {r}) union S. The completed A matching has exactly a+1 holes per parity with r free. The legal source exclusions retain v. The full endpoint theorem applies for every a, extending its former limited a<=2 input. Pairing-set parity is the original degree-counting identity, and arbitrary long or same-parity completion edges are allowed.

Every mirror is distinct and internally B-covered: independence excludes opposite-parity holes, a free original short mirror excludes a crossing port, and source choice excludes u. Delete D from the A path and attach all crossings/bridges. When u is in A the positive-crossing parity identities make D nonempty; when u is in B it is initially unattached. The tagged uv closure is a forest, including D-empty and target-port boundaries already present in the accepted uniform proof. Compress the A paths.

The only B conflicts are the same-parity mirrors Y. Each has a distinct original internally covered pendant mate of opposite parity, outside Y, ports, root and original holes. Conflict components therefore are paths and cannot close a cycle, even when a transferred edge joins two mirrors. Suppress them, retaining all path data and the tag. The resulting arbitrary B matching has holes exactly (H_B minus {u}) union Y and omissions Y. Apply its actual accepted marked theorem. Expand all recorded paths and delete the tag. All original edges and prescribed endpoints are restored; D was deleted, compressed edges expanded, and the tag removed. Every surviving new physical edge is short. This proves the theorem for free and covered v without extrapolating the old numerical endpoint bounds.

HOLE_RANGE_AND_COMPLETION.md — P6 的孔数范围与完整关闭标准

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：398fc807faa62a79d10c687828644b2111a0929c232e85d793c7c0f576fc9b84。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json。

P6 的孔数范围与完整关闭标准

日期：2026-11-01。完整 P6 尚未证明。

原问题的范围

Q6 有 64 个顶点、192 条边。一个匹配 M 每条边覆盖两个不同顶点，因此孔数为 64−2|M|。有指定自由根 u 的实例不可能完美，所以原问题可能涉及偶数孔数 2 至 64。每条短边各覆盖一个偶点与奇点，故孔的两个奇偶类大小相等。

保持根的极大补全与安全上界

固定 u，令 G=Q6−{u}。把 M 在 G 内不断添加两端都自由的短边，直到得到按包含关系极大的匹配 L。过程有限，且 M⊆L，u 始终未覆盖。若存在包含 L 的所需 Hamilton u—v 路径，该路径也包含 M。因此只须证明 G 内所有极大匹配的结论。“极大”不是“最大基数”，不能用最大匹配替代所有极大匹配。

G 有 192−6=186 条边，最大度数为 6。极大性意味着 G 的每条边都与 L 的某条边共端点，否则可以直接添加该边。对 ab∈L，G 中与它共端点的边数至多

dG(a)+dG(b)−1≤11.

这些边的集合允许重叠，但其并覆盖 G 的全部边。因此

186≤11|L|,|L|≥⌈186/11⌉=17.

另一方面，G 只有 63 个顶点，所以 |L|≤31。于是归约后只需考虑孔数不超过 64−2·17=30 的极大匹配，即候选孔数 2,4,6,…,30。这是安全范围，不声称每个候选孔数都可实现，也不声称上界最紧。

什么才算关闭整个 Q6

要对 G 内每个极大匹配 L、每个自由根 u、每个与 u 异奇偶的 v，证明存在包含 L 全部边的 Hamilton u—v 路径。允许以平移固定 u=0，以坐标置换把 v 归一化为重量 1、3、5 的三个代表，但每个代表都必须覆盖全部对应匹配，而不能只检查若干模板。

解析路线必须闭合每个归约及例外分支，并验证输入定理的全部假设。穷尽计算路线必须覆盖完整域，具有独立可复核的枚举或覆盖／UNSAT 证书。随机实例成功、超时、圈存在、自由—自由端点结果都不能替代这个全称指定端点结论。

双孔或四孔结果只是该目标的子类。即使 Z18 的完整四孔证明通过审计，仍要处理不能保持根自由而补到双孔／四孔的六孔及更多孔；也可以用一条统一定理一次关闭这些剩余情况，无须机械地逐孔数分别写定理。

Z16：目标侧异奇偶双孔的无半层转移

日期：2026-11-01。证明草稿，待独立审计。完整 P6 未证明。

命题

设 M 是 Q6 短匹配，孔为 u,z,w,t，u,z 偶、w,t 奇，目标 v 奇且被覆盖。设 z 不与 w,t 相邻。记 h=M(v)，M*=(M⧵{vh})∪{hu}。沿坐标 i 切分成 A,B，满足 v,z∈A、w,t∈B。若 MA* 不含半层，且 M* 有至少两条跨边，则 M 有 Hamilton u—v 延拓。

依赖 N11、N12、N14。跨边允许包含唯一的长边 hu；最终原匹配仍全为短边。

证明

记跨边端口为 XA,XB。因为 A 有两个孔，跨边数为偶数。候选 w⊕ei,t⊕ei 均不等于 z，且为 A 内偶点。除了原根 u 外，它们原来均由 MA 覆盖，因为跨面邻点是孔。收缩只改变 u,h 的伙伴：若两者同在 A，新 hu 内部覆盖二者；若只有一个在 A，则至多一个候选变成跨端口；若两者都在 B，候选覆盖不变。因此至少一个候选仍由 MA* 覆盖。

交换 w,t 后令 b=w⊕ei 是选中的候选，记 k=MA*(b)。令 F=MA*⧵{bk}。它不含半层，且在 A⧵{v,b} 内的自由集恰为

Y=XA∪{z,k}.

这些点互异，|Y|≥4 为偶数。由于 v,b 异奇偶，N12 给出 Y 上配对 W，使 F∪W 无半层。记 a=W(k)，则 a∈XA∪{z}；令 D=W⧵{ak}。于是 LA=MA*∪D 恰有孔 v,a，且 N11 的压缩恰为 F∪W。

N11 给出包含 LA、覆盖 A⧵{v} 的 a—b 路径。删除 D，得到非平凡顶点不交路径族，端点集恰为 XA∪{z,b}。D 不接触两个端点 a,b，故无孤立点；a=z 的情形也满足同一端点集公式。

给 XA 接回真实跨边，另加短边 bw、zy，其中 y=z⊕ei∈B。由于 z 不邻接 w,t，y 不等于 w,t；其为奇点，不等于偶点 u,h。原来 y 不是孔，跨面邻点 z 是孔，故 y 由原 MB 覆盖，收缩后仍由 MB* 覆盖。

将所得路径族缩成匹配 R，其覆盖集恰为 XB∪{w,y}。它与 MB* 的唯一覆盖冲突是 y。令 r=MB*(y)、s=R(y)，则 s∈XB∪{w}。y,r 原被 MB* 覆盖，s,t 不被覆盖，所以四点不同。定义

LB=(MB*⧵{yr})∪(R⧵{ys})∪{rs}.

该匹配恰有同奇偶的两个孔 y,t（均奇）。N14 给出包含 LB、覆盖 B⧵{y} 的圈。把 rs 展开为 r—y 及从 y 到 s 的对应转移路径，其余 R 边也全部展开。y 恢复一次，各 A 内点恢复一次，得到覆盖 Q6⧵{v} 并包含 M* 的圈。

最后删 hu、在 h 端接回 hv。原匹配全部恢复，所有辅助边消去或展开，新增边均短，得到所需 Hamilton 路径。证毕。

状态与依赖

PROVABLE AS STATED（相对于列明的已知定理）。独立同系列模型审读未发现实质性错误，接受状态为 provisional；见 NEAR_PERFECT_REVIEW.md，不代表形式化或跨系列验收。只使用用户 2501.19029v1.pdf 的 Theorem 1（Fink）、Theorem 6（Gregor–Novotný–Škrekovski，n≥5）和 Theorem 8（至多五方向匹配的端点路径刻画），以及 CORE_DERIVATION.md 的 D2/D3。全体 P6 仍未证明。

Theorem 6 的准确输入为 B(Q_n) 的完美匹配 P，异奇偶端点 x,y，xy不属于P。其结论是：存在包含 P、其余边全在 Q_n 的哈密顿 x–y 路径，当且仅当 R=(P{xa,yb})∪{ab} 不含半层，其中 a=P(x)、b=P(y)。

引理 N0：一般完美匹配的短边方向限制

设 P 为 B(Q_n) 的任意完美匹配，x,y异奇偶，xy不属于P。记 a=P(x)、b=P(y)，R=(P{xa,yb})∪{ab}。若R包含一个方向i的半层，那么P中的全部立方体边至多使用三个方向。

证明。 用下文N1相同的S,T记半层端点集及其补集，两者的诱导立方体边都仅沿i方向，且x,y属于T。如果ab不属于半层，则半层包含于P，S全部被内部匹配，因此P的所有短边都沿i。如果ab属于半层，则半层去掉ab包含于P；只有xa,yb可能跨越S,T。P的其余短边均在S或T内、沿i方向，xa,yb即使都是短边也至多引入两个额外方向。证毕。

本引理允许P包含任意多条长边。N3只需要这个短证明。下面N1保留为单长边情形的更精确结构说明。

引理 N1：单条长边时的半层刚性

设 P 为 B(Q_n) 的完美匹配，恰有一条非立方体边 f，其余边均为立方体边。给定异奇偶 x,y，xy不属于P，记 a=P(x)、b=P(y)，R=(P{xa,yb})∪{ab}。如果 R 含半层，则 f 长度为3，并且 P{f} 至多使用三个坐标方向。

证明。 设半层 H 的方向为 i，端点集为

S={z:∑k≠izk=ϵ(mod2)},T=V(Qn)⧵S.

Q_n[S] 和 Q_n[T] 都仅含方向 i 的边。R 不覆盖 x,y，所以 x,y属于T。

第一种情况：ab不属于H。 此时 H⊆P，因而 P 在 T 上也是完美匹配，其唯一长边 f 的两个端点 c,d 均在 T。T 的其余顶点仅能沿方向 i 匹配。于是 c 的 i 邻点必须是 d；否则 c 的 i 邻点没有可用的短边匹配伙伴。因此 f 是方向 i 的短边，矛盾。

第二种情况：ab属于H。 此时 b=a⊕e_i，且 H{ab}⊆P。S 中仅 a,b 不由这些半层边匹配，它们分别匹配到 x,y∈T。

若 f 是 xa 或 yb，则 T{x,y} 全由方向 i 的短边匹配。故 y=x⊕e_i。结合 b=a⊕e_i 得 d(x,a)=d(y,b)，不能恰有其中一条是长边，矛盾。

所以 f 不属于 {xa,yb}，并完全位于 T{x,y}。边 xa,yb 都是短边，可写

x=a⊕ej,y=b⊕ek,j,k≠i.

令 f=cd。T{x,y,c,d} 全由方向 i 匹配，故四点集 {x,y,c,d} 在翻转 i 下封闭。这四点互异。如果 x⊕e_i=y，那么 c⊕e_i=d，使 f 成短边，矛盾。因此交换 c,d 的名称后，必有

c=x⊕ei=b⊕ej,d=y⊕ei=a⊕ek.

若 j=k，则 y=x⊕e_i，已被排除。所以 i,j,k 两两不同，f 的两个端点恰在这三个坐标不同，d(c,d)=3。P 的短边除 xa,yb 之外全部沿方向 i；因此只使用 i,j,k 三方向。证毕。

引理 N2：包含完美匹配的路径必交替

若一条包含偶数个顶点的哈密顿路径包含完美匹配 P，那么沿路径编号0,1,…，P 的边恰连接位置(0,1),(2,3),…。

证明。 位置0的顶点只有一条路径边，该边必须是它的P边，故位置0与1由P匹配。位置2的P伙伴不能是已被匹配的位置1，只能是位置3。依次归纳即可。证毕。

若所有边连接二部图两侧，并从与 u 同奇偶的端点开始，则 P 中连接 u 到异奇偶 w 的边沿路径必按 u→w 的方向出现。

定理 N3：近完美补全足以解决所有指定终点

设 n≥5，M⊆E(Q_n) 是匹配，u不被M覆盖。假设存在立方体匹配 L⊇M，恰好不覆盖两个顶点 u,w。那么对每个与u异奇偶的v，都存在包含M的哈密顿 u–v 路径。

证明。 二部图两侧各有2^(n−1)点，每条匹配边覆盖两侧各一点，所以u,w异奇偶。

  1. 若 v=w，则由 D3（把人工边uw加入L，用Fink圈定理后删去它）得结论。
  2. 若 d(u,w)=1，则 L∪{uw} 是短边完美匹配。M 可补成完美匹配，应用已证 D2。
  3. 以下 v≠w 且 d(u,w)≥3。若 L 至多使用三个方向，则 M 也至多使用三个方向。应用原文 Theorem 8：u 未被 M 覆盖排除 C1、C2、C3，得到目标路径。
  4. 以下 L 使用至少四个方向。令 P=L∪{uw}，这是 B(Q_n) 的完美匹配，唯一长边为 uw。选一个 w 的立方体邻点 x，要求 x≠P(v)。这样的点存在：w 有n个邻点，至多一个被上述条件排除。由于uw不是短边，x≠u；又x与u同奇偶，v与u异奇偶，故x≠v。于是 xv不属于P。
  5. 对 P 和端点 x,v 应用 Theorem 6。若压缩匹配含半层，N0 将推出 L 只使用至多三个方向，与第4步矛盾。因此存在包含 P 的哈密顿 x–v 路径 K，其余边全为立方体边。
  6. 从 x 出发，N2 保证人工边 uw 的定向为 u→w。因此删去 uw 后得到两条顶点不交且覆盖全图的路径 K[x,u] 和 K[w,v]。这两条路径所有边均为立方体边，并仍包含 L 的全部边。
  7. 将第一条路径反向，再用立方体边 xw 接到第二条：
u ⤳ x—w ⤳ v.

x、w 原来属于不同分量，所以 xw 不可能已在删边后的路径中。连接后每个顶点恰出现一次，端点为 u,v，保留全部 L⊇M。证毕。

人工边在第6步被明确删除；第7步只添加已选的立方体边。因此没有把含长边路径冒充立方体路径。

推论及剩余范围
  • P6 的所有31边匹配均被 N3 覆盖；所有可在不覆盖u的前提下补成31边的匹配也被覆盖。
  • 在 Q6−V(M) 上作二部图最大匹配。若 M 可补成完美匹配，由 D2 解决；否则残余匹配能覆盖除u及某个w外的所有顶点时，由 N3 解决。
  • 不能由“|M|≤30”推出可近完美补全；极大匹配可能留下更多互不相邻的未覆盖点。
  • 全部六方向问题尚剩无法在保留M的前提下进行上述补全的匹配，需要继续处理这些残余图的匹配缺陷。
推论 N4：剩余问题的精确 Hall 障碍

设 F=V(Q_n)\V(M)，E 为 F 中与 u 同奇偶的点，O 为 F 中与 u 异奇偶的点。由于 M 是二部图匹配，|E|=|O|。对 S⊆E{u}，令 N_F(S) 为 S 在残余诱导图 Q_n[F] 中的邻点集。

等价判据。 存在某个 w∈O，使 M 可以补成恰不覆盖 u,w 的短边匹配，当且仅当

|NF(S)|≥|S|对每个 S⊆E⧵{u}成立。

证明。 补全边必须全部在 F 内且不覆盖 u，因此恰需在二部图 (E{u},O) 中找到饱和左侧的匹配。Hall定理给出所述充要条件。左右大小差1，饱和左侧后右侧恰剩一个w。证毕。

于是未被 N3 解决的实例都必须具有一个具体的非空集 S⊆E{u}，满足 |N_F(S)|<|S|。这是补全路线的障碍证书，不是哈密顿路径不存在的证书。

特别地，对 Q6 的30边匹配，若未覆盖点为 {u,z,w,t}，其中 u,z 同奇偶，则 N3 适用当且仅当 z 与 w,t 中至少一个相邻。该补全路线尚不能处理 d(z,w),d(z,t) 均大于1的情形。其余已知充分条件仍可能适用。

核验结果与来源

verify_near_perfect.py 对固定长边0—7的所有短边补全及所有异奇偶指定端点检查 N1：Q3 为2个补全、24个端点对；Q4 为48个补全、2688个端点对。所有半层障碍均符合N1的方向限制。这是小维数反例排查，不是六维全枚举。

construct_near_perfect.py 对16个六维31边匹配执行证明中的实际构造，分别让两未覆盖点距离为3或5；先找到允许唯一人工长边的中间路径，再按N2删边并拼接。最终16条路径全为立方体边，均通过全排列、端点和匹配包含检查。

原1152个六维样本依次按已知五方向、D2、N3、D5分类，数量为512、32、32、72，其余504个仍无这些引理的统一证明。此前剩余535个，故本轮新闭合31个此前只有逐实例证书的端点实例。这些数字仅说明原样本覆盖范围，不是全空间证明比例。

Theorem 6 的原始来源已核对：Gregor–Novotný–Škrekovski (2018), Theorem 2。它允许完美匹配来自 B(Q_n)，并要求延拓添加的边来自 Q_n；没有把“短边完美匹配”条件误套到人工长边情形。

与之同名检索结果中的 Fink–Mütze 长圈论文 是另一篇论文，其Theorem 9再次陈述这个输入定理；不能与用户的 Fink–Hotmar 五方向论文混为一篇。有限检索未认证本推论的新颖性。

单跨边实验的地位

single_bridge_probe.py 对固定种子的96个六维单跨边、错误奇偶实例搜索，匹配大小27—30；全部找到恰用三条跨边的合法路径。它包含终点等于强制跨边另一端的边界例。每条见证已检查全顶点覆盖、端点、邻接、匹配包含关系。

这些实例不是全空间枚举；N1—N3 的证明不依赖实验。相反，N3 给出了独立于三跨边配对选择的统一证明入口。
