Four-dimensional core certificates and an unconditional A4 split class

Date: 2026-11-01. Status: finite positive certificates plus mathematical reductions; independent review pending at initial writing. Full Q5 A4 and P6 remain unproved. None of the claims below assumes Q5 A4 or P6.

Exact core claims

N14_4. Every matching of K(Q4) with exactly two same-parity holes has a cycle through all vertices except either prescribed hole, preserving every matching edge and using only short new edges.

A4_4. Every matching of K(Q4) with exactly four holes of parity counts 3 and 1 has a cycle through all vertices except any prescribed majority-parity hole, preserving every matching edge and using only short new edges.

All matching edges may be arbitrary pairs of vertices, including same-parity long edges. A short edge changes exactly one coordinate. Hamilton circles in these statements have 15 vertices and may include the prescribed long edges.

Finite proof of N14_4

Translate the prescribed forbidden vertex to 0 by bitwise XOR. The other hole is a distinct even vertex, at Hamming distance two or four. A coordinate permutation takes it to 3 or 15 respectively. These automorphisms preserve short edges, long prescribed edges, and the extension question.

For each representative, all perfect matchings of the other 14 vertices are covered by a certificate file: q4_two_hole_3.bin or q4_two_hole_15.bin. There are 13!!=135135 such matchings in each representative. Every record contains the entire mate array and a 15-vertex cycle witnessing the assertion.

The independent checker verify_q4_extension_certificates.py checks:

  1. The mate array is an involution without fixed points on exactly the 14 prescribed covered vertices, with precisely the two prescribed holes.
  2. The cycle contains all 15 required vertices exactly once, includes every matching edge, and has only short edges outside the matching.
  3. No perfect matching is omitted or repeated. To certify this without depending on the generator's recursion order, compute its rank as follows. Remove the least remaining vertex x. If its mate has index i, starting at zero, in the increasing list of other remaining vertices, its rank is i(2k−3)!! plus the recursively computed rank of the remaining matching, where 2k is the number of vertices before removing this pair. Empty rank is zero and (−1)!!=1. There are 2k−1 disjoint equal-size blocks, so induction proves a bijection with 0,…,(2k−1)!!−1. The checker marks all these ranks and requires each exactly once.

All 270270 records pass. Thus, modulo the transparent finite certificate verification, the two representatives and symmetry prove N14_4 completely. This proof does not import the five-dimensional version of N14.

Finite proof of A4_4

Translate the minority-parity hole to a=0. Let v be the forbidden odd hole and b,t the two remaining odd holes. If a is adjacent to b or t, add that short edge. The resulting matching has two same-parity holes, and N14_4 proves the required 15-cycle avoiding v.

Otherwise b,t are distinct weight-three vertices in Q4. Permuting coordinates makes their unordered pair {7,11}. Their supports share coordinates 0 and 1 and differ in coordinates 2 and 3. The permutations of the two common coordinates and of the two differing coordinates preserve this unordered pair. The six possible forbidden odd vertices have exactly three orbits:

{1,2},{4,8},{13,14}.

Choose representatives v=1,4,13. For each, the other 12 vertices have 11!!=10395 perfect matchings. Files q4_four_hole_1.bin, q4_four_hole_4.bin, q4_four_hole_13.bin contain a 15-cycle certificate for each one. The same independent checker validates the matching, cycle, and full rank coverage. All 31185 records pass. Together with the adjacent branch, this proves A4_4.

The five files total 301455 certificates. The search programs' positive outputs are independently checked; neither a numerical solver's feasibility judgment nor the completeness of its search is needed for acceptance.

Derived four-dimensional path inputs

N10_4. Let L be an arbitrary matching of K(Q4) with exactly two holes r,s. For any y≠r with p(y)=p(s) there is a Hamilton r--y path containing L, with all newly added edges short.

If y is free, then y=s. Add rs to make a perfect matching of K(Q4), apply Fink's perfect-matching extension theorem, and delete rs from the resulting Hamilton circle. It yields the stated path. This is the only external extension theorem needed here; it permits arbitrary original edges of the complete graph and adds short edges.

If y is covered, let k=L(y). The matching L′=L−yk+kr has same-parity holes y,s. N14_4 supplies a 15-cycle avoiding y and containing L′. Delete kr to obtain an r--k path on all vertices except y, and append the original edge ky. The path now contains all of L and only short edges outside L. The appended edge may be long, but is an original required matching edge.

NC_4. If the two holes of L have opposite parity, L extends to a Hamilton circle of K(Q4) with only short new edges. Choose any short neighbor y of the free root r, use N10_4, and close the Hamilton path by ry. Such a spanning path on 16 vertices cannot already contain the edge between its two endpoints, so this produces a simple circle.

K4_4. A balanced four-hole matching of K(Q4) has a Hamilton path from any free root r to any vertex y of the opposite parity, preserving the matching and adding only short edges. If y is free, add the auxiliary edge ry; the remaining holes are opposite, so NC_4 gives a full circle; delete ry. If y is covered with mate k, swap yk to kr. The four holes now have counts 3 and 1, with y in the majority. Apply A4_4 avoiding y, delete kr, append the original ky. Both constructions meet the specified endpoints and restore all original matching edges.

S4D: a Q5 A4 class closed without assuming A4

Let F be an arbitrary K(Q5) matching with holes a,b,t,v, where a has the minority parity and the desired circle must avoid v. Suppose a coordinate cut has on one side A exactly the holes v,b, on the other side B exactly a,t, and at least one original F edge crosses the cut. Then the Q5 A4 conclusion holds for F.

Let the crossing matching be C, with endpoint sets XA,XB. Since |A|=16 and exactly two vertices of A are globally free, the equality 2|FA|+|C|=14 makes |C| even. Thus it is at least two. Choose any perfect matching D of the complete graph on XA. Then FA∪D has the same-parity holes v,b. N14_4 supplies a cycle on A⧵{v} containing it, with all other edges short.

Delete D. Because D is a nonempty matching in a simple circle, the result is a disjoint family of nontrivial paths, with endpoints exactly XA. Attach each corresponding original crossing edge of C. The paths now have endpoints XB, disjoint interiors in A⧵{v}, and together cover that entire side. Replace each by a formal edge to get a matching R on XB. No restriction on the length or parity of edges in C or R is imposed; edges of C are original required edges, not new short edges.

The matching FB∪R of K(B) has precisely the opposite-parity holes a,t. NC_4 supplies its full Hamilton circle. Expand every R edge into its corresponding path. This gives a single circle through V(Q5)⧵{v}, containing F and with every edge outside F short. All artificial edges D,R have disappeared. This proves S4D.

G4D: a whole hole-geometry family, with no matching restriction

Normalize a=0. If both masks

v&b&¬t≠0,v&t&¬b≠0

are nonzero (all masks restricted to the five cube coordinates), then every matching with these holes satisfies Q5 A4.

Choose a coordinate i from the first mask and j from the second. The four holes have distinct (i,j) patterns: a:00, b:10, t:01, v:11. If any matching edge crosses either coordinate cut, that cut has the S4D hole split, so S4D applies. If no edge crosses either cut, all matching edges lie within the four 8-vertex Q3 cells. Each cell has exactly one hole and hence seven covered vertices, impossible for an internal matching. Therefore at least one cut has crossings, proving the claim.

For normalized residual Q5 geometries (a=0, b,t nonadjacent to a, unordered b,t, and distinct forbidden odd v), there are 770 choices. Exactly 255 have both masks nonzero, 350 only one, and 165 neither. These are labeled geometric counts, not isomorphism counts or matching counts. G4D closes all matchings in the first class. S4D can also close instances in the one-mask class when a corresponding cut actually has a crossing edge.

Remaining obligations

The four-dimensional input A4_4 does not by itself prove five-dimensional A4. The complete remaining transfer for hole configurations outside G4D, including zero-crossing cases, is not supplied here. A4_4 and K4_4 are now available for that research; they must not be invoked with an unverified dimension or endpoint condition. The unconditional full six-hole P6 result and all remaining 8--18-hole obligations remain open.

General Q4 inputs obtained by short-edge augmentation

Date: 2026-11-01. These consequences use the already certified N14_4, A4_4,N10_4,K4_4 from Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md, not Q5 A4 or full P6.

Geometric fact

Any two distinct vertices of the same parity in Q4 have at least six distinct neighbors: their distance is two or four, giving respectively two or zero common neighbors among their four neighbors each. Therefore at most two opposite-parity vertices are nonadjacent to both. Consequently any two free vertices of one parity and three free vertices of the other parity contain a short edge between the two sets.

GQ4-avoid

Let F be any matching of K(Q4) whose holes have counts m and m+2 in the two parity classes. For any prescribed hole v in the larger class, F extends to a circle through exactly Q4 minus v, with only short new edges.

For m=0 use N14_4. For m=1 use A4_4. For m>=2 choose two holes in the smaller class and three holes in the larger class excluding v; the latter are available because m+1>=3. The geometric fact supplies a short edge between these free sets. Add it to F, preserving v as free and decreasing m by one. Repeat to a base case. The base-case circle contains all added edges, which were short, so it is also the required extension of F.

GQ4-path

Let F be any matching of K(Q4) with equally many holes in both parity classes. For any free root r and any opposite-parity vertex y, F extends to a Hamilton r--y path with only short new edges.

If each class has one hole, use N10_4; if each has two, use K4_4. If each has m>=3 holes, choose two holes of r's parity distinct from r and three holes of the other parity. Add a short edge given by the geometric fact. This preserves r as free and reduces m by one. The target y is allowed to become covered: N10_4/K4_4 do not require it to remain free. Iterate to a base case, whose path preserves the original matching. All added matching edges were short, as required.

GQ4-cycle

Every matching of K(Q4) with balanced hole counts extends to a Hamilton circle with only short new edges. If there are no holes, use Fink's perfect-matching theorem. Otherwise use GQ4-path from a free root to a short neighbor and add their short edge to close the spanning path.

These general Q4 lemmas are available for the next five-dimensional auxiliary problems arising from the eight-hole Q6 layer. They do not themselves establish any whole eight-hole or higher P6 level.

Q4_PERFECT_ENDPOINT_ABUNDANCE.md — Q4 完美匹配的 Hamilton 路径端点丰度

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：aea312b744c6c6902128007c8a08853b32980eeae5c7ecb83429b3b52feb57a8。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_ALL_EP0_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, Q4_NEIGHBOR_ABUNDANCE_REVIEW.json, T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json, T44_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING_REVIEW.json。

Q4 完美匹配的 Hamilton 路径端点丰度

日期：2026-11-01。状态：有限证书和逆像穷尽核验 PASS；Q5 T15、P6 不由此关闭。 完整 Q5 A4 及 A6/K6 的先前已证状态不变。

定理

设 P 为完全图 K(Q4) 上的任意完美匹配，允许长边和同奇偶边。 固定根 0，令 G(P) 为所有满足下述条件的奇顶点 y 的集合：存在 Hamilton 0--y 路径， 包含 P 的每条边，且每条不属于 P 的路径边都是短边。

则

|G(P)|≥4,G(P)∩{7,11,13,14}≠∅.

两条下界都能取等。平移所有顶点可得任意根 r 的版本：至少四个异奇偶可行端点， 且至少一个与根距离 3 的可行端点。

所有大小恰为 4 的端点集精确如下，每种发生于 105 个完美匹配：

精确可行奇端点集 G(P) 个数
{1,2,4,7} 105
{1,2,8,11} 105
{1,4,8,13} 105
{2,4,8,14} 105

例如 P={01,23,45,67,89,(10)(11),(12)(13),(14)(15)}（全部位 1 方向短边） 恰有端点 {2,4,8,14}。因此不存在把“四”改成“五”或把“一个距离 3 端点”改成“两个”的普遍结论。

路径与避两孔圈的精确等价

若 P(0)=y，任何包含 P 的路径在两个端点处都必须使用边 0y，它会成为两个顶点的独立分量， 所以不可能是 16 顶点 Hamilton 路径。

现在设 P(0)=a≠y，记 P(y)=b。四点 0,y,a,b 不同，定义

T=P−{0a,yb}+{ab}.

这是恰有孔 0,y 的七边匹配。存在目标 Hamilton 0--y 路径， 当且仅当存在避开 0,y、包含 T 且新增边短的 14 圈。

证明：路径的端点边必为 0a,yb。删去两个端点得到覆盖其余 14 点的 a--b 路径， 加上 ab 得到圈。其余边保留 P−{0a,yb}，新增的辅助边 ab 已列为 T 的必含边。 14 点路径的两个端点不会已经相邻，否则长度只能为一条边，所以不会产生重边。 反向从圈删除其必含边 ab，在两个端点分别接回 a0,by，即得到所需路径。 两方向都保留原匹配的所有边，所有非匹配边仍短。

已认证的两张完整圈表及本次复核

两个基础孔型为 {0,1} 和 {0,7}，分别对应距离 1 和距离 3。 每张表包含 13!!=135135 个匹配；正记录给出显式 14 圈，负记录圈区为全 255。 已有完整审计见 CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.md。

本次独立 checker 直接读取两张二进制表，不导入旧生成器、checker 或保存的例外 JSON，重新验证：

孔型 匹配记录 正圈 负例
0,1 135135 135084 51
0,7 135135 135082 53

匹配均通过 mate 对合和孔支持检查；独立的匹配秩没有重复且覆盖完整区间。 每个正圈检查确切支持集、所有匹配边以及新增边短。 对每个负例，枚举所有与原匹配边不重合的短完美匹配：任何所需圈都必须由原七边匹配与这样一个 短完美匹配组成。checker 直接计算每个所得 2-factor 的连通分量，全部都超过一个，故严格证明不可行。 结果 JSON 保存全部 104 个负例及其补匹配的分量计数分布；没有信任失败的 Hamilton 搜索。

任意奇 y 的重量为 1 或 3；选取把 1 或 7 映到 y 的坐标置换，将相应完整负例表传送到孔 0,y。 固定任何一个这样的置换都足够，因为它在全部匹配上给出双射。输出保存了八个置换。

只枚举负例逆像足以证明全称命题

给定一个不可行 T，对它每条边 ab 及两个方向，构造

P=T−{ab}+{0a,yb}.

这些恰好是所有满足 P(0)≠y 且在 y 不可行的完美匹配。 任意这样的 P 经正向公式必得到一个负表记录，再选其辅助边 ab 就能被逆构造找回； 反之，每个逆构造的 P 在该 y 不可行，由上面的等价直接得到。

四个距离 1 端点、四个距离 3 端点，共生成 4(51+53)·7·2=5824 个带端点标签的逆像，去重后得到 4708 个完美匹配。 对每个候选再次遍历八个奇端点，计算正向 T 并查负表，与逆生成端点集合核对， 另外加入 P(0) 为奇点时的必坏端点。所得精确分布为：

坏奇端点数 4708 个候选中的完美匹配数
1 2072
2 2180
3 36
4 420

候选之外的每个完美匹配，除可能的奇点 P(0) 外，其余七个或八个奇端点全部可行。 因此没有扫描其余约两百万个正匹配，也没有遗漏任意一个可能有两个以上坏端点的输入。 上表最大坏数为 4，证明第一个下界。

候选内的可行距离 3 端点数分布为 {1:420,2:276,3:2212,4:1800}； 候选外至少有三个可行距离 3 端点。因此所有完美匹配至少有一个距离 3 可行端点，证明第二个下界。 不存在四个重量 3 奇端点全部不可行的完美匹配。

这里“最小端点集”如指最小基数，精确为开头的四种大小 4 集合； 如指在全部可能端点集中按包含关系极小，则共有 22 种（4 个大小 4、12 个大小 5、6 个大小 6）， 完整列表也保存在结果 JSON 中，避免混淆这两个含义。

可复现文件和使用边界

独立实现：q4_perfect_endpoint_abundance_check.py。 执行命令：

D:\anaconda\python.exe research\six_directions\q4_perfect_endpoint_abundance_check.py

结果：q4_perfect_endpoint_abundance_check.json， 包含 4708 个候选的全部匹配边与精确坏端点集合、两表哈希、checker 哈希及上述计数。 整个结论只使用 Q4 的有限证书，不调用 Q5 或 P6。 在拼接中可直接使用“任意完美匹配至少一个距离 3 可行端点”；要推出 Q5 T15 的具体分支， 仍须单独核对顶点映射、端点交集及原边保持等拼接条件。

Q4_RICH_GLUING.md — Opposite forbidden parities force intersecting optional-edge unions

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：69ac96bc618aeffdf4c3d1d1094d80d783a9ac6d5c7bd55a6120d377a5dd4b19。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REUSE_REVIEW.json, Q4_RICH_GLUING_REVIEW.json, TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json, TEN_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json。

Opposite forbidden parities force intersecting optional-edge unions

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft; independent audit pending. This is a four-dimensional gluing input, not the full Q5 T15 theorem.

Exact claim

On one labeled Q4, let L have exactly two same-parity holes, one specified as forbidden vertex a. Let R have either two same-parity holes including its forbidden vertex b, or four holes with parity counts 1:3 and b in the majority class. Assume a and b have opposite parities. Both matchings are arbitrary matchings of K(Q4), not necessarily short.

There is a short edge e outside BOTH matchings and extending 15-cycles C_L on Q4-a and C_R on Q4-b, each containing its matching and e, and having all new edges short.

Equivalently, their optional-new-edge unions intersect. The two cycles may be chosen independently after choosing the common edge. No simultaneous prescription of a whole optional-edge union in a single cycle is asserted.

Dependencies and normalization

Translate a to 0, so b is odd. Coordinate permutations reduce the other hole of L to 3 or 15. The same two-hole normalization applies to R when it has two holes. Four-hole R with a short edge between its minority hole and a nonforbidden majority hole reduces by adding that edge to a two-hole instance, still avoiding b.

For remaining four-hole R, translate the minority hole to 0. Its two nonforbidden majority holes have weight three, so permute them to 7,11. The remaining forbidden majority hole has representatives 1,4,13. This classification was checked on all marked geometries in A6_FINITE_INPUTS_REVIEW.md; it uses no Q5 theorem.

Positive certificates, not exact spectrum assumptions

The files q4_n14_rich_3.bin, q4_n14_rich_15.bin list every matching with the corresponding two holes 0,p, avoiding 0. Each has 135135 records. The files q4_a4_rich_1.bin, _4.bin, _13.bin list every matching with holes 0,7,11,v, avoiding v. Each has 10395 records. Each record stores the sixteen mate bytes (255 denotes a hole), a one-byte cycle count, and that many explicit 15-vertex cycles. Define the stored union U to be the union of all their edges outside the required matching. It is a subset of the true optional-edge union.

verify_q4_rich_spectrum_gluing.py verifies matching rank coverage, each cycle's exact vertices, every required edge and every new short edge. It checks all 301455 records and 1634808 positive cycles. Every stored union has at least 15 edges. Call a stored union high if it has at least 18 edges, and low otherwise. The low records are exactly:

  • holes 0,3: 6 records, each with stored union size 16;
  • holes 0,15: 36 records, each with stored union size 15;
  • four-hole representative v=4: 20 records;
  • four-hole representatives v=1,13: no low records.

These statements concern stored, witnessed unions. An exact upper bound on the true spectrum is not required. The producer may have explored all cycles on a low record, but this proof never relies on that exhaustiveness.

If either matching has a high witnessed union and the other has a union of size at least 15, intersection follows from 18+15>32, since Q4 has 32 edges. It remains to compare the finite low candidates.

Complete coverage of low candidates

Expand the two-hole low records under all coordinate permutations. This gives 72 distinct candidate matchings with forbidden vertex 0. For the second face, also translate by each odd vertex; there are 576 distinct two-hole candidates with odd forbidden vertex. If different transported certificates describe the same matching and forbidden vertex, take the union of their stored unions. This is still a witnessed subset of the true optional-edge union, so is valid for improving the bound.

For a four-hole R admitting an added short edge f, set P=R+f. If P is high, R is high as well: every witnessed new edge for P is a new edge for R. If P is low, R is obtained by deleting f from one of the transported two-hole low candidates. The same witnessed cycles show the union U(P) union {f} is available for R. Enumerate removal of every SHORT required edge from every such low P. This includes each potentially low adjacent-reducible R; it may also include R that has another high completion, which is harmless. Repeated R candidates can again merge their unions.

For nonadjacent four-hole R, transport the 20 low representative records under all 384 Q4 automorphisms and retain odd forbidden vertices. Combine these candidates with those obtained by edge removal. After merging and discarding unions already of size at least 18, 4128 four-hole candidates remain. All have witnessed unions of size at least 15.

No matching outside these lists can lack a high certificate: the two-hole tables, the four-hole residual tables, and the adjacent augmentation exhaust all input possibilities. In particular the procedure never assumes that a low table entry has a mathematically small exact spectrum.

Finite intersection and conclusion

The verifier compares every one of the 72 first-face low candidates with all 576 second-face two-hole candidates and all 4128 second-face four-hole candidates. In every pair the witnessed unions intersect; the minimum intersection size is three in each comparison. Thus the low-low cases hold as well. This proves the exact claim.

Five-dimensional consequences

Consider a matching F of K(Q5) with two prescribed omitted holes of the same GLOBAL parity. Split into Q4 faces A,B separating the omitted holes. Suppose either each face has exactly two holes of that parity (the T44_5 split case), or one face has two holes of that parity and the other has 1:3 holes with that parity the majority (the T15 split case).

The crossing count c is even. If c>0, pair A ports into D and use the appropriate Q4 avoided cycle on A. Delete D, attach original crossings, and compress paths onto B ports. The B matching has exactly its original holes; its avoided-cycle theorem supplies the second cycle, and expansion gives one 30-vertex circle omitting the two prescribed holes.

If c=0, the faces' required matchings are independent. On identifying the two faces by short bridges, their omitted vertices have opposite LOCAL parities because their GLOBAL parities agree. The present theorem supplies corresponding optional edges in the two avoided cycles. Delete those edges and add the two short bridges joining corresponding endpoints. The result is a single 30-vertex circle. Required edges are never removed, and the new bridges are short. This closes the zero-crossing case as well.

Thus these two geometric split conditions suffice for ALL original matchings, regardless of crossing count. Other T44_5/T15 geometries and full Q6 P6 are not asserted here.

Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION.md — Q4 T15：精确分类（含可核验正证书与解析负证书）

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：bab8d4cecffa46f3f8fb55046a381cfa0303878671f7b273f6ae011630c68adc。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：A10_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json, A10_ORBIT2_REVIEW.json, A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBIT4_FULL_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBIT5_FULL_REVIEW.json, A8_ORBITS2_3_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION_REVIEW.json, Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json, T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_REVIEW.json, TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json。

Q4 T15：精确分类（含可核验正证书与解析负证书）

日期：2026-11-01。状态：Q4 分类已独立核验；Q5 T15、P6 仍未关闭。 完整 Q5 A4 及 A6/K6 已由先前独立证明包关闭并审计，本任务不改变这些结论。

定义与定理

把 V(Q4) 写为 {0,…,15}，短边指端点异或为 1,2,4,8 的边。 K(Q4) 是该顶点集上的完全图；原匹配中的边可以是长边。

设 F 是 K(Q4) 上的匹配，其孔集恰为 {a}∪H，其中 a 为偶顶点、 H 为五个奇顶点。指定两个不同的避点 v,w∈H。记 N(a) 为 a 的四个短邻点。

精确分类。 存在一个顶点集恰为 V(Q4)⧵{v,w}、包含 F 全部边、 且所有新增边均为短边的简单 14 圈，当且仅当下面的障碍不存在：

{v,w}⊆N(a),N(a)⧵{v,w}={p,q},pq∈F.(OB)

由异或平移，同一定理也适用于奇偶互换的孔型。这里首先认证的是一偶孔、五奇孔的版本。 这不是断言所有 T15 输入均可扩张：条件 (OB) 确实给出负例。

障碍的必要性：被迫的三角形

假设 (OB) 成立。a 是孔，因此圈在 a 处的两条边均为新增短边。 两个避点 v,w 不在圈上，故圈在 a 处只能使用 ap,aq。 又 pq∈F，圈必须保留 pq。三个顶点 a,p,q 已各有两条圈边，形成一个完整的三角形分量。 它不能同时属于一个连通的简单 14 圈，矛盾。 这证明每个被标为负例的输入数学上不可行，不依赖搜索失败或搜索实现的完备性。

充分性第一步：有可用邻孔时增广到 T44_4

若存在 b∈H⧵{v,w} 与 a 短邻接，则增添短边 ab。 由于两端都是 F 的孔，F′=F∪{ab} 仍是匹配，其孔集为 H⧵{b}， 恰为四个同奇偶顶点，并包含两个指定避点 v,w。

应用已证的 T44（即 Q4 的 T44_4）：四个同奇偶孔的任意匹配都可以扩张成一个避开指定两个孔的 14 圈，所有新增边为短边。所得圈包含 F′，因此包含 F；边 ab 相对原 F 也是短边。 这完整证明该分支。

这个分支不可能含 (OB)：若两个避点都是 a 的邻点，而一个剩余邻点 b 是孔， 则剩余两个邻点不能由 F 配成一条边。

本次独立 checker 没有只引用旧审核结论，而是重新验证 T44 的全部 30 个文件、 311850 个正圈证书以及两奇偶类共 840 个有标记孔几何的覆盖。 T44 的证书参数及先前表述见 Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_TRANSFER.md。 本证明使用其有限 Q4 结论，不调用同一文件中的 Q5 推论，也不另行导入 Fink 定理。

充分性第二步：无可用邻孔时的四个轨道

平移 a 到 0。三个可用奇孔 H⧵{v,w} 都不是 0 的邻点， 因而都是重量 3 顶点。四个重量 3 顶点为 7,11,13,14；坐标置换可把三个可用孔取成 7,11,13，即把唯一未选的重量 3 顶点取成 14。

此时两个避点必须来自 {1,2,4,8,14}。保持 {7,11,13} 的坐标置换固定坐标位 1， 任意置换位 2,4,8。所以避点的无序对恰有四类：

避点代表 固定可用孔后的轨道大小 所有 a=0 残余几何中的大小 匹配数 正证书 解析负例
(1,2) 3 12 945 840 105
(2,4) 3 12 945 840 105
(1,14) 1 4 945 945 0
(2,14) 3 12 945 945 0

每个输入有十个被覆盖顶点，所有匹配共有 9!!=945 个。 四个文件 q4_six_two_avoided_v_w.bin 各有 945 个长度 30 字节的记录：前 16 字节是 mate 数组， 值 255 表示孔；后 14 字节是圈顶点序列，全部为 255 表示负记录。

全新 checker 独立生成无序边集表示的完整匹配集合，然后逐记录核验孔、无自环对合及唯一性， 从集合删除该匹配，最终集合必须为空。对每条正记录检查：恰好 14 个不同顶点、恰好避开 v,w、 保留全部匹配边，且每条不属于匹配的圈边均为短边。无需信任产生圈的 DFS。

对每条负记录，checker 直接验证 (OB)，然后使用上面的三角形证明。 前两类的负记录恰为含剩余邻点边 pq 的所有匹配；固定 pq 后其余八个顶点有 7!!=105 个匹配。 后两类有避点 14∉N(0)，全部 945 个输入都有正圈证书。 四类共验证 3780 条记录，其中 3570 个正证书、210 个解析不可行证书。 这同时证明了残余分支充分性与精确性。

全部有标记孔几何的独立覆盖

对固定 a=0，共有 (85(52=))560 个几何，其中 520 个属于增广分支， 40 个属于上述四个互不重叠的坐标置换轨道，轨道大小为 12,12,4,12。 checker 进一步遍历所有八个偶顶点 a，直接检验全部 8·560=4480 个有标记孔几何： 4160 个通过增广，320 个通过四轨道覆盖。

归一化使用图自同构 x↦π(x⊕a)；它保留短边、匹配及圈， 把原避点对精确映到证书的避点对。没有把避点与可用孔混同，也没有丢失原匹配的任意长边。

综上，两个分支覆盖全部输入，正记录提供充分性，(OB) 提供负例的必要且充分刻画。

复现与边界

独立 checker：q4_t15_classification_independent_check.py。 在工作区运行：

D:\anaconda\python.exe research\six_directions\q4_t15_classification_independent_check.py

输出 q4_t15_classification_independent_check.json， 记录所有输入证书和 checker 的 SHA-256。独立审核见 Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION_REVIEW.md 及其 JSON。 本定理仅是 Q4 层内的精确工具。向 Q5 拼接时必须另证压缩匹配不落入 (OB)，或另行修复； 不能从这里推出 Q5 T15 或完整 P6。完整 Q5 A4 已由先前独立证明包证明，本任务没有重新证明它， 也不改变它及 A6/K6 的已关闭状态；当前结论记账见 A6_AND_EIGHT_FREE_CLOSED.md。

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：717f1f538eaf22d8dbb40699358516c5921d2cc24df63a4fe3420bb5f80b2f48。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json, A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_REVIEW.json, Q5_T63_COMPLETE_SPLIT_REVIEW.json, TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json。

Two avoided vertices in Q4 and minority-isolating A4 cuts

Date: 2026-11-01. Status: finite certificates and reductions; independent review pending at initial writing. Q5 A4 and full P6 remain unproved.

T44: four same-parity holes, two prescribed avoided holes

Let L be an arbitrary matching of K(Q4) with four holes, all of the same parity. For any two prescribed holes x,y, there is a cycle through exactly V(Q4)⧵{x,y}, containing every edge of L, with only short new edges. Thus this is a 14-vertex cycle, including the other two holes.

Translate x to 0. The other holes then are even. Permute coordinates to take y to 3 or 15, covering its possible distances two and four. For each choice, the remaining two holes are any unordered pair of the remaining six even vertices, giving 15 configurations. Each of the 30 configurations has 11!!=10395 perfect matchings of its 12 covered vertices.

The files q4_two_avoided_p_b_t.bin contain all these matchings and a 14-cycle for each. Every 30-byte record contains a 16-byte mate array (255 denotes holes), followed by the 14 cycle vertices. The independent checker verify_q4_two_avoided_certificates.py verifies the matching, the cycle and its required/new edges, and complete bijective matching-rank coverage as defined in Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md. All 311850 records pass. No Hamilton-search completeness or negative result is relied on. This proves T44 by explicit exhaustive positive certificates and the stated symmetries.

S1D: minority-isolating cuts

Consider a Q5 A4 matching F with minority hole a and majority holes b,t,v, where v is forbidden. Suppose a coordinate cut has all three majority holes in side A and a in side B. Let w be the short neighbor of a across this cut. Assume w∉{b,t,v}, and suppose either

  1. w is covered by an internal edge of FA; or
  2. w is a crossing endpoint and the crossing matching has at least three edges.

Then the full Q5 A4 conclusion holds for F.

Let C be the crossing matching, with endpoint sets XA,XB and size c. Since side B has exactly one hole, 2|FB|+c=15, so c is odd and positive. Choose a perfect matching D on XB∪{a}; an additional choice in case 2 is specified below. Then FB∪D is a perfect matching of K(B). By Fink's perfect-matching extension theorem it has a Hamilton circle with only short new edges. Delete the nonempty matching D to obtain disjoint nontrivial paths with endpoints XB∪{a}. Attach the original edges of C at XB, and attach the new short bridge aw at a.

Case 1: internal partner at the bridge endpoint

The resulting paths have distinct endpoints XA∪{w}, and interiors partition B. Compress them to a matching R on this endpoint set. Its unique overlap in covered vertices with FA is w. Write k=FA(w) and d=R(w). The matching

L=(FA⧵{wk})∪(R⧵{wd})∪{kd}

has precisely the four holes b,t,v,w, all of the same parity because w is opposite to the minority hole a. All listed edges are disjoint: k is internal to FA, d∈XA, and none is a hole. Apply T44 to avoid v,w and obtain a cycle on A⧵{v,w}. Expand kd into the original edge kw followed by the transferred w--d path. Expand every other edge of R. This restores w, all of B, all original edges of F, and gives a single circle through Q5⧵{v}.

Case 2: a crossing partner at the bridge endpoint

Let x∈XB be the original partner of w. Choose D to contain ax; pair the remaining c−1 ports arbitrarily. Because c≥3, D has at least two edges. In the B circle with D removed, the vertices a,x lie in different path components: deleting ax alone leaves an a--x path containing every other edge of D, so deleting one more of those edges separates a from x.

After attaching aw and the original xw, those two different paths join at w into a single path. No cycle is created. All resulting paths have distinct endpoints XA⧵{w} and disjoint interiors partitioning B∪{w}. Compress them to a matching R on XA⧵{w}. Now L=FA∪R has the four same-parity holes b,t,v,w. Apply T44 avoiding v,w and expand R. The expanded circle restores w and B, preserves F, and uses only short new edges. This proves case 2 and S1D.

The excluded crossing case c=1 cannot be inserted into this proof: then D={ax} and the two attachments close a separate B-side circle. A different argument would be needed; no conclusion is asserted for it here.

G2D: two coordinates shared by all majority holes suffice

Normalize a=0. If b,t,v have at least two common 1-coordinates, then every matching with these holes satisfies Q5 A4.

Choose two such coordinates i,j. For each, the minority-isolating cut has an odd positive crossing count. The bridge endpoint wi=2i (respectively wj=2j) is not a hole, because the majority holes have both coordinates equal to one. Thus each endpoint is either internally matched in its majority side, or is a crossing endpoint. S1D solves the input unless both cuts have exactly one crossing edge and that edge meets the respective wi,wj.

Suppose both cuts have this exceptional form. Write the unique crossing edges as ei,ej. If they are the same edge, it must be wiwj, connecting cells 10 and 01 in the (i,j) split. No matching edge then leaves cell 00. That 8-vertex cell has exactly one hole, a, so it cannot match its seven other vertices internally. This is a contradiction.

If ei≠ej, then ei cannot cross coordinate j, whose unique crossing edge is ej. Consequently ei runs from cell 10 to cell 00; the same reasoning makes ej run from cell 01 to cell 00. No matching edge leaves cell 11. That cell has exactly the three holes b,t,v, so it cannot match its five other vertices internally. This is again a contradiction. Therefore at least one cut satisfies S1D, proving G2D.

Scope together with G4D

In the 770 normalized residual Q5 hole configurations (a=0, unordered nonadjacent b,t, distinct odd forbidden v), G4D from Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md covers 255 and G2D covers 120, with intersection 30. Their union therefore covers all matchings in 345 configurations; 425 configurations remain outside these two geometry-only sufficient conditions. S4D and S1D can additionally handle individual matchings in that remaining domain when their crossing conditions hold.

These counts are neither matching counts nor a minimal orbit classification. The full Q5 A4 statement, and hence the unconditional full six-hole P6 reduction, remains open. All other remaining P6 hole levels also remain open.

Full Q5 A10: assembly from augmentation and three marked orbits

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer candidate; final independent acceptance pending.

Claim

For every matching F of K(Q5) with four holes of one parity and six of the other, and every specified majority hole v, there is a simple cycle on exactly Q5⧵{v} containing every edge of F. Every edge of the cycle outside F is a cube edge. Required edges of F may be long or join vertices of equal parity.

Status and dependencies

The proof below is a complete assembly conditional on acceptance of the final-orbit GF(2) certificate package. The original theorem is not weakened. Its dependencies are full A8, the accepted exact A10 geometry classification, the first two accepted A10 orbit theorems, and the new last-orbit forest/rank theorem. Independent review must discharge that last dependency and inspect the assembly before marking full A10 true.

Proof

Translate the cube by v. This is an automorphism preserving short edges, arbitrary matching edges, and the specified omitted vertex; after translation v=0 and its parity class is the even class. Write the other majority holes as Z, |Z|=5, and the minority holes as W, |W|=4.

If z∈Z and w∈W are short-adjacent, add zw to F. The resulting matching has five even and three odd holes and still leaves 0 free. Full A8 gives the required 31-cycle containing this larger matching and omitting 0. Relative to F its one additional required edge zw is short, so this cycle proves the original claim.

Otherwise Z∪W is independent. The exact geometry classification accepted in Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json contains 55 such marked geometries. Under coordinate permutations they form exactly these three disjoint orbits:

representative Z representative W orbit size positive input
3,5,6,15,23 8,16,25,26 30 A10_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json
3,5,6,15,23 8,25,26,28 20 A10_ORBIT2_REVIEW.json
15,23,27,29,30 1,2,4,8 5 final-orbit forest/rank theorem

The first theorem uses two forced closed matching sets with an odd intersection. The second uses one forced closed set and a complete canonical family with independently checked positive cycles. The third uses legal short-complement forests whose endpoint-pairing rows have full rank in the matching connectivity matrix. Each theorem quantifies over every arbitrary matching on the complement of its marked hole set.

Choose a coordinate permutation taking the normalized instance to its listed representative. Apply the relevant orbit theorem and invert the permutation and translation. This preserves each required edge, shortness of every new edge, simplicity, and the exact omitted vertex. The augmentation case and the three orbits exhaust all inputs, so the stated full A10 theorem follows once the listed inputs are accepted.

Consequences of accepted full A10

Together with full A8, A10 discharges the two assumptions of Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION.md, whose reduction and finite neighbor bound were independently accepted in Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json. Consequently every feasible Q5 imbalance-two avoid-one input holds; every arbitrary K(Q5) matching with balanced holes has a spanning path from any free root to every opposite-parity target, covered or free, and a spanning cycle extension. All surviving new edges are short. The zero-hole cycle case is the explicit perfect-matching import, and the 32-hole endpoint case has no covered target, as checked in that reduction. No infeasible 17-hole parity class is used.

These are Q5 auxiliary results. They do not by themselves discharge the marked multiple-omission inputs in Q6. Complete ten-hole covered targets, the complete 12/14/16/18-hole layers, and full P6 remain open.

Required final audit

Verify all upstream final reviews and source hashes, the last-orbit forest and rank certificates and the precise published rank theorem, the exact disjoint 30+20+5 geometry cover, the augmentation and symmetry steps, and the hypotheses of the already audited Q5 consequence theorem. The complete Q6 goal must remain open in the resulting state.

A8 consequences: full balanced-eight-hole endpoints and ten-hole progress

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Acceptance requires complete A8 final PASS and a separate review of these consequences. Full ten-hole P6 remains open.

1. Exact endpoint theorem

Let F be any matching of K(Q5) with four holes of each parity. For every free root r and every opposite-parity vertex y, covered or free, there is a Hamilton r-y path containing F, with all edges outside F short.

If y is free, add the auxiliary edge ry. The resulting matching has three holes of each parity. The already accepted K6 full-cycle theorem applies even when ry is long, since its required matching edges are arbitrary. Delete ry from that cycle to obtain the desired path.

If y is covered, put h=F(y) and F'=F-yh+hr. Its holes are the old holes minus r plus y, with counts3:5 and y a majority hole. Complete A8 gives a cycle on exactly Q5-y containing F'. Delete hr and append the original edge hy at h. This is a Hamilton r-y path restoring all original edges. The auxiliary edge hr disappears and all other new edges are short.

This theorem includes every possible mate h and every arbitrary complete- graph matching, so it is suitable for the long edges created by Q6 path compression. It fills the prescribed-covered-target part that K8 alone did not supply. Taking y to be a short neighbor of r and closing the path also gives a full cycle; K8 had already been independently established.

2. Six unconditional ten-hole cut rows

For a Q6 short27-edge matching, free root u=0 and covered odd target v, use Z,W,A,B,a,b from TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_A8_TRANSFER.md. After the standard short augmentation, Z union W is independent. The six rows

(0,1),(1,1),(0,2),(3,4),(4,4),(3,5)

are now sufficient without any additional local marked-geometry test. The first row uses K8, the next two use complete A8 at the bridge mirror, and the final three use the full balanced-eight-hole endpoint theorem above. All completion, root selection, optional bridge, tagged closure, conflict suppression and expansion steps are exactly those already audited in TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW. The only former additional hypothesis was membership in the accepted partial A8 geometries; complete A8 removes that hypothesis for every marked geometry arising in these rows.

The existence of an admissible bridge source remains automatic where required: among two or five original odd holes at most one mirrors to the root, and v is covered so it is not one of those sources. Required matching edges are preserved, and both the free root and covered target remain the prescribed global endpoints.

3. Exact additional coverage obligation

The accepted TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW fixed the remaining covered- target domain at91225 normalized geometries (26880,29955,34390 for v=1,7,31). Its frozen independent residual files are the inputs here. For every record, test all six actual cuts for one of the six rows above. If such a cut exists, Section2 supplies a path for every matching realizing that geometry. Keep every other record unchanged as an open obligation.

The producer ten_covered_after_full_A8.py records every chosen row/cut and the exact remaining input bytes. Its predicted additional coverage is37003, leaving54222 (16920,17022,20280). These are complete hole-geometry counts, not numbers of sampled matchings. A separate independent enumeration and fixed-input hash check are required before accepting these exact counts.

4. What this does and does not establish

Complete A8 supplies a reusable local endpoint theorem and expands the accepted ten-hole covered-target domain. The remaining54222 geometric cases, once independently confirmed, still need universal matching proofs. Multiple-omission local cycle inputs and b=0 exposed-port cases are not automatically covered by A8. Full A10, complete12--18-hole Q6 layers and full P6 remain open. No claim of mathematical novelty is made here.

Exact theorem

Let F be any matching of K(Q5) whose holes have counts3 and5 in the two parity classes. For every specified majority-parity hole v there is a cycle on exactly Q5 minus {v}, containing F, with all edges outside F short. The required matching may contain arbitrary long and same-parity edges.

Two remaining auxiliary levels suffice for all balanced Q5 endpoints

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Conditional reduction, not a proof of A8, A10, or full P6. Independent review pending.

Claim and notation

For t≥1, let A2t mean: every matching of K(Q5) with hole counts (t−1,t+1) has a cycle on precisely Q5−v for every specified majority hole v, containing the matching and using only short new edges. Either global parity can be the majority. Full A2,A4,A6 are established imports. The exact additional obligations are A8 (hole counts 3,5) and A10 (hole counts 4,6), with arbitrary required edges and arbitrary majority v.

If A8 and A10 hold, then:

  1. Every feasible A2t holds, with any number of holes.
  2. Every matching of K(Q5) with balanced holes has a Hamilton path from any free root to any opposite-parity target, covered or free, containing the matching and using only short new edges.
  3. Every matching of K(Q5) with balanced holes has a Hamilton cycle extension using only short new edges.

These are conditional auxiliary consequences, not assertions that the remaining Q6 cut configurations all reduce to these local inputs.

1. Finite geometric fact

Every set of five vertices of one parity in Q5 has at least eleven neighbors. Hence every five vertices of one parity and every six vertices of the other parity contain a short edge between the sets.

The first statement is a finite assertion on (165)=4368 sets for one parity. q5_higher_hole_reduction_geometry.py enumerates those sets, unions the five coordinate neighbors of each vertex, and records the full histogram. Its minimum is eleven; translation by a coordinate unit supplies the other parity. An independent checker must re-enumerate this small universe before treating the fact as accepted evidence.

2. Reduction of every larger avoid-one input

Suppose t≥6 in an A2t instance. There are at least five minority holes and at least six majority holes other than v. Section 1 gives a short edge between these sets. Add it to the matching; v stays free, and both hole counts decrease by one. Repeat until t≤5. The terminal instance is covered by A2/A4/A6/A8/A10. Its cycle contains the original matching, omits precisely v, and every added matching edge was short. Thus it has the required scope relative to the original instance.

3. Balanced endpoints and cycles

Let Pm be the endpoint assertion for m holes of each parity, and let Cm be the corresponding full-cycle assertion. Fink's arbitrary perfect- matching extension theorem supplies C0.

Inductively assume Cm−1. For Pm, let r be a free root and y an opposite-parity target. If y is free, add the possibly long auxiliary edge ry; apply Cm−1 to this arbitrary complete-graph matching, then delete ry. All surviving new edges are short.

If y is covered, write h=F(y) and set

F′=(F⧵{yh})∪{hr}.

Its holes have counts (m−1,m+1), with the majority parity that of y; y is now free. Apply A2m from Section 2, avoiding y. In the resulting 31-cycle replace the required auxiliary edge hr by h−y−r and delete the temporary edge yr. This yields a Hamilton r--y path, restores the original edge yh, and removes the only new auxiliary edge. Thus Pm holds.

To obtain Cm, take any free root and any short neighbor as target in Pm, then close that Hamilton path by the short edge between its ends. This closes the induction. For m=16 the matching is empty, so the covered-target branch (which would call the infeasible A32) never occurs; the free-target branch uses C15. All other covered-target calls have feasible majority counts at most sixteen.

4. Exact new geometry sizes, not matching counts

Normalize the forbidden majority vertex to 0. For A8, the other majority holes are four even vertices Z and the minority holes are three odd vertices W. For A10 the corresponding sizes are five and four. If a short Z-W edge exists, add it to reduce to the predecessor A theorem without covering 0.

The producer's complete nonadjacent domains have 2700 A8 geometries and 55 A10 geometries. No such domain remains for A12 or larger; the geometric fact above supplies an analytic explanation for all larger feasible sizes. These are marked hole configurations, not matchings. Each unresolved configuration must still be proved for every arbitrary complete-graph matching on its covered vertices. The separate A8 writer is investigating the 160 geometries without a delta-1/2/3 cut; those transfers and that residual classification are not imported as proved by this document.

Status

The implications above are PROVABLE AFTER EXTRA ASSUMPTIONS A8 and A10, and acceptance of the explicitly finite five-neighbor fact. A8 and A10 remain open. None of the complete 10--18-hole Q6 layers is closed here.

Q5 balanced eight-hole cycle extension

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Complete proposed proof relative to the listed imports and finite geometry witnesses; independent review pending.

Exact claim

Every matching F of K(Q5) with exactly four even and four odd holes has a Hamilton cycle containing F, all of whose edges outside F are short. Required matching edges may be long or join equal parities. Call this assertion K8. It is not the full balanced-eight-hole endpoint theorem and not the full A8 avoid-one theorem.

Dependencies
  1. Full Q5 balanced-six-hole cycle extension K6, accepted with A6 in A6_AND_EIGHT_FREE_CLOSED.md and its cited independent reviews.
  2. Only the delta-1/2/3 branches of Q5 A8 from A8_PARTIAL_PROOF_PACKAGE.md, which require independent acceptance. No unresolved A8 orbit, A10, or higher-hole P6 theorem is used.
  3. The finite geometric assertion and positive witnesses below, generated by q5_k8_geometry.py; a separate independent check is required.
Proof

If two holes are short-adjacent, add their edge. The new matching has three holes of each parity and K6 supplies the full cycle. The added edge was short, so this is also an allowed extension of F. Thus assume all eight holes are independent. Write their parity classes as E and O.

The following finite assertion holds: for every independent set with four holes of each parity, there is a free vertex r and a short neighbor y such that, after replacing hole r by y, the new 3:5-hole geometry has a coordinate cut containing y with majority-minus-minority count 1, 2, or 3. Here y is necessarily covered by F, since the holes are independent. The majority class is the parity of y, and y is its prescribed omitted hole.

Choose such r,y and write h=F(y). The four vertices r,y,h and the other holes have the required distinctness: r is free and h,y are covered. Set

F′=(F⧵{yh})∪{hr}.

This is an arbitrary complete-graph matching whose holes are precisely the old holes minus r plus y. The selected delta-1/2/3 branch of A8 gives a cycle on exactly Q5−y containing F', with short new edges. Replace its required edge hr by the two-edge path h-y-r. The original edge hy is restored and yr is short. This is a Hamilton cycle containing F; the auxiliary edge hr disappears. Its construction works for every matching on the specified covered support, independently of the value of h. This proves K8, subject to acceptance of the finite assertion.

Finite assertion: explicit complete universe

Enumerate each of the (164) even hole sets E. List all odd vertices nonadjacent to E, and enumerate all four-element subsets O. This produces exactly 980 independent balanced-eight-hole geometries, without symmetry reduction. For each, enumerate the eight choices of r and its five coordinate neighbors y. For each pair compute the five cut imbalances of the marked 3:5-hole set (E∪O⧵{r})∪{y}, always taking the face containing y. A pair is successful if some imbalance is 1,2,3.

All 980 geometries have a successful pair. The exact histogram of successful (r,y) pairs is 580 geometries with 40, 320 with 18, and 80 with 24. q5_k8_geometry.json records each input and one actual r,y, coordinate, and imbalance witness. A verifier need only rebuild the complete finite domain and check each witness with the stated formulas; it need not search for Hamilton cycles or inspect matching instances.

Limits

K8 supplies a cycle with freely selected construction endpoints. It does not supply a path to an arbitrary prescribed covered endpoint: that would require handling the corresponding fixed A8 geometry, which may be open. No full ten-hole covered-target or other full P6 conclusion is asserted.

Proof Package: Q5 free-neighbor abundance and EP0

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. New proof package; previously audited files and global coverage state are unchanged. Independent semantic/finite audit is pending.

Claims

Q5 neighbor abundance. Let M be an arbitrary complete-graph matching on V(Q5) with exactly two distinct holes q,v of equal parity. Let U(M;q,v) consist of the short neighbors a of q for which there is a simple cycle on V(Q5)⧵{v} containing M and the edge qa, with every edge outside M short. Then

|U(M;q,v)|≥3.

Since q is a hole, every incident cycle edge is new and short.

EP0 consequence. In an (a,b)=(2,0) eight-hole cut as defined in EIGHT_HOLE_COVERED_NEXT_DRAFT.md, suppose there is an odd original crossing port q≠v with

|NA(q)∩S|≥3,S={w¯:w∈W}.

Then EP0 holds at that cut. The original Q6 matching is short; the auxiliary complete-graph matching need not be short or bipartite.

Status

PROVABLE AS STATED, subject to the explicit finite inputs and existing imported theorems below passing their independent audit. A complete mathematical reduction and positive finite certificates are supplied. The new sixty-million-pair finite check currently has a complete producer result; independent fresh-context verification is in progress. This document alone does not assert an unconditional final eight-hole or P6 theorem.

Assumptions and notation

A short edge differs in one bit. All required matching edges in the Q5 abundance theorem may have arbitrary lengths or parity. A free vertex is not incident to a required matching edge. Coordinate cuts have mirror pairs with the same remaining local labels.

For a Q4 matching F with free vertex0 and omitted equal-parity vertex h, let P(F) be the family of unordered neighbor pairs at0 occurring in its valid fifteen-cycles. For a complete perfect matching P on Q4, let G(P) consist of unit vertices a∈{1,2,4,8} for which a Hamilton cycle containing P uses 0a as a new edge. An edge of P itself is excluded from this optional-edge set.

Dependencies
  1. Q4 free-neighbor classification below: |⋃P(F)|≥3 for either possible equal-parity hole distance.
  2. The existing Q4 perfect-matching extension theorem, allowing arbitrary complete-graph matchings and only short new edges.
  3. Q4_PERFECT_ENDPOINT_ABUNDANCE.md and its checked full minimal-endpoint-set classification: |G(P)|≥2 for every Q4 perfect matching. A Hamilton 0--a path containing P is equivalent to a Hamilton cycle containing P with optional edge 0a, by closing/deleting that short edge. The path cannot contain its own endpoint edge 0a on sixteen vertices.
  4. The audited complete opposite-hole Q4 fourteen-cycle tables, used to describe exact unavailable optional edges of a perfect matching.
  5. The finite star-input mask check described in Step4.
Proof of Q5 abundance
Step1. The complete Q4 neighbor-pair data

Normalize free vertex q to0. Its distinct equal-parity omitted vertex can be normalized to3 or15 by coordinate permutation. For either geometry, every one of the 135135=13!! arbitrary matchings on the other fourteen vertices is included.

The exact neighbor-union histograms are:

Omitted vertex Matchings with union size3 Matchings with union size4
3 208 134927
15 212 134923

These are independently obtained in two ways. eight_ep0_q4_neighbor_inverse.py contracts a required optional edge 0s through the original edge st, obtaining a fourteen-cycle matching with holes h,s. Each audited negative matching has the unique inverse obtained by replacing its edge 0t with st. No matching is unavailable at two different unit neighbors. Outside the complete negative inverse sets, the positive fourteen-cycle expands through 0−s−t to give a fifteen-cycle.

verify_eight_ep0_q4_neighbor_spectrum.cpp independently enumerates all input matchings and every possible short degree completion: degree two at0, zero at the omitted vertex, one at all other vertices. It rejects repeated required edges, checks exact cycle support and connectivity, and accumulates every available neighbor. There are116 degree patterns for omitted3 and96 for omitted15. The exact histograms coincide and the checker reports PASS.

For omitted15, the fuller pair-family classification in eight_ep0_q4_pair_spectrum.json shows precisely444 matchings for which

⋂B∈P(F)B≠∅.

The intersection is a single center a; two mandatory neighbors would contradict the union lower bound. For each center a∈{1,2,4,8} there are111 such matchings. These are the star matchings. The remaining134691 matchings have empty pair intersection.

eight_ep0_q4_star_A_prepare.cpp supplies every star matching, its center, all its positive fifteen-cycle witnesses, and the union UA(F) of optional short edges in those cycles that are not incident to0. The files are eight_ep0_q4_star_A.jsonl and eight_ep0_q4_star_A.bin. No required matching edge is included in this union.

Step2. A positive-crossing cut of Q5

Choose a coordinate on which q,v agree. Let A contain both holes and B be its opposite Q4 face. The crossing count c is even. Suppose c>0.

Pair all A crossing ports arbitrarily into an artificial matching D. Together with MA this is a Q4 matching with holes q,v. Step1 supplies fifteen-cycles whose optional neighbors at q have union size at least three.

For any one of these cycles, delete D, attach every original crossing, and compress the resulting A path forest to edges on the distinct B ports. There is no closed component: deletion of the nonempty D breaks the original A cycle into paths, and crossing attachments have distinct leaves. Join the compressed edges to MB to form a perfect matching on B. The Q4 perfect-matching extension theorem gives a Hamilton B cycle; expansion restores the entire A face except v and produces a thirty-one-cycle containing the original M.

No edge at q was deleted, since q is a hole and is in no edge of D. Therefore each of the at-least-three A neighbor options survives in a Q5 cycle, possibly with a different B completion. This proves the abundance bound whenever such a positive-crossing common-coordinate cut exists.

Step3. Zero crossings when d(q,v)=2

There are three coordinates on which q,v agree. If any has positive crossings, Step2 applies. Otherwise each of the three common-coordinate cuts has zero crossings.

For any one of these cuts, choose an A fifteen-cycle and a B Hamilton cycle both having the same optional short edge qa in their common local labels. Such an edge exists: Step1 gives at least three available A unit neighbors; Dependency3 gives at least two B unit neighbors among the same four units, so the two sets intersect.

Delete the two copies of qa and add the two mirror bridges at q,a. The two opened disjoint cycles become one thirty-one-cycle on exactly Q5−v, retain every original matching edge, and use only short new edges. Its neighbor at q across this cut is the vertical mirror of q. Repeating this existential construction at each of the three zero-crossing common-coordinate cuts yields three distinct vertical neighbors of q. The cycles need not be the same. This proves the abundance bound for distance2.

Step4. Zero crossings when d(q,v)=4

There is exactly one common-coordinate cut. If it has positive crossings, use Step2. Otherwise A contains a Q4 matching F with holes q,v, and B a Q4 perfect matching P. Normalize common local labels to q=0,v=15.

Let F=P(F) and G=G(P). Splicing A and B at an optional edge 0a with a∈G preserves the other A neighbor b from the pair {a,b}∈F and adds the vertical neighbor of0. Thus every vertex in

T={b: some a∈G satisfies {a,b}∈F}

is a realizable nonvertical Q5 neighbor.

Here |G|≥2 and |⋃F|≥3. If T had size one, say T={b}, then b∉G: any edge of F entirely in G would put both its endpoints in T. Every family edge incident to G must contain b. At most two vertices lie outside G, so any family edge disjoint from G must also contain b. Hence every edge of F contains b. Therefore F has a mandatory center outside G.

It follows that |T|≥2 unless F is one of the444 star matchings and its center a is unavailable in P. In all nonexceptional cases the two nonvertical neighbors in T and the vertical neighbor give the desired bound.

For the exceptional pairs, use a non-q optional edge. If

UA(F)∩UB(P)≠∅,

where UB(P) is the exact union of optional short edges over B Hamilton cycles, select one common edge, choose its witnessing A and B cycles, and splice at that edge. Since the edge is not incident to q, the resulting Q5 cycle retains both distinct A neighbors of q. Separately the q-edge splice already supplies a cycle containing the vertical q neighbor. This again yields at least three Q5 neighbor options.

The displayed intersection holds for every exceptional F,P pair, by the following complete finite certificate.

Exact exceptional P universe. For a fixed unit center a, P is unavailable at optional edge 0a in exactly two disjoint cases. First, P contains 0a, giving 135135=13!! matchings. Second, P(0)≠a and its Hamilton 0--a path contraction is one of the51 audited negative fourteen-cycle matchings on holes0,a. For each negative T, choose an edge bc and either endpoint assignment, then replace it by 0b,ac. These give714 distinct nonmatching-edge obstructions. This follows from the exact endpoint-path contraction and its unique inverse; hence all135849 exceptional perfect matchings are included.

Exact UB masks. For each of the32 Q4 short edges, perform the same negative inverse construction. eight_ep0_q4_PB_bad_optional.py produces16816 distinct perfect matchings with22848 labeled unavailable nonmatching optional edges. For any P, an optional short edge is unavailable precisely when it is an edge of P or appears in this inverse dictionary. Thus its exact positive union mask is the complement, among the32 short edges, of those two bad masks.

Complete pair comparison. eight_ep0_q4_star_joint.cpp reads all444 star F inputs. For each center it enumerates all135135 P containing the center edge and all714 additional inverse obstructions. For each of the111 star F with that center, it tests the two short-edge union masks. All

4·111·135849=60316956

pairs have a nonempty common non-q optional edge; there are zero residual pairs. The producer's result is eight_ep0_q4_star_joint.json, with the positive A cycles stored separately for checking. This finite mask comparison completes the distance4 zero-crossing case.

Distinct equal-parity vertices in Q5 have distance2 or4. Steps2--4 exhaust all cuts and both distances, proving Q5 neighbor abundance.

Deriving EP0

Fix the original eight-hole matching and a cut satisfying the second claim. Set r=0 if the root lies in A, otherwise choose either of the two nonroot even holes in A. Choose any perfect matching D on the EP0 completion domain

(XA⧵{q})∪((Z∩A)⧵{r}).

This domain has even cardinality, and its vertices are disjoint from the internal matching MA. The completed matching L=MA∪D has exactly holes r,q. The covered target v≠q has the same parity as q; let t=L(v).

Define

K=L−{vt}+{rt}.

The four vertices r,q,v,t are distinct. K is a matching with holes v,q of the same parity, so Q5 abundance applies. At least three neighbors of q occur on its valid thirty-one-cycles omitting v. Since |NA(q)∩S|≥3 and q has five neighbors, at least one of these cycles C has an edge qs with s∈S.

C contains the required artificial edge rt. Replace rt by r−v−t and delete rv. The result is a Hamilton r--v path on A containing every edge of L. The original edge vt is restored and the artificial edge rt is gone. The inserted edge rv is deleted, so its length is immaterial. All surviving new edges are short.

The edge qs is unchanged: q is a hole of K, and differs from r,v,t. This remains true if s equals r or t. Therefore this path, together with the chosen q,D,s, satisfies exactly the quantified EP0 obligation. No prescribed-edge strengthening of the imported N10 theorem is assumed. Instead that strengthening is derived from the proved abundance theorem.

Additional local facts and limits

The separate endpoint-path lemma in eight_ep0_endpoint_path_probe.py is valid but closes no additional representative by itself: if the only non-S q neighbors are r,a and the chosen completion contains av, avoiding qS forces the entire Hamilton path to be the four-vertex path r−q−a−v, a contradiction. Adding these clauses still leaves realizing matchings for the five previously open orbits. Such matching witnesses refute only that sufficient rule, not EP0.

The maximal-short-matching reduction and its exploratory counts are recorded separately; they are not needed for this proof. The abundance proof uses only the finite Q4 inputs and Q5 constructions above.

Open risks and audit boundary
  • A fresh checker must verify the444 star-input list, positive optional unions, complete negative PB inverse dictionary, and all60316956 mask comparisons; semantic review must verify Steps2--4 and the EP0 conversion.
  • Q6 geometry must separately establish that a suitable cut and q with three S neighbors always exist. eight_ep0_three_neighbor_geometry.json is the root agent's separate geometry input, not assumed silently here.
  • The final Q6 path transfer still needs its corresponding T15 cores and the existing audited two-bridge proof.
  • This file does not update any global coverage ledger or claim a final eight-hole theorem independently of those remaining imports and audits.

Short-forest and rank proof

Fix one row. Put H={0} union its majority set, U=the two marked omissions, and K=Q5-H. Thus K has26 vertices and H-U has4 included holes. A selected forest S has short edges only, omission of U, degree1 at every vertex of K and degree2 at H-U, and is acyclic. It therefore consists of13 paths, has17 edges, and has endpoint set precisely K. P(S) pairs its path ends. For any original matching F on K, a connected labelled alternating 26-cycle F+P(S) expands to a single simple30-cycle on Q5-U. A shared F/P pair would be an isolated labelled2-cycle, impossible in a connected 26-cycle, so no length-one forest path duplicates an original edge. Every surviving new edge lies in S and is short.

The imported generic matching-connectivity theorem is rank_GF(2)(H_26)<=2^(26/2-1)=4096. H_26 is indexed by ALL perfect matchings of the complete graph on K, with entry1 exactly for one labelled alternating cycle. Corollary3.5 of Cygan--Kratsch--Nederlof, Fast Hamiltonicity checking via bases of perfect matchings, supplies the upper bound for every even endpoint count. Primary version and statement alignment are recorded in A10_ORBIT3_UNIVERSAL_PRIMARY_SOURCE.md. Only this generic upper bound is imported; no bipartiteness restriction on required matchings or experimental rank extrapolation is used.

For each registry row the supplied4096 forest pairings restricted to the supplied4096 valid complete-graph matching columns have full GF(2) rank. Their complete rows of H_26 are consequently independent and span its entire row space. Every fixed matching F has a nonzero column: if its 13 edges are(a_i,b_i), pair b_i to a_(i+1) cyclically. This gives another perfect matching connecting with F. If all selected rows vanished at F, their entire span and hence every row would vanish there, contradiction. At least one selected forest connects with every F; expand it as above. This proves the exact universal matching theorem for the registry row. The argument applies independently to all15 rows.

No enumeration of every original matching is needed. A deficient or capped forest search would be OPEN rather than a counterexample. All15 searches reached rank4096 without a cap or deficient termination.

Assumptions, notation and dependency map

Import only the generic binary matching-connectivity matrix bound rank(H2n)≤2n−1 from the primary theorem identified in A10_ORBIT3_UNIVERSAL_PRIMARY_SOURCE.md. An admissible forest has degree zero at U, one at all 24 terminals in K, and two at the five included holes. It has 17 short edges and 12 path components. Its endpoint pairing is denoted P.

Proof
1. Full-rank unforced rows

Each selected forest is verified directly as a graph and compressed to its actual terminal matching P. For each of the ten unforced rows the saved 2048 forest pairings and matching columns have connectivity rank 2048 over F2. The imported upper bound makes those complete rows span the whole matching-connectivity row space. Every column indexed by an arbitrary original matching F is nonzero: cyclically connect consecutive required edges to construct another arbitrary matching whose union with F is one alternating cycle. Hence some selected forest pairing connects with F. Expanding the forest paths yields the required simple 29-cycle. Only stored legal forests are needed, not exhaustive forest enumeration.

Every actual union retains the two matching labels. A common pair would form an isolated two-edge component and cannot pass the single-cycle test. Thus no physical short edge duplicates a required edge on expansion.

2. Forced cherry and exact conditional classification

For a forced row all three omissions are short neighbors of 0. The two remaining neighbors are precisely p,q, and both are covered vertices: the four included majority holes are nonneighbors of 0. Every admissible forest must include p−0−q, so every P contains pq.

If the required matching contains pq, its three edges with this forced path make an isolated triangle. No spanning 29-cycle can have such a component. This proves necessity analytically, without a failed search.

Otherwise put a=F(p) and b=F(q). The four vertices are distinct. Suppress a−p−q−b in the labeled graph F+P: replace pa,qb in F by ab and remove pq from P. The resulting perfect matchings F′,P′ are on K⧵{p,q} and have a single alternating cycle exactly when F+P does. This is path suppression, valid even for long or same-parity original edges.

For each of the seven forced rows, the saved 1024 shortened forest pairings P′ have rank 1024 against supplied arbitrary matching columns on those 22 endpoints. The generic upper bound and the same nonzero-column argument give some connecting P′ for every F′. Use its associated full forest S and expand the suppressed path to recover all original edges, p,q and the included minority hole 0. The result is the required 29-cycle. Thus absence of pq is sufficient as well as necessary.

3. Exact certificate formats and verification

Unforced prefixes are Q5_T17_RANK_batch_XX, forced prefixes are Q5_T17_RANK_forced_XX. Every config contains the eight holes and three omissions; forced configs additionally append p,q.

For an unforced prefix, _forests.bin has 2048 records of 34 bytes, _pairs.bin and _columns.bin have 2048 records of 24 bytes, and the matrix/pivot/combination files each have 2048 rows of 256 bytes.

For a forced prefix, _forests.bin has 1024 records of 34 bytes; _full_pairs.bin has 1024 records of 24 bytes. Its corresponding _pairs.bin deletes the forced pair and has 1024 records of 22 bytes; _columns.bin also has 1024 records of 22 bytes. Its matrix/pivot/ combination files each have 1024 rows of 128 bytes. Bits in each row are stored least-significant-bit first. Pairs use actual Q5 labels.

The new reduced search preserves the full twenty-four endpoint degree constraints and full forest paths, checks that the compressed pairing contains the forced pair, and only then removes it for the rank matrix. It does not silently pretend p,q are omitted vertices of the forest.

These checks are producer evidence and need fresh independent acceptance.

The raw remaining files contain the exact unresolved records, without any matching-feasibility exclusion.

5. Forced Q6 completion avoidance remains a separate obligation

For the 1036 remaining records admitting forced projections, the witness file gives every supported projection and its actual B obstruction pair. The original internal short matching cannot contain that same-parity edge, but the compressed matching can acquire it through transferred paths and the global endpoint tag. Absence from the original B matching is therefore insufficient to apply the local conditional classification.

The obstruction pair may even contain the global root u=0 when it lies in B: tagged closure consumes that originally free vertex before local classification, so it is legitimately a local covered endpoint. The witnesses explicitly flag this boundary. No claim that both obstruction endpoints were originally covered is made.

The companion Q5_T17_RANK_ROOT_NOT_OB_TRANSFER.md proves how to choose D whenever the global root is outside the obstruction pair, including a target that is a crossing port. A concrete safe choice exists for all 1036 forced-only records and is retained in Q5_T17_RANK_forced_safe_witnesses.json. That new universal lemma and its finite application require fresh review together with these local inputs. Root-in-obstruction templates are not used or declared positive.

Corrections, scope and open risks

All seventeen local theorem statements retain arbitrary required edges. Their classifications and positive certificates are proposed complete local inputs, subject to independent review and the explicit primary rank bound. The unforced union is a proposed sufficient global class. Root-in-obstruction transfer templates, the 462 records without any T17 projection, and full P6 are outside this package; the safe companion transfer is a separate proposed proof submitted with it. Failed or capped searches are never used as nonexistence claims. Previously frozen first-case files remain unchanged.

Q5_T17_RANK_ROOT_NOT_OB_TRANSFER.md — Forced T17 transfer when the global root is outside the obstruction pair

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：e6820a5928623fbe058a6c1a99312178acf15b6180e11eaa099cd57d70dd84c9。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_REVIEW.json, Q5_T17_RANK_BATCH_REVIEW.json, TEN_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json。

Forced T17 transfer when the global root is outside the obstruction pair

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer candidate; fresh independent review required.

Claim, imports and status

Let M be a short matching of Q6 with ten holes, free even root u, and covered odd target v. Write the other even holes as Z, the odd holes as W, and assume Z∪W independent. Choose a cut A,B with v∈A and (a,b)=(|Z∩A|,|W∩A|) equal to (3,1) or (0,4). Select a legal triple of bridge sources as in the uniform transfer. Suppose its actual B marked geometry is one of the seven forced T17 inputs in Q5_T17_RANK_BATCH_PROOF.md, with forced pair pq, and suppose u∉{p,q}. Then M has a Hamilton u--v extension.

PROVABLE AS STATED relative to the accepted uniform transfer, its balanced-two-hole local endpoint input, and the proposed independently checkable forced-T17 conditional classifications. The universal completion-avoidance proof below is new and requires fresh review. No root-in-obstruction claim is made.

Notation and dependency map

Let C be the original crossing matching with port sets XA,XB and c=|C|. Let MA,MB be the internal restrictions. Let S be the three selected A holes, and Y their short B mirrors. The final B input has one minority hole and seven majority holes, omitting exactly Y. The forced pair p,q consists of the two remaining short neighbors of the minority. In particular p,q have the same parity as Y, are outside Y, and are covered in the final B matching. The root exclusion and original independence also make them originally covered.

The proof uses the exact uniform completion and forest construction. It adds at most one prescribed edge to its artificial matching D. The local endpoint theorem allows every arbitrary D, including long same-parity edges. The forced local classification is used only after proving that the actual compressed matching avoids pq.

Proof
1. Legal roots, completions and a lower bound on deleted gaps

If c=0, use the already declared five-direction endpoint theorem on the original short matching and finish. Assume c>0 and let δ=1[u∈A].

For (a,b)=(3,1) all three members of Z∩A are sources. If δ=1, take r=u and pair XA∪S. Here c is odd and d=|D|=(c+3)/2≥2. If δ=0, choose any r∈S and pair XA∪(S⧵{r}). Here c is positive even and d=(c+2)/2≥2. No even crossing port is needed in this case.

For (a,b)=(0,4) choose any three members of W∩A excluding the mirror of u. This is possible because the target is covered and at most one of the four hole sources is excluded. If δ=1, take r=u and pair XA∪S, again with positive odd c and d=(c+3)/2≥2. If δ=0, the original even-port surplus is b−a=4. Choose an even port r and pair (XA⧵{r})∪S. Then c≥4 is even and d=(c+2)/2≥3.

In every case MA+D has one even and one odd hole, with r even/free. The prescribed target v remains a legal covered odd target. The local endpoint theorem supplies a Hamilton r--v path PA containing all of MA+D, with only short new edges.

2. Suppression cannot create the obstruction through a bridge mate

Every y∈Y is originally internally matched in B: its mirror source was free, independence excludes an original opposite hole, and source selection excludes the B root. Write hy=MB(y). Since MB is short, hy has parity opposite to Y. The vertices hy are distinct and are not B ports, original holes, the free root, or members of Y.

After tagging and transferring the A forest, its matching T has endpoint set XB∪Y and additionally u when u∈B. Its only overlaps with MB are the vertices Y. Suppression extends an endpoint at y to the pendant mate hy, or replaces a transferred Y--Y path by a path between its two pendant mates. All these mates have parity opposite to p,q. Also pq∉MB because its endpoints have the same parity and every original B matching edge is short.

We claim that the final matching L can contain pq only if both p,q∈XB and pq∈T before suppression. If, for example, p is not a transferred endpoint, it retains its original B matching edge to a vertex of opposite parity. That mate is internally covered, cannot be a port or free root, and cannot be in Y by parity; this edge is an unchanged isolated component. It cannot end at q.

Since p,q are outside Y and the root, their being transferred endpoints therefore means they are ports. A transferred edge from a port to Y can only have its other endpoint changed by suppression to an opposite- parity hy, never to p or q. A transferred edge to the B root stays attached to that distinct root. Other port--port edges are unchanged. A Y--Y component has only opposite-parity pendant endpoints. These cases exhaust all components. Thus a newly compressed pq can arise only from the direct transferred pairing of those two ports, as claimed.

3. Prescribe a gap when both obstruction vertices are ports

If either obstruction vertex is not a B port, Step2 already proves pq∉L for any legal completion. Otherwise let p′,q′∈XA be their actual original crossing partners. Prescribe p′q′∈D.

This prescription is legal. In the even-source row, r is u or an original hole in S, hence never a port. In the odd-source row with u∈B, the B obstruction vertices are even, so their crossing partners p′,q′ are odd, whereas r was chosen even. In the other root-face cases r=u is originally free. Thus neither prescribed endpoint was excluded from the completion set. Both are distinct and disjoint from all source holes; the remaining even number of completion vertices can be paired arbitrarily. The local theorem allows this D.

4. The prescribed ports never become one transferred segment

First suppose u∈A. Add the tagged artificial edge uv to the local Hamilton path. This is one simple cycle on all A vertices; the tag was not already a path edge since a Hamilton path on thirty-two vertices cannot contain its endpoint edge. The matching D lies on this cycle. By Step1, at least two D edges are removed. The endpoints p′,q′ of the prescribed removed D edge lie in different remaining components: their direct arc was removed, and the other arc contains another removed D edge. Attaching original crossings and the short source bridges merely adds distinct B leaves to these components and cannot merge them. Hence their B leaves p,q cannot be paired by one transferred segment.

Now suppose u∈B. Start from the local simple r--v path and delete D, including its edge p′q′. Removing that edge from a path separates p′,q′ into different components; deleting other edges cannot rejoin them. Adding the tag uv only attaches the previously untouched B root as a leaf at v. Each original crossing and each bridge likewise attaches a distinct B vertex. No two A components are joined. This remains true in the even-source case r∈S: its short bridge attaches a new covered B leaf, rather than connecting two A components. Therefore p,q are again in different transferred segments.

The target-port boundary is included. If v is a crossing port and p′q′ is incident with v, deletion of D from the Hamilton path can isolate v. With u∈A, the tag remains at v and the tagged- cycle proof above applies without any exception. With u∈B, the tag and the original crossing give the segment u−v−v¯, where the original crossing partner is the actual B port. This segment has one endpoint u; since u∉{p,q}, it is not a p--q segment. The prescribed partner on the other side of the removed gap stays in a different A component. No claim that the deleted-edge forest lacks isolated A vertices is needed.

We have proved pq∉T. Step2 then proves pq∉L after all bridge conflicts are suppressed.

5. Apply the conditional local theorem and expand

The holes of L are exactly the actual one-minority/seven-majority marked geometry. The vertices p,q are covered and the omitted triple is Y. Its proposed rank classification applies because its sole obstruction edge was just excluded in the actual compressed matching. Its 29-cycle on B⧵Y expands to one global tagged cycle: the thirty-two A vertices and the three suppressed bridge mirrors restore the full sixty-four vertices. Every original edge of M survives. All artificial D and compressed edges disappear, and the other new edges are local short edges or chosen short bridges. Removing the tagged uv edge yields the prescribed Hamilton u--v path through M.

Scope and unproved boundaries

The root exclusion is essential to this proof. If the B obstruction is {u,v¯} and v is an original crossing port, tagging after deleting its D edge forces the transferred segment u−v−v¯. No choice of D removes that particular obstruction. Such a fixed-cut template failure is not a global P6 counterexample. It is not used in the application below, which chooses another actual safe projection.

The retained Q5_T17_RANK_forced_safe_witnesses.json gives a root-not-OB projection for every one of the 1036 forced-only records remaining after the unforced T17 union. This is a separate finite geometry assertion requiring fresh independent reconstruction. Combined acceptance of that assertion, this transfer and the seven conditional local classifications is required before any global class is promoted. Full P6 is not claimed.
