关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_CLOSURE_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json。

A4 蕴含六孔自由端点，从而蕴含全部六孔 P6

日期：2026-11-01。

Claim / Status

C6-free（条件性定理）。 假设五维 A4。对 Q6 的任意六孔短匹配 M 及任意两个指定异奇偶自由点 u,v，存在包含 M 的 Hamilton u—v 路径。

结合 SIX_HOLE_COVERED_REDUCTION.md 的 C6-covered，得到：A4 蕴含任意六孔短匹配的完整 P6 端点结论，目标可自由或已覆盖。

状态：PROVABLE AFTER EXTRA ASSUMPTION。A4 仍未证明；本文件不证明完整 P6，也不处理一般八孔及更多孔。

Assumptions / Dependency Map

平移后原自由点为 u,z,q 偶、v,w,t 奇，目标是自由奇点 v。若 z,q,v,w,t} 中有相邻对，加边后用已证 Z18，保持 u 自由。以下这五个非根孔无相邻对。

引用已审读的 N10、N14、Z18、五方向自由根定理，以及 SIX_HOLE_MIXED_AND_GEOMETRY.md 的条件性 K4。K4 是在 A4 假设下，K(Q5) 中恰有平衡四孔的任意匹配，具有自由根到任意异奇偶目标的 Hamilton 延拓。中间匹配的原长边允许保留，新增边必须短。

N10 的一个直接推论记为 NC：五维完整图匹配恰有两个异奇偶孔时，可扩为 Hamilton 圈。证明是从一孔到任一短邻点应用 N10，再加端点间短边；32点路径不含其端点之间的边。

本证明不调用 C6-covered。依赖顺序为 A4→K4，随后用 K4、N10/N14/NC 和 A4 构造 C6-free；最后才与 C6-covered 合并。

Proof
1. 统一切分与拼接约定

选任一使 zi≠qi 的坐标。含 v 的面为 A，另面为 B，交换 z,q 名字使 z∈A,q∈B。直接处理原短匹配 M，不收缩目标。记内部匹配 MA,MB，真实跨边 C，端口集 XA,XB，跨边数 c。

当 c=0，原匹配只用至多五方向，已有五方向定理立即给出原目标。因此下面在可能出现零跨边的情形中直接排除该分支。

下列构造先在 A 选择人工匹配 D，找包含 MA+D 的 Hamilton 路径 PA。若 u∈A，其端点为 u,v；若 u∈B，其端点为某个端口 a∈XA 与 v。每次 D 均不接触所选端点；当 u∈A，D 均非空。

删除 D，接回全部真实跨边；必要时再接一个短桥。所得为路径森林：所有接入的 B 顶点不同，因而不会形成圈或合并旧分量。

  • u∈A 时，有从 u 到 B 端点 r 的终端段及从另一个 B 端点 s 到 v 的终端段。两者不同，因为 D 非空。其余路径缩成匹配 R。
  • u∈B 时，有从某个 B 端点 r 到 v 的终端段，其余路径缩成 R。

因此，只需在 B 构造相应端点间、包含压缩匹配的路径，展开 R 后接终端段即可。所有 A 点出现在互不相交的转移段中恰一次，所有 B 点出现在该局部路径中恰一次；下面若临时遗漏一处冲突点 y，会明确展开恢复它。

若短桥在 B 的端点 y 被 MB 覆盖，只有当 y 也在 R 中时才有覆盖冲突。记 k=MB(y)、d=R(y)，用

FB=(MB−yk)∪(R−yd)∪{kd}.

此时 d 是非终端跨端口，故 k,d 不同，辅助 kd 与剩余匹配无覆盖冲突。未来将 kd 展开为原边 ky 及对应 y—d 转移段，恰恢复 y 和这条被压缩的路径。其余 R 边逐一展开。此规则与 S9 的单冲突展开相同，但本文件逐分支列出实际孔集与所用定理。

2. A 内恰有两个原奇孔：v,w 在 A，t 在 B
2a. 根 u 在 A

A 原孔为 u,z 偶及 v,w 奇，B 原孔为 q 偶及 t 奇。c 为偶数；已排除零跨边，所以 c≥2。在 XA 上取任意配对 D。MA+D 保留平衡四孔，K4 给 Hamilton u—v 路径。删 D、接跨边，端口集为 XB，终端段给出不同 r,s∈XB，R 覆盖其余端口。

LB=MB+R 恰有孔 q,t,r,s。加入人工边 rs，只剩异奇偶孔 q,t；NC 给全 B 圈。删 rs 得 r—s 路径，展开 R 并接两终端段。r,s 不必异奇偶，因为 NC 的孔是 q,t。

2b. 根 u 在 B

A 原孔为 z 偶、v,w 奇，B 原孔为 u,q 偶、t 奇。短内部匹配保证 XA 的偶端口比奇端口多一，所以 c 为正奇数，可选偶端口 a。在 XA−{a} 上配对 D，可以为空。MA+D 恰有平衡四孔 z,a,v,w，K4 给 Hamilton a—v 路径。删 D、接跨边，得到终端段 r—v，R 覆盖 XB−{r}。

LB=MB+R 孔为 u,q,t,r。加入辅助 ur 后仅剩异奇偶孔 q,t；NC 给圈，删 ur 得 Hamilton u—r 路径。展开并接终端段。全部匹配边保留。

3. A 内只有原奇孔 v：w,t 均在 B

令 y=z⊕ei∈B。y 奇，不是 w,t，否则原非根孔相邻；不是偶根 u 或偶孔 q；它的跨面短邻点 z 自由，因此 y 必由 MB 内部覆盖。使用短桥 zy。

3a. 根 u 在 A

A 原孔为 u,z 偶、v 奇，B 原孔为 q 偶、w,t 奇。c 为正奇数。在 XA∪{z} 上任取配对 D。MA+D 恰有异奇偶双孔 u,v，N10 给 Hamilton u—v 路径。D 非空，删去后接跨边及 zy。B 端点集合为 XB∪{y}，其中不同的 r,s 属于两条终端段，R 覆盖其余点。

若 y∈{r,s}，令另一个终端点为 b∈XB。LB=MB+R 是匹配，孔为 q,w,t,b，y 被覆盖。记 k=LB(y)=MB(y)，构造 T=LB−yk+kb。其孔恰为 q 偶及 w,t,y 奇，不依赖 b 的奇偶。A4 避 y 给31圈。删 kb，接原边 ky，得到全 B 的 b—y 路径。按两终端段需要定向，展开 R 后连接。

若 y∉{r,s}，它在 R 中产生唯一冲突。依统一规则构造 FB，孔恰为 q,w,t,r,s,y。加入辅助 rs，剩孔为 q 偶及 w,t,y 奇。A4 避 y 给31圈；删 rs 得 B−y 的 r—s 路径。展开 kd 恢复 y 及相应转移段，其余 R 展开，再接终端段。

3b. 根 u 在 B

A 原孔为 z 偶、v 奇，B 原孔为 u,q 偶、w,t 奇。XA 奇偶端口数相等，c 为偶数；排除零跨边后，可取偶端口 a。在 (XA−{a})∪{z} 上配对 D，MA+D 恰漏 a,v。N10 给 Hamilton a—v 路径。删 D、接跨边和 zy，得到终端段 r—v，R 覆盖 (XB∪{y})−{r}。

若 r=y，LB=MB+R 恰有平衡四孔 u,q,w,t。K4 给自由偶根 u 到已覆盖奇点 y 的全 B 路径，展开后接终端段。

若 r∈XB，y 在 R 中，依统一规则构造 FB，孔为 u,q,w,t,r,y。加辅助 ur，仅剩 q 偶、w,t,y 奇。A4 避 y 给31圈，删 ur 得 B−y 的 u—r 路径。展开恢复 y，接终端段。

4. 三个原奇孔 v,w,t 全在 A

这是 S9 的同类切分，但目标现在自由，不能仅以旧定理标题作引用；以下列出所需改动和全部局部输入。

从 w,t 中选择一个（命名为 w）使 y=w⊕ei 被 MB 内部覆盖。y 不等于 q（非根孔不相邻）；若根在 B，至多一个候选等于 u；另一个候选内部覆盖。桥为 wy，y 偶且 y≠q。

若 u∈B，A 原孔为 z 偶及 v,w,t 奇，B 原孔为 u,q 偶。偶跨端口比奇跨端口多二，取偶端口 a，在 (XA−{a})∪{w} 配对 D。MA+D 的孔为 a,z 偶及 v,t 奇，K4 给 a—v 路径。删 D 接跨边和桥后，有终端段 r—v，R 覆盖其余 XB∪{y}。

  • 若 r=y，MB+R 恰有同偶孔 u,q，N10 给 u—y 路径。
  • 若 r∈XB，冲突修复后的 FB 孔为 u,q,r,y；加 ur，仅剩同偶 q,y。N14 避 y 给31圈，删 ur 得 u—r 路径，展开恢复 y。

若 u∈A，A 原孔为 u,z 偶及 v,w,t 奇，B 只有偶孔 q。c 正奇，在 XA∪{w} 配对非空 D。MA+D 平衡四孔为 u,z,v,t，K4 给 u—v 路径。删 D 接跨边和桥，得到终端段的不同 B 端点 r,s 及压缩匹配 R。

  • 若 y 是一个终端点，令另一个为 b。MB+R 恰漏 q,b，N10 从自由根 b 到与 q 同偶的 y 给全 B 路径。
  • 若 y 在 R 中，冲突修复后的 FB 孔为 q,y,r,s；加 rs，仅剩同偶 q,y。N14 避 y 给31圈，删 rs 得 r—s 路径，展开恢复 y。

每个子情形最后均展开所有人工边并连接终端段。自由目标 v 不在 D 中，所以此处无 S9 中跨端口目标孤立的边界；v 的最终度数恰为一。

5. 覆盖完整性

选定坐标分开两个非根偶孔后，另外两个奇孔 w,t 在目标面 A 中的数目只能是零、一、二，分别由第3、2、4节处理。每节又覆盖根在任一面、桥端点属于终端段或压缩匹配的全部情况。零跨边及原非根孔相邻的分支已先解决。因此 C6-free 成立。

与 C6-covered 合并，在 A4 假设下，六孔短匹配的任意自由根和任意异奇偶目标均有 Hamilton 延拓。这个合并没有证明 A4，亦没有覆盖更多孔。证毕。

SIX_HOLE_MIXED_AND_GEOMETRY.md — 六孔：新增异奇偶双孔侧转移与完整切分例外分类

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：9c4450060f472b54397a337c9d2128a26d31077b677c35b0a0669fb1d3022e68。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json, CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_A1B4_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json, EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_CLOSURE_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_COVERED_REVIEW.json, SIX_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json。

六孔：新增异奇偶双孔侧转移与完整切分例外分类

日期：2026-11-01。原目标是完整 P6；本文件不宣称完成。

Claim / Status
  • K4、S8、S7：PROVABLE AFTER EXTRA ASSUMPTION，唯一新增未证输入为 A4。
  • G6：PROVABLE AS STATED，是孔位置与目标位置的全称几何分类，不是路径存在性定理。
  • A4、E3、完整 P6：NOT CURRENTLY JUSTIFIED。

新增 S7。 假设 A4。对六孔短匹配 M⊆E(Q6)，自由偶根 u、已覆盖奇目标 v，记 h=M(v)，M*=M−vh+hu。若存在坐标切分，包含 v 的面恰含 M* 的一偶孔、一奇孔，则存在包含 M 的 Hamilton u—v 路径。不另外要求跨边数或该面不含半层。

G6 的应用形式。 结合原 S4 和新增 S7，任意六孔已覆盖目标输入：要么已可补到四孔；要么在 A4 假设下可解；要么经立方体自同构落入文末六行、共十二个“非根孔集合—目标”代表。根仍有至多30个偶点选择，原匹配仍任意。十二不是剩余匹配数，也不涵盖六孔自由目标、八孔及更多孔。

Assumptions / Notation

顶点为六位整数，短边表示距离一，p(x) 为位重量模二，ei=2i。允许中间匹配在完整图上，必须保留其指定长边直到明确展开或删除。

A4 是 SIX_HOLE_FOUR_AUX_REDUCTION.md 中的五维命题：完整图匹配恰有三同奇偶孔和一异奇偶孔时，可扩为遍历除任一指定多数奇偶孔外全部31点的圈，新增边短。A4 未证明。

已审读输入：N10（GENERAL_NEAR_PERFECT.md），N11/N12（AVOIDED_VERTEX_TRANSFER.md），E2（DISTANCE_TWO_ALL_TARGETS.md 的交叉面半层互斥引理），Z18（任意四孔短匹配），以及 Fink–Hotmar 五方向自由根端点定理。原 S4 的三种目标面孔数为 (1,2),(1,3),(0,3)，顺序是偶孔数、奇孔数。

本文件的新 K4 不是文献半层条件定理；它仅是 A4 的条件性推论。这里引用的 E2 不要与另一文件新命名的 E3 消辅助边义务混淆。

Dependency Map
  1. A4 + N10 → K4（五维完整图平衡四孔的全部自由根端点路径及圈）。
  2. K4 + N11 + N12 → S8（目标单孔侧、无半层、多跨边时的六孔转移）。
  3. A4 + S8 + N11/N12 + E2 + 五方向定理 → S7。
  4. 位数计数和四点简单图的三边分类 → G6。
  5. Z18 + S4 + S7 + G6 → 上述带 A4 假设的剩余几何范围。
Proof
K4：A4 蕴含平衡四孔完整图匹配的指定端点结论

设 F⊆K(Q5) 恰有两个偶孔、两个奇孔，a 为任一自由根，y 为任一异奇偶目标。原匹配边不要求短，也不要求二部。证明存在含 F 的 Hamilton a—y 路径，新增边短。平移后取 a 偶。

若 y 自由，向 F 加辅助边 ay，剩下两个孔异奇偶。N10 从其中一孔到任一短邻点给 Hamilton 路径，闭上端点间短边得到全32点圈，含 F+ay。删除 ay 即得所需路径。此处 N10 的目标与另一孔同奇偶，条件满足。

若 y 已覆盖，记 k=F(y)，构造 F′=F−yk+ka。四点配对合法：a 自由，k,y 覆盖且互异。孔变为另一个偶孔和三个奇孔（包括 y）。A4 给含 F′、避开 y 的31圈。删 ka，在 k 端接回原边 ky，得到含全部 F 的 Hamilton a—y 路径。ky 即使长也合法，因为它原属于 F；新辅助 ka 已删除。

再选择 y 为 a 的任一短邻点，即可将该路径闭成包含 F 的 Hamilton 圈。路径有32点，不可能已经包含两端间的边 ay。证毕。K4 全程依赖未证 A4。

通用预处理与候选桥接点

原六孔记为 u,z,q 偶及 w,s,t 奇。若 z,q,w,s,t} 内有相邻对，加该边后用 Z18，保持 u 自由，原目标完成。以下这五点无相邻对。换配 M*=M−vh+hu 的孔恰为 z,q,v,w,s,t，唯一可能的长边 hu 同偶。

对任意切分 A,B，记 C 为 M* 的真实跨边、XA,XB 为端口，c=|C|。若某些原奇孔在 B，其镜像 b=w⊕ei 在 A：它不等于 A 中的非根偶孔（否则原孔相邻），除可能为根 u 外原来都由 MA 内部覆盖，因为其跨面邻点 w 自由。换配只改变 u,h 的配对。若 u,h 同在 A，新边内部覆盖它们；若同在 B，无影响；若分居两面，至多一个候选变成跨端口。因此三个奇孔给出的三个不同候选中，至少两个由 MA* 内部覆盖。

S8：目标侧只有 v、无半层且至少三跨边

假设 A 的唯一孔是 v，MA* 无半层，c≥3。此时 B 的孔为 z,q 偶及 w,s,t 奇，c 为奇数。

选内部覆盖候选 b=w⊕ei，记 k=MA*(b)。F=MA*−bk 无半层，在 A−{v,b} 内的自由集为 Y=XA∪{k}，大小为偶数且至少四。N12 给配对 W 使 F+W 无半层。取 a=W(k)∈XA、D=W−ak，则 LA=MA*+D 恰漏 v,a，其 N11 压缩为 F+W。

N11 给覆盖 A−v 的 a—b 路径。删除 D 后所得路径族无孤立点，端点为 XA∪{b}；接真实跨边及短桥 bw，缩段得到匹配 R，覆盖 XB∪{w}。与 MB* 无覆盖冲突，故 LB=MB*+R 恰有平衡四孔 z,q,s,t。K4 给 B 的 Hamilton 圈。展开全部 R 得覆盖 Q6−v、包含 M* 的圈；删 hu、接回 hv，得到原目标路径。所有辅助边均展开或删除。证毕。

S7 第一阶段：一偶一奇孔侧的可用压缩

设 A 的孔为偶 z 与奇 v，B 的孔为偶 q 与奇 w,s,t。c 为偶数。取内部覆盖候选 b=w⊕ei，记 k=MA*(b)。

若 c≥2 且 F=MA*−bk 无半层，则在 A−{v,b} 中自由集为

Y=XA∪{z,k},|Y|=c+2≥4.

N12 给无半层补全 F+W。令 a=W(k)∈XA∪{z}，D=W−ak。N11 应用于 LA=MA*+D，给出覆盖 A−v 的 a—b 路径。删除 D 后端点集为 XA∪{z,b}，无孤立点：D 是不接触 a,b 的匹配。a=z 时同一公式成立。

接回真实跨边，并加入 bw 与 zy，其中 y=z⊕ei∈B。y 为奇点，不等于 w,s,t（预处理已排除相邻原孔），也不等于偶 u,h。它原由 MB 内部覆盖，换配后仍然内部覆盖。

缩段得到 R，覆盖集为 XB∪{w,y}，与 MB* 的唯一覆盖冲突是 y。记 r=MB*(y)、d=R(y)，其中 d∈XB∪{w}，与 y,r,q,s,t 不同。定义

LB=(MB*−yr)∪(R−yd)∪{rd}.

LB 是匹配，孔恰为 q,s,t,y，一偶三奇。A4 避开 y 给出31圈。将 rd 展开为原边 ry 及 y—d 转移段，其余 R 边全部展开，恢复 y 及全部 A−v。得到 Q6−v 圈，再删 hu 接 hv。若 hu 在真实跨边中，也作为原指定边随展开保留到最后删除。

同一构造还允许 c=0：只要某候选的 Tb=MA*−bk+zk 无半层，就直接使用 N11，取 a=z,D=∅。其余桥接、单冲突消除与 A4 恰如上述，所用 N11 全部条件仍成立；这里不调用要求四个自由点的 N12。

S7 第二阶段：所有不可用压缩归结为真实半层

有自由点 v，所以 MA* 至多包含一个半层：含半层的匹配全部短边只能用同一方向，而该方向两个半层会覆盖整个面。

若 c≥2：当 MA* 无半层时，任取内部覆盖候选进入第一阶段；当其唯一半层覆盖某个候选时，选该候选并删去匹配边，半层消失，同样进入第一阶段。因此未解决情形必有真实半层 H⊆MA*，避开 v,z 和全部三个候选镜像。

若 c=0：hu 只能内部位于 A 或 B。若在 A，则 u,h,v 均在 A，原 M 同样无该方向跨边；五方向自由根定理直接解决。

若 hu 在 B，则 MA*=MA 是短匹配，孔为 v,z。三个候选均由它内部覆盖，伙伴 kb 均奇，三条候选边两两不同。若一个 Tb=MA−bkb+zkb 无半层，第一阶段解决。否则每个 Tb 都含半层。

任取两个候选 b,e。Tb 中的半层至少有七条短边来自 MA；Te 至少保留其中六条，迫使两半层方向相同。它们都避开 v，故是同一个半层 H。对全部三候选重复这一比较，得到共同的 H，它避开每个 b，因为 b 是 Tb 的孔。

固定 b，在另一个 Te 中原边 bkb 保留；b 不在 H 端点集且 Te 是包含 H 的匹配，所以 kb 也不在 H 端点集。于是新增 zkb 不属于 H，从而 H⊆MA，并避开其孔 z,v。仍得到真实半层避开全部候选。

S7 第三阶段：换切分完成真实半层分支

设上述半层方向为 j≠i。其端点补集含奇 v 及偶 z,bw,bs,bt，故

zj=wj=sj=tj≠vj.

沿 j 重切，A′ 为含 v 的面。E2 保证 MA′* 无半层，旧 H 的八条边都成为新跨边。z,w,s,t 全在另一面，q 可在任一面。

  • 若 q∈A′，新目标面恰有一偶一奇孔，跨边至少八；直接用第一阶段无半层分支。
  • 若 q∉A′，新目标面只有 v，跨边为奇数且至少九；用 S8。

两个分支均已证明且不依赖当前 S7 的未完成部分，没有循环。因此 S7 成立，但仍以 A4 为条件。证毕。

G6：原 S4 切分不存在时的完整几何结构

预处理后 z,q,w,s,t} 无相邻对，z,q 偶且不同，W={w,s,t} 是三个不同奇点，v 奇且不在 W。

令 D 为 z,q 不同的坐标集。对任一 i∈D，目标面始终含恰一个偶孔。如果三个 W 点在此坐标不全相同，目标面奇孔数为二或三，属于 S4。因此没有 S4 切分时，三个 W 点在 D 的每个坐标都相同。

三个不同、同奇偶的点只在其余 6−|D| 个坐标变化。至少需要三个自由坐标，否则一个固定奇偶类最多含两个点。|D| 是正偶数，所以只能为二。特别地，若 d(z,q)≥4，必有 S4 切分。

平移 z 为零，置换坐标使 q=3，即 D={0,1}。三个 W 点的低两位相同，记为 r。若 r=3，将所有顶点异或3（同时交换两个偶孔的名字）；若 r=2，交换坐标0、1。因此可令 r=0 或1。

记 W 的高四位为三个不同四位向量。

  • r=0 时，高四位为奇重量。因不邻接偶孔0，重量一被排除，所以三个向量都重三。四坐标置换后唯一代表为 7,11,13。
  • r=1 时，高四位为偶重量。重量零会使该点邻接两个偶孔，故排除；可用向量是六个重量二向量及重量四向量15。若不含15，把重量二向量看成四点完全图的边：三条边构成三角形、三边星或四点路径，恰三类。若含15，另外两条边相邻或不相邻，恰两类。

这给出下面六种 W 代表。

对任一高位坐标 j≥2，两偶孔均为零：当 vj=0，目标面有两个偶孔，不属于 S4；当 vj=1，目标面有零偶孔，其奇孔数是 1+cj，其中 cj 是三个 W 点在该位的1个数。因此此坐标属于 S4 当且仅当 vj=1,cj=2。所以没有 S4 切分的充要条件为

vj=0对每一个 cj=2 的高位坐标。

再加入 S7 的 (1,1)：高位坐标不可能有一个偶孔；在低位坐标，若 vi≠ri，三个原奇孔均在目标对面，目标面奇孔数正好一。因此没有 S4 或 S7 切分，当且仅当上述条件成立并且 v 的低两位等于 r。同时要求 v 奇、v∉W。

逐列计算得到完整表。所有数都是六位整数编码；两非根偶孔固定为 0,3。

高四位类型 三个原奇孔 W 无 S4 的目标数 无 S4、S7 的目标 v
三个重量三向量 28,44,52 4 4
三角形 13,21,25 4 1
三边星 13,21,37 29 1,25,41,49,61
四点路径 13,25,49 8 1,37
15 加相邻两边 13,21,61 8 1,37
15 加不相邻两边 13,49,61 2 1

表中合计十二个代表。此处无需把目标和根再按各行稳定子去重，因此不主张它是不可约同构类的最小数目。根 u 可以是任一不同于 0,3 的偶点，至多30种；是否有给定孔集的短匹配不影响这个充分覆盖分类。除列出的类外，预处理、S4 或 S7 至少一个适用。证毕。

Verification and scope

six_hole_geometry_census.py 在平移 z=0 后逐一检查全部 1,198,860 个规定几何输入：31种非零偶 q，与 0,q 均不相邻的三个奇孔，以及不同于这些孔的奇目标。直接逐坐标统计孔数，与上述位条件及六行标准形逐项比较。

其中 1,188,480 个有 S4 切分；10,380 个没有。新增 S7 几何覆盖其中8,010个，余2,370个均落入上述十二代表。这里穷尽的只有明确的几何输入域，不是所有匹配，更不是所有 Hamilton 路径义务；S7 的路径结论仍依赖 A4。

Remaining obligations
  1. A4 / E3 本身仍未证明。
  2. 即使 A4 证明完成，表中十二个代表中的任意原短匹配、任意合规根仍须处理；已有其他充分条件可能覆盖其中部分，不能默认全部覆盖。
  3. 六孔自由目标及更多孔仍须处理，完整 P6 未证明。
T15_ALTERNATIVE_GROUP_PROGRESS.md — Proof Package: alternative T15 cores18,21,25

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：78dd90d869c30179c6dffc228ed20425b695137fe122a327dad98981da097f84。

Proof Package: alternative T15 cores18,21,25

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. New result only; no previously audited file or global state is modified.

Claim

For each row below, every arbitrary complete-graph matching F on V(Q5) whose holes are {0}∪O∪I extends to a simple cycle on V(Q5)⧵O, with every added edge short. The marked omitted pair is O. Cube-automorphic images and either global parity orientation are included.

Core O omitted I retained holes cut coordinate
18 {1,7} {11,14,28} 2
21 {1,7} {11,22,28} 2
25 {1,7} {14,26,28} 1
Status

PROVABLE AS STATED, relative to the previously imported Q4 N14 theorem and audited balanced Q4 tables. Every new finite input and every positive residual certificate described below has been checked by a separate implementation. Fresh-context semantic audit is pending. This package does not claim full T15 or eight-hole P6; parent coverage requires a separate geometry calculation.

Assumptions and notation

Original matching edges may have arbitrary length and parity. A short edge joins binary labels differing in one coordinate. Delete the cut coordinate and use common local Q4 labels on the one-face A and zero-face B. For core25 additionally send local bit positions (0,1,2,3) to (3,0,1,2) on both faces. The exact resulting geometry is independently verified in t15_alternative_small_verification.json.

Core A holes {x,r,s}, omit x B holes {0,7,y}, omit y negatives for bridges r,s
18 {3,6,12} {0,7,1} 2,1
21 {3,10,12} {0,7,1} 1,1
25 {9,3,6} {0,7,8} 10,10

Write FA,FB for the internal matchings, C for original crossing edges, XA,XB for their endpoint sets, and c=|C|. Both faces have thirteen originally covered vertices, so c is odd and 1≤c≤13. The crossing partner bijection is arbitrary throughout.

For a bridge label z∈{r,s}, let w be the other label. The imported balanced Q4 table concerns holes {0,7,y,z}, omits y,z, and classifies all 10395=11!! arbitrary required matchings on the other twelve vertices. The table has a positive explicit fourteen-cycle for every nonnegative entry. All table images used here are obtained by coordinate permutations preserving 0,7.

Proof strategy and dependency map
  1. Import Q4 N14 at its arbitrary complete-graph scope: two equal-parity holes allow a fifteen-cycle omitting either specified hole.
  2. Use N14 with an arbitrarily chosen artificial boundary pairing. Its output pairing must form one alternating cycle with the chosen pairing.
  3. For cores18/21 a single negative table entry for bridge12 makes every c≥5 input avoidable by a deliberately disconnected artificial pairing.
  4. For core25 transport the fully checked core23 B inverse-blocker certificate to bridges3,6; the A omitted label plays no role in that certificate.
  5. Exhaust all small-crossing B spectra, then verify every exceptional c=1 input by a direct positive cycle certificate.
Proof
Step1. The arbitrary boundary-pairing construction

Fix z∈{r,s}. For every perfect pairing D of E=XA∪{zA}, the matching FA∪D has exactly the equal-parity holes x,w. N14 gives a fifteen-cycle on A−x containing it. Delete D. The result is a spanning forest of paths inducing a pairing R of E. The multigraph R∪D is connected: contracting the remaining paths in the original cycle yields this alternating cycle. Every surviving edge outside FA is short.

Attach all original crossings and the short bridge zAzB.

If zB∉XB, it is internally matched to k=FB(z). The paths have distinct B endpoints in XB∪{zB} and cannot close a component. Add FB, suppress zB, and compress all paths. The resulting matching L has holes {0,7,y,z}. The map from R to L is injective: identify the mate q of the fixed internal vertex k in L, restore kz,zq, remove the other fixed edges of FB, and pull crossing labels back to A. Thus a table with b negatives forbids at most b possible output pairings R.

If zB∈XB and c≥3, let d=C−1(zB) and prescribe

D={zAd}∪D′,

where D′ is any pairing of XA⧵{d}. Because at least two edges of the original A cycle are deleted, zA and d are in different remaining path components. Adding the bridge joins these components through the crossing at d, with no closed component. Their resulting pairing on the remaining boundary is Q. Suppression of the distinguished edge zAd in the alternating cycle shows that Q∪D′ is connected. After transport to B, the compressed required matching is L=FB∪QB, with holes {0,7,y,z}. Again at most b output pairings are negative.

Whenever L is positive in its table, expand its required edges through the remembered disjoint paths. The fourteen-cycle restores fifteen A vertices and the suppressed B vertex z, hence becomes a thirty-cycle on exactly Q5−{xA,yB}. It contains all original internal and crossing edges. Only short A edges, short bridges, and short B cycle edges survive as added edges.

Step2. All large crossing counts for cores18 and21

Choose z=12, whose table has exactly one negative matching in either geometry. In the internal case there is at most one forbidden pairing R0. For c≥3, the boundary has c+1≥4 vertices. If a forbidden pairing exists, take D=R0. Then R0∪D is a union of at least two doubled matching edges, so is disconnected. The N14 output must be connected with D and therefore differs from R0. If there is no forbidden pairing, any D works.

In the occupied case, for c≥5 the remaining boundary has c−1≥4 vertices. If a forbidden Q0 exists, choose D′=Q0. The same disconnected-union argument forces the N14 output to differ from Q0. Thus bridge12 handles every c≥5 input, uniformly in the original matching and crossing bijection. The internal c=3 case is also handled here, but Step4 treats all c=3 cases together.

Step3. All large crossing counts for core25

The B geometry is {0,7,8} with bridges3,6. Swap local bits0 and1 in the already developed B geometry with bridges3,5. This permutation fixes 0,7,8,3 and sends5 to6. It sends the complete negative table families and every boundary pairing to the target families, preserving graph connectivity.

verify_t15_alternative_core25_blockers.py reruns the complete inverse-family and graph-connectivity check of r3_boundary_blocking_3_8.json into new output files, then independently checks this coordinate transport against the complete negative lists for both target bridges. It verifies2644 explicit blockers for bridge3, including complete reconstruction of every inverse family, and checks the mapped bridge6 families. No original audited file is rewritten.

The checked property is: for every fixed FB, all possible bad output pairings can simultaneously be disconnected from a suitable artificial pairing whenever the bridge mirror is internal and c≥5, or occupied and c≥7. Pull that artificial pairing back through the arbitrary crossing bijection and apply Step1. Its connected output avoids every bad pairing and is positive.

For occupied c=5, there are precisely two unblocked internal B matchings for each bridge. Each has all three possible output pairings bad. The two target null families are explicitly listed in t15_alternative_core25_blockers_verification.json and have empty intersection. If either bridge mirror is internal, its internal blocker already works. If both mirrors are occupied, at least one bridge lies outside its null family and has a valid blocker. Consequently every c=5 input is handled as well.

The blocker calculation depends on the B geometry, internal B matching, boundary pairing and crossing bijection. It does not use x, the third A hole, or the particular A internal matching. Therefore the fact that this coordinate swap would move the core23 omitted A label9 to10 does not affect its application to core25 with omitted A label9. N14 in Step1 is applied directly to the actual core25 A geometry.

Step4. Complete three-crossing classification

For c=3 there are three pairings of each four-vertex A boundary XA∪{z}. At least two are realizable: if only R0 were realizable, selecting D=R0 in Step1 would make its output union disconnected, contradicting N14.

For each B internal partial matching and each ordering of its three crossing ports, test these three abstract pairings for each bridge. Map endpoints through the specified crossing order, add FB, reject loops or closed components, suppress the bridge mirror, and consult the exact balanced table. This determines the B-admissible pairing subsets without referring to an A matching.

The separate checker verify_t15_alternative_small_B.cpp independently traces graph paths and reads the original audited binary tables. For each core it exhausts all

(133)9!!3!=1621620

B partial matchings with ordered ports. Every input has a bridge with at least two of its three pairings admissible. This property is asserted for every nonzero histogram entry by verify_t15_alternative_small_results.py; producer and independent histograms coincide exactly. Therefore that bridge's at-least-two realizable A pairings and at-least-two admissible B pairings intersect. Step1 expands their common pairing to the required cycle.

Ordering all B ports covers every original crossing bijection: order the actual A ports once, and then list their B mates in that order. No restriction on lengths, positions, or partner order is imposed.

Step5. Complete one-crossing classification and certificates

For c=1 the A boundary has just two vertices, hence its unique pairing is realizable by N14. The complete B enumeration has 13·11!!=135135 inputs per core. The only inputs with neither bridge admissible number respectively3,2,20 for cores18,21,25. The independent graph checker regenerates these exact lists. verify_t15_alternative_small_results.py checks equality with the lists supplied to the residual producer, including duplicate and count checks.

For each exceptional B input, enumerate all thirteen A port choices and all 10395 pairings of the other twelve originally covered A vertices. The crossing is uniquely determined by the chosen A port and the exceptional B port. The certificate outcomes are:

Core Exceptional B inputs Complete residual inputs Positive Unknown or exhausted
18 3 405405 405405 0
21 2 270270 270270 0
25 20 2702700 2702700 0

The three independent checkers verify_t15_alternative_core*_c1_residual.cpp regenerate every original required matching, compare all thirteen required edges to the saved record, and verify thirty distinct cycle vertices, exact omitted pair, containment of all required edges, shortness of all other edges including the closing edge, exact record counts, and absence of trailing data. All three report PASS. Each binary record has26 required-edge endpoint bytes and30 cycle vertex bytes.

These certificates use the isomorphic labels 2a+1 on A and 2b on B. They omit 2x+1 and 2y respectively. This is a common coordinate insertion, preserving every local short adjacency and every short cross-face bridge; transport back through the explicit original cut and coordinate permutation yields exactly the marked global omissions in the Claim.

The search caps have no logical role: every residual input has a checked positive witness, and none is omitted or classified negative by timeout.

The possible crossing counts are 1,3,5,7,9,11,13. Steps2--5 exhaust them in all three geometries. Step1 preserves every original edge and produces exactly the required support. The claim follows.

Corrections or missing assumptions

No narrowing of the three-core claim is made. The perfect-matching and table imports must retain their arbitrary complete-graph scope. Only the inverse B certificate is transported from core23; the entire marked core23 geometry is not asserted isomorphic to core25.

Open risks and reproducibility
  • Fresh-context semantic audit remains pending.
  • Global eight-hole coverage and whether these cores replace core26 must be checked separately.
  • Compile each C++ source with g++ -O3 -std=c++17 and run from research/six_directions, where the imported tables are located.
  • New verification reports are t15_alternative_small_verification.json, t15_alternative_core25_blockers_verification.json, and the three t15_alternative_core*_c1_residual_verification.json files.
  • The earlier core4 zero-crossing proof package is preserved separately; no assertion about full core4 is made here.
T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_FOUR_CORES.md — Four more T15 cores via a balanced four-hole bridge

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：c165b97de2fb28f78da16d7bd8a02a85819405a0ac25a7eb4ab98111bc946e10。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW.json。

Four more T15 cores via a balanced four-hole bridge

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Candidate complete proof for the stated four orbits, pending independent finite-input and semantic audit. Full T15, the whole eight-hole layer, and P6 remain unproved.

Claim, assumptions and normalized geometry

For every arbitrary complete-graph matching on Q5 with a marked T15 hole geometry in orbit 2, 7, 10 or 44 of t15_analytic_geometry.json, the two prescribed majority holes can be omitted in a 30-vertex cycle containing the matching, with only short added edges. All cube-automorphic images and both parity orientations are included.

Take the cut in the following table, delete its coordinate, and apply the same coordinate permutation to both faces so the retained B majority hole is 7. The minority hole is 0 in B. The one-face A has three even local holes x,r,s; omit x. B has three original holes 0,7,y; omit y. The labels r,s are A original holes and their B mirrors are covered by the original matching (internally or by a crossing).

core cut x (A omitted) y (B omitted) r (preferred bridge) s (other bridge)
2 1 0 1 9 3
7 0 0 1 9 10
10 1 0 1 9 15
44 3 9 11 10 6

These labels follow by explicit coordinate deletion/permutation, not by assuming a matching symmetry. Denote internal matchings by F_A,F_B, crossings by C, port sets by X_A,X_B, and c=|C|. Each face has 13 covered original vertices, so c is odd, 1<=c<=13, and the internal edge count is (13-c)/2 on each face. Crossings may be arbitrary long edges; their partner bijection is unrestricted.

Dependencies and finite inputs
  1. Q4 N14: a matching with two equal-parity holes extends to a 15-cycle omitting either specified hole, using short new edges. This is an explicit prior import, valid for arbitrary complete-graph matchings.
  2. Complete Q4 tables for balanced holes {0,7,t,y}, omitting t,y, with a required matching on the other twelve vertices. Each table contains all 10395=11!! matchings. Files are q4_balanced_two_avoided_<t>_<y>.bin; the geometry list is q4_balanced_two_avoided_generation.json. There are 13 marked orbits covering all 49 choices of even t!=0 and odd y!=7, with retained free pair 0,7. Positive records give explicit 14-cycles; negatives must be independently checked by exhausting short degree completions.
  3. For the preferred pair (r,y) in all four rows, the table has no negative matching: (9,1), or (10,11) in the orbit of (9,11).
  4. For the other pair (s,y), the negative counts are respectively 3,1,10,1. Only those exact complete negative lists, not failed bounded searches, are used below.
  5. Fifteen B optional-edge spectra, stored with positive cycles in t15_balanced_bridge_spectra.json. A finite degree-factor obstruction outside each spectrum is recorded in t15_balanced_bridge_spectrum_verification.json.

The complete table generator is q4_balanced_two_avoided_probe.cpp. The finite exceptional B inputs and positive spectra are prepared and checked by t15_balanced_bridge_probe.py; fresh independent checking is required for acceptance. No Q5 T15 theorem is used as an input.

1. General one-bridge transfer

Choose z in {r,s}. Pair the vertices of X_A union {z} into an artificial matching D. F_A union D has exactly the two even holes x and the other member of {r,s}; N14 gives a 15-cycle on A-x containing it. Delete D, attach all C, and add the short bridge z_A z_B.

If z_B is not in X_B, it is covered internally by F_B. The graph from A, C and the new bridge is a path forest with endpoint set X_B union {z_B}, interiors A-x. Compress these paths to a matching R. If F_B(z)=k and R(z)=q, replace kz,zq by kq in F_B union R. The internal endpoint k is not a crossing port, whereas q is a crossing port, so k!=q and this replacement creates a matching. The resulting L_B has holes {0,7,y,z}. A 14-cycle omitting y,z and containing L_B expands to a 30-cycle: restore z_B and all 15 A vertices, along with every original edge. All artificial edges disappear by deletion or expansion.

If z_B is a port and c>=3, let d=C^{-1}(z_B) and prescribe zd in D. This is a legitimate pairing because z is an original A hole and d is a covered A port. D contains at least two edges. After deleting D, the endpoints z,d of its distinguished edge lie in different path components: the remainder of their former cycle is broken by another deleted D edge. Attaching crossings supplies distinct B endpoints. Adding z_A z_B joins those two distinct components at the leaf attached to d, making no cycle. The resulting forest has endpoints X_B-{z_B} and interiors (A-x)+z_B. Compress it to R. Now L_B=F_B union R is a matching with holes {0,7,y,z}. Its 14-cycle omitting y,z expands to the required 30-cycle.

For c>=3 choose z=r. Its table has no negatives, so the transfer always works, independently of the crossing bijection and internal matchings. For c=1 it also works unless X_B={r}.

2. One crossing and the alternate bridge

The only outstanding case has one original crossing d_A r_B. Choose z=s, which is internally covered in B because r!=s. The pairing is necessarily D={ds}. Deleting ds from the N14 cycle gives a path through A-x with endpoints d,s; attaching d_A r_B and the s bridge compresses to the edge rs on B. If k=F_B(s), suppress s to obtain

L_B = F_B - {sk} + {rk},   holes {0,7,y,s}.

If this L_B is positive in the complete table, Section 1 finishes. Otherwise the original B matching is recovered uniquely as

F_B = L_B - {r L_B(r)} + {s L_B(r)}.

The vertex r is covered in every negative L_B, because it is different from 0,7,y,s. This gives exactly 3,1,10,1 possible B matchings for the four rows, respectively. No other F_B can obstruct this alternate bridge. Their reconstruction is entirely independent of F_A and d.

3. Exceptional B matchings: force a shared optional edge

Fix one of these 15 exceptional B matchings. It has holes {0,7,y,r}. The preferred (r,y) table is universally positive. Let U be the union of short edges outside F_B that occur in the saved valid 14-cycles on B-{y,r}. Only a certified lower set of possible edges is needed; we do not assume every possible edge is saved.

On the common Q4 labels let A'=Q4-x, and form the short-edge graph

G = E(Q4[A']) minus U.

The finite check proves there is no simple spanning graph H in G whose degree is 2 at s and 1 at every other A' vertex. This is an exact small enumeration: choose the two distinct G-neighbors of s; on the remaining twelve vertices enumerate every perfect matching using G edges. None exists for any of the 15 B inputs. This enumeration does not mention F_A, d, or any chosen A path; its absence therefore applies uniformly to all of them. The saved U sizes range from 17 to 22.

Now take the N14 A cycle using D={dr}, and delete dr to get a path P on A-x from d to r containing F_A. The vertex s is its remaining free hole and is internal. The edge set H=P-F_A consists of short edges and has degree 2 at s and degree 1 at every other A' vertex: covered vertices are internal with one F_A edge, and the two endpoints d,r are free in F_A. Consequently H cannot lie in G. There is an edge uv in H intersect U. Choose a B cycle C_B witnessing this particular edge uv.

This proves the correct existential order: choose any permitted A path, find one of its edges in the union, then select a B cycle witnessing that edge. It does not assume one B cycle contains the entire union.

4. Finish the one-crossing construction

Attach the original crossing d_A r_B and the new short bridge r_A r_B to P. Since d!=r, this gives a simple 16-cycle C_A supported on (A-x) union {r_B}. It is disjoint from C_B on B-{y,r}. The common optional edge uv is inside A-x in C_A and inside B-{y,r} in C_B. It is in neither original matching. Delete its copy from each cycle and add the two short bridges u_Au_B and v_Av_B. Each opened cycle is a path, and the two bridges join these two disjoint paths into one simple 30-cycle. Its support is exactly Q5-{x_A,y_B}. It retains F_A, F_B and the sole original crossing; all surviving new edges are short.

This handles all fifteen exceptional B matchings and every A matching and root d without enumerating those A matchings. Sections 1--4 exhaust all c and prove the four-orbit claim, conditional only on the listed finite inputs and N14 import being verified.

Limits

The other hard T15 cores, the seven Q6 exceptional geometries' full path obligations, and full eight-hole P6 are not closed by this proof. Any new eight-hole parent count requires separate exact coordinate projection and integration with the earlier eight-core theorem.

T15_CORE0_FULL_CLOSURE.md — Complete T15 core 0 by boundary-pairing exclusion

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：83608b6995c5fb33bf791caf7f6a8f1ce2b2d00c0e0f1c7fbec101da98e670ea。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_CORE0_FULL_REVIEW.json。

Complete T15 core 0 by boundary-pairing exclusion

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Candidate full core-0 proof; fresh independent semantic and finite-input audit pending.

Exact claim

Let F be any matching of K(Q5) with holes {0,1,2,7,11,13}. There is a simple 30-vertex cycle on Q5-{1,2} containing every edge of F and with all new edges short. This includes every cube-automorphic image of the marked geometry. Original matching edges may have arbitrary length and parity. Full T15 and full eight-hole P6 remain separate open targets.

Cut coordinate 1 (zero-based). Identify both faces with Q4 by deleting that coordinate. The one-face A has holes {0,3,5}, of even local parity; omit 0_A. The zero-face B has holes {0,7,1}; omit 1_B. All labels below are these common local labels. Write internal matchings F_A,F_B, crossings C, port sets X_A,X_B, and c=|C|. Both faces have 13 originally covered vertices. Hence c is odd and 1<=c<=13.

Dependencies and strategy
  1. Q4 N14, at its previously audited arbitrary-complete-graph scope.
  2. The complete audited Q4 balanced four-hole tables: holes {0,7,z,1}, omit z,1, where z=3 or 5. Each has exactly three negative matchings and 10392 positive matchings. The z=5 table is obtained from z=3 by interchanging coordinates 1 and 2. T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW audited all positive certificates and all negative short completions.
  3. THREE_MATCHINGS_DISCONNECTION.md and its finite N6/N8 basis.
  4. T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md, including full B enumeration and the 810810 complete residual positive cycle certificates, for c=1,3.
  5. t15_core0_r3_c5_inverse.py/.json: complete two-negative-family inverse accounting for the only remaining c=5 port configuration.

The new part is not a count of many A matchings. It uses the fact that N14 can be applied for every artificially chosen boundary matching. A small forbidden output set can therefore be ruled out by deliberately choosing the auxiliary matching to disconnect every forbidden output.

1. Boundary pairings supplied by N14

Choose a bridge label z in {3,5}, and let w be the other one. Put E=X_A union {z}. For every perfect matching D on E, F_A union D has exactly the two even holes 0,w. N14 supplies a 15-cycle on A-0 containing that matching. Delete D. Its path components form a spanning forest with endpoint set E and some induced perfect pairing R on E.

The multigraph R union D is connected: compressing each forest path in the original 15-cycle produces exactly this alternating cycle. Conversely, any later manipulation of the compressed paths records their interiors for expansion; these interiors are disjoint and exhaust A-0. All new surviving path edges are short, since all D edges are deleted.

Attach every original crossing and the new short bridge z_A z_B. There are two distinct cases.

Internal bridge mirror

If z_B is not a port, it is internally covered by F_B, since it is not one of its original holes. Attaching the crossings and the bridge maps the endpoints E bijectively to X_B union {z_B}. Join the resulting path pairing to F_B and suppress the degree-two vertex z_B. The result is a matching L with holes {0,7,1,z}. The suppressed vertex has one internal F_B neighbor and one port neighbor, which are distinct; therefore no cycle or loop is created.

For this fixed F_B and crossing bijection, the map R -> L is injective. Indeed, in L identify the partner of the internal vertex k=F_B(z). Replace its incident edge kq by kz,zq, remove the other fixed F_B edges, and pull all port labels back through C. This recovers R uniquely. Consequently at most three possible R give negative L, one for each negative entry of the exact balanced table. Every positive L expands its 14-cycle to a 30-cycle by restoring z_B and the 15 A vertices.

Occupied bridge mirror

If z_B is a port, set d=C^{-1}(z_B). The vertex z is an A original hole, so d!=z. For c>=3 prescribe zd in D, and write D={zd} union D', where D' is any perfect matching on X_A-{d}.

Replace the deleted edge zd of the N14 cycle by the path z_A--z_B--d_A, whose first edge is short and whose second is the original crossing. Delete D'. Because D' is nonempty, this leaves a path forest, not a closed component. Attach all the other original crossings. Its endpoints are X_B-{z_B}, and its interiors cover (A-0) union {z_B}. Let Q be its endpoint pairing, pulled back to X_A-{d}.

Here Q union D' is connected: it is obtained by compressing paths in the same single cycle after replacing zd. The B matching obtained by adding the transported Q to F_B has holes {0,7,1,z}. This map Q -> L is injective, because F_B is fixed and disjoint from the port endpoints. At most three Q are negative. A positive 14-cycle expands to the same 30-vertex conclusion, with no remaining auxiliary edges.

These constructions apply to every arbitrary crossing bijection; no shortness assumption is made on original C, F_A or F_B.

2. All c>=7, and an internal mirror when c=5

For an internal mirror the boundary set E has size c+1. When c>=5 this size is even and at least six. Apply the three-matchings disconnection lemma to the at most three forbidden R. Choose D whose union with every forbidden R is disconnected. Section 1 and N14 produce an R with connected R union D. It cannot be one of the forbidden R. This gives a positive L and finishes the construction.

For an occupied mirror at c>=7, the boundary of Q has size c-1>=6. Apply the same lemma to the at most three forbidden Q to select D'. Then invoke N14 with {zd} union D'. The resulting Q has connected Q union D' and is therefore positive. It expands as in Section 1.

Thus every c>=7 input is closed, and for c=5 an input is closed if either 3_B or 5_B is internally covered.

3. The remaining c=5 case: both mirrors are ports

Suppose {3,5} is a subset of X_B, which has size five. For bridge z, any compressed matching is L=F_B union Q_B, where Q_B pairs the four ports X_B-{z}. Thus Q_B consists of two edges, F_B consists of four, and their vertex supports are disjoint.

If even one such compression can be negative, its F_B must be obtained from one of the three negative L entries by choosing two L edges for Q_B and deleting them. The port set is then {z} union V(Q_B). Since the other bridge mirror w is also a port, the chosen two edges must cover w. Conversely these choices enumerate all possible negative compressions for this bridge, independently of the A forest.

There are precisely 15 distinct (X_B,F_B) candidates for z=3, and 15 for z=5. t15_core0_r3_c5_inverse.py enumerates every choice explicitly from the complete negative tables, including the coordinate permutation for z=5. The two sets have empty intersection. This is a small finite exhaustion, not a sampling statement.

Therefore, for the actual (X_B,F_B), at least one bridge z has no possible negative compressed matching at all. For that bridge choose any D' on the four remaining A ports, add zd and use Section 1. The resulting forest is valid and its compressed L must be positive. This closes every c=5 input.

4. Three crossings

For each bridge there are three possible pairings of the four endpoints X_A union {z}. At least two are realizable by Section 1: if only R0 were realizable, choosing D=R0 would force R0 union D disconnected, contrary to N14. This is the two-of-three lemma, independent of any A enumeration.

For fixed B partial matching and crossing bijection, test the three pairings for each bridge. After mapping A ports through C, join the compressed paths to F_B. It independently traces graph components and reads the original binary negative tables; it does not reuse the producer's suppression formula. The resulting full histograms and checks are recorded in t15_r3_small_B_independent.json and t15_r3_small_verification.json.

For that bridge, its at-least-two realizable A pairings and at-least-two admissible B pairings intersect. Choose their common pairing and expand the positive B 14-cycle. This closes all c=3 cases.

For c=1 the A endpoint set has two vertices, so its unique pairing is realizable by N14. The same complete B enumeration checks all 13*11!!=135135 partial matchings. Only six have no admissible bridge. Their exact lists are in T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md; the independent graph checker agrees with the producer and the search inputs.

The only possible crossing counts are 1,3,5,7,9,11,13. Sections 2--5 cover all of them and every arbitrary internal matching and partner bijection. The exact core-0 theorem follows once the explicit finite inputs and dependency applications above pass fresh independent review.

This proof does not rely on the large A port-spectrum producer counts, the alternative cut's c2 or c4 research, or any random Q5 experiment. No claim of full T15, complete eight-hole P6, or full P6 is made.

For every matching F of K(Q5) with holes {0,1,2,13,22,31}, there is a simple cycle on Q5−{1,2} containing every edge of F, with every new edge a cube edge. The claim includes all cube-automorphic images of this marked geometry. Original matching edges may have arbitrary lengths and parity types.

  2. The complete independently audited balanced Q4 tables, each covering all 10395 matchings on twelve covered vertices. See T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW.md/.json.
  3. The independent small-crossing B enumeration in T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md and t15_r3_small_verification.json.

verify_t15_core15_table.py independently reads the audited raw table, applies the coordinate permutations that produce this geometry, checks their consistency, and verifies this unique negative. Its report is t15_core15_table_verification.json.

Proof Strategy

N14 applies for every artificially chosen endpoint matching. The induced forest pairing must have connected union with that chosen matching. For each fixed B input there is at most one forbidden compressed output for bridge 10. Choosing the artificial matching equal to its forbidden endpoint pairing makes that union disconnected, forcing a positive output. This covers every c≥5. The independently checked B kernels cover all small-crossing inputs except twelve one-crossing and one three-crossing B partial matching. Complete positive cycles close all those residual inputs.

Dependency Map
  1. N14 supplies the A forests and compatibility with every prescribed artificial matching.
  2. The balanced table has one exact forbidden output for bridge 10.
  3. The small-crossing independent enumeration supplies complete exceptional B lists.

Proof

Let z∈{10,15}, and put E=XA∪{z}. For every perfect matching D on E, the matching FA∪D has exactly the two even local holes 0 and the other retained A hole. N14 gives a 15-cycle on A−0 containing it. Delete D. The remainder is a spanning path forest whose endpoint pairing is a perfect matching R on E.

The multigraph D∪R is connected: compression of those paths in the original single cycle gives exactly that multigraph. Every artificial edge is deleted, so every remaining edge outside the original matching is short.

Step 2. The bridge mirror is internal

Suppose zB∉XB. Attach the original crossings and the short bridge zAzB. Let k=FB(z), and let q be the transported partner of zB in the forest pairing. Suppress zB, replacing its two incident edges by kq. Since k is internally covered and q is a crossing port, they are distinct. The result is a matching L with holes {0,7,z,1}.

For fixed FB and C, this map from R to L is injective. The edge incident to k in L determines q; splitting it through zB, removing the other fixed B edges, and undoing C recovers R. Thus bridge z=10 has at most one forbidden pairing R0 for every fixed input.

When c≥5, |E|=c+1≥6. If there is a forbidden R0, choose D=R0 in Step 1. Its union with R0 has (c+1)/2 separate two-vertex components, so the connected output pairing cannot be R0. If no forbidden output exists, choose any D. In either case L is positive.

Suppose zB∈XB, and set d=C−1(zB). Because z is an A hole, d≠z. Prescribe zd in D, writing D={zd}∪D′ for any matching D′ on XA−{d}.

In the N14 cycle replace the artificial edge zAdA by the path zAzBdA, using the new short bridge and the original crossing incident to zB. Delete D′ and attach all remaining original crossings. For c≥3 the nonempty set D′ breaks the cycle into a forest whose interiors cover (A−0)∪{zB} and whose endpoints are XB−{zB}.

Let Q be the endpoint pairing, pulled back to XA−{d}. Its union with D′ is connected by compression in the original cycle after replacing zd. Its B output is L=FB∪C(Q), with holes {0,7,z,1}. For fixed FB,C the map from Q to L is injective, since the fixed internal edges and port-pairing edges have disjoint endpoint sets.

For bridge 10 there is at most one forbidden quotient Q0. When c≥5, the quotient boundary has c−1≥4 vertices. If a forbidden quotient exists, choose D′=Q0. Their union has at least two components, so Step 3 cannot produce that forbidden quotient. With none forbidden, choose any D′. Thus L is positive.

Each bridge has four endpoint vertices and exactly three possible pairings. At least two pairings are realizable by an A forest: if only R0 were realizable, choosing D=R0 in Step 1 would contradict connectedness.

The independent core-15 B kernel checks all (133)9!!=270270 B partial matchings and all six crossing bijections. Except for one B partial matching, every resulting spectrum allows at least two pairings on at least one bridge. These intersect its at least two realizable A pairings, giving a positive output and expanded cycle. The independent checker and producer agree on the entire B spectrum histogram.

The unique exceptional B input is

XB={5,10,15},FB={(2,4),(3,13),(6,8),(9,11),(12,14)}.

It has zero admissible pairing on both bridges for each crossing bijection. Its 270270 possible A partial matchings and six arbitrary crossing bijections leave precisely 1621620 complete residual inputs.

Step 5. One crossing outside the twelve exceptional B inputs

For one crossing, each bridge has a unique endpoint pairing, which Step 1 realizes. The independent B kernel checks every 13·11!!=135135 partial matching. Exactly twelve B inputs have neither bridge admissible. They are listed in t15_r3_small_core15_c1_B_exceptions.txt; their exact equality with t15_core15_c1_B_inputs.txt is checked in the final manifest program.

All other one-crossing inputs therefore have an expanded positive cycle. For each exceptional B input there are 13·11!!=135135 A partial matchings, leaving exactly 12·135135=1621620 complete residual inputs.

The generic producers t15_core15_residual_fast.cpp and t15_core15_residual_hybrid.cpp support both crossing counts and every crossing bijection. The hybrid version first tries bounded alternative search orders and then falls back to the full search; the independent checker does not depend on this heuristic. It enumerates the A port subsets in increasing order, all perfect matchings on their remaining covered A vertices, each exceptional B input, and all permutations of its ports. It emits 1621620 positive certificates for each crossing count, with zero UNKNOWN and zero exhausted input. The two binary certificate files are t15_core15_c1_fast.bin and t15_core15_c3_hybrid.bin. Each record stores thirteen required edges followed by thirty cycle vertices, totaling 56 bytes.

It requires exactly 1621620 records for each crossing count and rejects trailing bytes.

Both complete independent checks pass, covering 3243240 original residual matchings. The manifest T15_CORE15_FULL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION.json records the counts, exact binary sizes and SHA-256 values. Correctness depends on these direct certificate checks, not on the producer's search pruning or node cap.

Steps 2--6 exhaust every odd crossing count. Undoing the coordinate swap proves the original marked geometry; cube automorphisms preserve the entire conclusion and give its orbit. ∎

None beyond the explicitly stated imported theorems and audited tables. The large-crossing proof uses a single forbidden output and has no general boundary-blocking lemma or additional finite-basis dependency.

S={s,t,z,w}.

Replace the artificial edge zd in the N14 cycle by the two-edge path zAzBdA, using the short bridge and the original crossing. Delete D′ and attach the other original crossings. When c≥3, the nonempty set D′ breaks the cycle into a spanning path forest. Its interiors cover (A−9)∪{zB}, and its endpoint set is XB−{zB}.

Write Q for its endpoint pairing in B labels. It has connected union with the transported D′, because compression of its paths recovers the same single cycle. Its compressed output is L=FB∪Q, with holes {0,7,z,8}.

In either case a positive L has a fourteen-vertex cycle in the audited table. Expanding the compressed paths adds the fifteen A−9 vertices and zB, giving a simple thirty-vertex cycle. Expansion preserves all original edges, and every surviving added edge is short. The path interiors are disjoint, so simplicity is preserved.

Step 2. Complete inverse families for a fixed B matching

First use bridge z=3. Let L range over all ten exact negative matchings in its table.

For an occupied bridge, every negative decomposition is L=FB∪Q. Thus, for the given internal edge count m, select any m edges J of L. Set FB=J and Q=L−J. This enumerates every bad quotient family for every fixed internal matching. There is no edge-length restriction on J.

For an internal bridge, write k=FB(z) and let q=L(k). The edge kq belongs to L. The remaining m−1 internal edges form a subset J⊆L−{kq}. Conversely every choice of an oriented edge kq of L and such a subset gives

FB=J∪{zk},RB=(L−J−{kq})∪{zq}.

Here RB is the transported forest endpoint pairing on XB∪{z}. This is exactly the inverse of the suppression in Step 1. Hence all forbidden outputs are enumerated, and none are discarded according to a heuristic about an A matching.

If a fixed actual FB is absent from an inverse list, it admits no negative output in that mode. If it occurs, the list contains its full forbidden output family. The arbitrary crossing bijection simply relabels the boundary; it changes neither completeness nor connectedness.

Complete T15 core 24

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Candidate complete-core proof, with explicit finite certificates and independent checks. Fresh overall semantic review is required before integration. Full T15 and the whole eight-hole layer are not asserted here.

Claim

Every arbitrary matching F of K(Q5) with holes {0,1,7,14,22,31} extends to a simple cycle on Q5−{1,7} containing every edge of F, with all new edges short. This includes the entire marked cube-automorphism orbit. Original matching edges may have arbitrary lengths and parity types.

Status and imports

PROVABLE AS STATED, conditional on the imported Q4 N14 theorem and the audited Q4 finite tables below. The manifest is T15_CORE24_FULL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION.json; the full package awaits fresh overall review.

  1. Q4 N14 for arbitrary complete-graph matchings with two same-parity holes, omitting either specified hole.
  2. Audited three-avoided Q4 tables: holes {0,1,a,b}, omissions 1,a,b, each containing all 10395 matchings and positive thirteen-vertex cycles. See R4_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_REVIEW.md/.json and the imported table audits there.
  3. The five-mode inverse-blocking theorem R4_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_BLOCKING.md, with its independent complete inverse-family and blocker audit R4_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_REVIEW.json (PASS, provisional same-family review). It proves the large-crossing reduction stated below, not the remaining residual cases.
  4. Eighteen eleven-cycle tables for this core's four-bridge choices. Their positive cycles and exact input domains are checked in r4_parent_fourbridge_preparation.json. Only positive certificates are used by the four-bridge construction.
Geometry and notation

Swap global coordinates zero and one. This maps the original holes to {0,2,7,13,21,31} and the omissions to 2,7. Write normalized labels as vA=2v+1 and vB=2v. Then A has holes {3,6,10,15} and omits 3A; B has holes {0,1} and omits 1B. The retained free global vertices are 0,13,21,31.

Write FA,FB for internal matchings, XA,XB for their ports, and C:XA→XB for the arbitrary crossing bijection. The crossing count c is even, 0≤c≤12; the internal edge counts are (12−c)/2 in A and (14−c)/2 in B. A ports may include local vertex zero, which is originally covered in A.

Strategy and dependency map

For c≥4, the audited five-mode two-bridge inverse argument closes all but explicit joint B residuals. Every complete input over these residuals is solved by an independently checked four-bridge forest. A separate exact small spectrum closes all two-crossing inputs except 786 B partial matchings, and the same four-bridge check closes every input over these too. At zero crossings, N14 gives a uniform A path; only 255 B matchings remain, and explicit independently verified thirty-cycles cover their entire product with A matchings.

Thus the dependencies are N14 and audited tables; the five-mode reduction; exact small-spectrum input completeness; the four-bridge forest expansion; and positive residual cycle verification. No unknown search result is used as a universal certificate.

Proof
Step 1. The audited two-bridge reduction for c≥4

Choose two bridge labels a,b among 6,10,15. Add an arbitrary auxiliary pairing D on XA∪{a,b} to FA. N14 gives a 15-cycle on A−3. Deleting D leaves an A forest whose endpoint pairing has connected union with D.

The five distinct B situations are: distinct internal mates; internally paired bridges; only the first mirror occupied; only the second occupied; both occupied. In the latter four modes prescribe and replace the corresponding auxiliary edge or edges before deleting the remaining auxiliary pairing. As proved and audited in R4_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_BLOCKING.md, each permitted quotient pairing has connected union with its chosen remaining auxiliary pairing, and a positive thirteen-cycle in B expands to the required thirty-cycle.

The complete inverse lists account for every possible negative B output for each fixed FB. Every saved blocking pairing disconnects all bad outputs. N14's connected output is therefore positive. An input absent from the inverse list has no negative output. Intersecting unresolved families over all three retained-hole bridge pairs leaves precisely 312, 34, and 1 B internal matchings for c=4,6,8, respectively, and none for c=10,12. These exact joint lists are in r4_joint_blocking_check.json and the core24 B input files.

Step 2. Four bridges and their finite positive test

Set J={(5,7),(9,11),(12,14)}, with the first endpoints even and second endpoints odd. Choose a retained-hole bridge pair a,b, two distinct edges of J, and an even endpoint p of one and the odd endpoint q of the other, in either order. There are 3·3·2=18 choices. Let u be the third retained A hole and let S={a,b,p,q}.

Enumerate every short-edge set H on A−3 having degree two at u, zero at p,q, and one at every other vertex. This enumeration chooses the two distinct neighbors of u and then every short perfect matching on the remaining eligible vertices. Reject H if it overlaps a required FA edge or if FA∪H has a cyclic component.

Its boundary has one crossing endpoint incidence for every A port and one bridge endpoint incidence for every member of S. A vertex in {p,q}∩XA has two endpoint incidences at the same isolated A vertex; this is a zero-length path, not a deleted vertex. The implementation preserves both incidences as distinct indexed endpoints. Every other component is a path with two endpoint incidences. Thus this correctly represents all fifteen A vertices, including zero-length components when needed.

Attach all original crossings, the four short bridges at S, and FB. Reject a cyclic component. Suppressing the interiors, including the four B bridge mirrors, gives a perfect matching L on the ten covered vertices of B−{0,1,a,b,p,q}; the retained free vertex zero is not part of L.

If L has a saved positive eleven-cycle in the corresponding five-avoided table, expand the compressed paths. Their interiors are exactly the fifteen A vertices and four B bridge mirrors. Their disjointness and acyclicity preserve simplicity, and 11+15+4=30 gives the exact required support. Every original matching edge lies in a compressed path or in L and is restored. Every surviving added edge is short. This proves the soundness of each accepted four-bridge test.

r4_joint_fourbridge_parent.cpp enumerates every A port subset and every matching on the remaining originally covered A vertices, every joint residual B internal matching, and all c! crossing bijections. Step 4. The two-crossing spectrum and its exact residual domain

There are (122)9!!=62370 A partial matchings and (142)11!!=945945 B partial matchings. Each of the three retained-hole bridge pairs has four endpoint incidences and three possible pairings, giving a nine-bit spectrum on each face. Both crossing orientations fail for every A partial input over these B matchings, giving precisely 786·2·62370=98045640 complete residual inputs. There are no additional nonzero-spectrum B failures.

The B list is r4_joint_fourbridge_core24_B2.txt; its exact equality with the zero-spectrum list is checked by the manifest program. Step 5. Zero crossings: a uniform A path and complete B reduction

For any retained-hole bridge pair a,b, add the single auxiliary edge ab to FA. It leaves the same-parity holes 3 and the third retained A hole. N14 gives a 15-cycle on A−3; deleting ab gives a spanning path between a and b, uniformly for every A matching.

If FB contains ab, attaching both bridges closes a component and that bridge pair is rejected. Otherwise let k=FB(a) and l=FB(b). They are distinct and outside the bridge pair. Suppress the resulting path from k through the two B mirrors and all A vertices to l, replacing ak,bl by kl. This gives a six-edge matching L with holes {0,1,a,b}. Any positive thirteen-cycle for L expands to the required thirty-cycle.

verify_t15_core24_c0_B.py independently enumerates all 13!!=135135 B matchings, tests all three bridge pairs by this exact suppression, and identifies exactly 255 exceptional B matchings. Thus the residual domain has exactly 255·10395=2650725 inputs; its completeness is not inferred merely from its file size.

t15_core24_raw_residual.cpp produces a thirty-cycle for every saved zero-crossing residual input. The result is 2650725 positive records, zero UNKNOWN and zero exhausted input. Each record contains the thirteen required edges followed by thirty cycle vertices.

verify_t15_core24_raw_residual.cpp performs no search. It compares every required edge byte with the independently regenerated original input stream, checks distinct required endpoints and the exact original hole set, checks thirty distinct cycle vertices with support exactly Q5−{2,7}, and verifies all thirteen original edges and shortness of every other cycle edge. It asserts the complete record count and rejects trailing bytes. All records pass. File sizes and SHA-256 values appear in the manifest.

The even crossing counts zero through twelve are now exhausted. Undo the global coordinate swap to prove the original marked claim; cube automorphisms preserve the entire conclusion and yield its orbit. ∎

N14 gives A forests and connectedness with each chosen artificial pairing. Balanced tables classify their compressed B matchings. Complete inverse enumeration and explicit blockers close larger crossings. Complete B spectra give exact small-crossing residuals. Full positive certificates close the residual domains. No T15, eight-hole, P6, or core27 conclusion is used upstream.

Proof
Step 1. N14 boundary pairing and expansion

Fix z and let w be the other retained A hole. Set E=XA∪{z}. For every perfect matching D on E, FA∪D is a seven-edge matching with exactly the two local even holes 9,w. N14 gives a simple cycle on A−9 containing it. Delete D. Since its edges are nonempty and vertex-disjoint, the result is a spanning path forest. If zB is occupied and c≥3, let d=C−1(zB) and prescribe zd∈D, with D={zd}∪D′. Replace zd in the N14 cycle by zAzBdA, using the bridge and the original crossing. Delete the nonempty D′ and attach the other original crossings. This gives a path forest with interiors (A−9)∪{zB} and boundary XB−{zB}. Its pairing Q has connected union with the transported D′. The compressed matching is L=FB∪Q.

For positive L, replace its compressed edges in the balanced fourteen-vertex B cycle by the recorded forest paths. The paths have mutually disjoint interiors disjoint from those fourteen vertices. Expansion adds fifteen A vertices and zB, giving a simple thirty-vertex cycle. Every original edge survives, including a suppressed original kz and all crossings; artificial D edges are deleted, compressed edges are expanded, and all remaining added edges are short.

These formulas invert Step 1 in both directions, so no negative endpoint pairing can be missed for any fixed actual FB. An absent FB has no negative output. Arbitrary C merely relabels the boundary and preserves connectedness; no A matching or edge-length restriction is used to discard an output.

All 82432350 complete residual inputs have positive cycles, zero UNKNOWN and zero exhausted inputs; all three independent rank-bitmap verifications pass. The complete binary size is 4616211600 bytes across t15_core27_c1_residual.bin, t15_core27_c3_residual.bin, and t15_core27_c5_residual.bin. The aggregate checker verify_t15_core27_full_closure.py requires all expected positive records, no UNKNOWN/exhausted input, exact independently verified coverage, reduction-list equality, import-hash equality, and geometry checks before emitting T15_CORE27_FULL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION.json.

Steps 2–5 therefore cover every odd crossing count. Undo the global coordinate permutation and transport by cube automorphisms to conclude the original claim with all original edges retained and only short new edges. ∎

Reproduction

Compile t15_residual_fast.cpp and verify_t15_residual_rank.cpp with g++ -O3 -std=c++17; -march=native is optional for the producer. For each c=1,3,5, use t15_residual_fast.exe <c> t15_core27_c<c>_B_inputs.txt t15_core27_c<c>_residual.bin t15_core27_c<c>_residual_failures.txt 0 9 6 15 8. Zero requests the full domain. Run the B graph checker, blocker checker, and aggregate checker as named above.

The bounded pilots each covered 100000 inputs, all positive and no UNKNOWN, taking approximately 1.4–1.6 seconds locally. Full enumeration was chosen from this measured cost. Pilot success does not establish universal coverage.

Corrections or Missing Assumptions

Only the explicitly retained N14 and balanced imports are intended as assumptions. All failed-bridge cases remain in the exact finite positive-certificate domains.

The full finite package has passed. A fresh overall semantic review is required before integration; no independent overall acceptance is claimed here. Full T15, the full eight-hole layer, and P6 remain unproved by this package.

Proof Package: full T15 core4

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. New proof package only; global state and previously audited documents are not modified.

Claim

Every arbitrary complete-graph matching F on V(Q5) with holes {0,1,2,7,11,31} extends to a simple thirty-cycle on V(Q5)⧵{1,2}, using only short additional hypercube edges. Every cube-automorphic image of this marked geometry is included.

Status

PROVABLE AS STATED, relative to the explicitly listed imported N14 theorem and checked finite tables/blockers. All new finite domains and direct positive certificates below have separately implemented checks reporting PASS. Fresh-context semantic audit remains pending. No full T15, full eight-hole, or P6 conclusion is asserted in this document.

Assumptions and notation

Cut coordinate zero and label the one-face A by a↦2a+1, the zero-face B by b↦2b. A has holes {0,3,5,15}, omits0; B has holes {0,1}, omits1. Denote original internal matchings by FA,FB, original crossings by C, their port sets by XA,XB, and their cardinality by c. Each matching edge may have arbitrary length and parity. A short edge differs in exactly one coordinate.

A has twelve originally covered vertices and B fourteen, so c is even and 0≤c≤12. The internal edge counts are (12−c)/2 and (14−c)/2. The crossing bijection is arbitrary.

Proof strategy and dependency map

  2. The audited Q4 three-avoided tables: omit 1,s,t for two retained A holes s,t. Each contains every 10395 six-edge matching with free vertex0; the bridge pair3,5 uses33 negatives, while pairs3,15 and5,15 each use128 negatives (the last pair is a coordinate image of3,15).
  3. R4_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_BLOCKING.md and the independently checked canonical inverse files for3,5,1 and3,15,1: exact five-mode inverse families and checked positive boundary blockers for c≥4.
  4. The new independently checked eighteen Q4 five-avoided tables, each containing all945 five-edge matchings, recorded in t15_core4_five_avoided_inputs.json.
  5. Complete two- and four-bridge finite classifications and directly checked residual positive certificates described below.
Proof
Step1. Zero crossings

Choose s,t from {3,5,15} and let u be the remaining retained hole. Add the artificial edge st to FA. N14, with equal-parity holes 0,u, gives a fifteen-cycle omitting0. Delete st to get a spanning A path from s to t preserving FA.

If FB(s)≠t, write k=FB(s),l=FB(t) and suppress the two bridge vertices in B:

L=FB−{sk,tl}+{kl}.

This is a six-edge matching with holes 0,1,s,t. A positive thirteen-cycle omitting 1,s,t expands the edge kl through k,sB,sA, the A path, tA,tB,l to give the required thirty-cycle. This restores the original B edges and uses only short new bridges.

verify_t15_core4_r4_c0_B.py independently enumerates all135135 B matchings and the three suppressions. Precisely175 B matchings have no positive suppression, including rejection of an existing edge st. The saved residual input file contains all10395 A matchings for each of these B matchings. All1819125 full inputs have direct positive certificates, checked for exact input edges, required holes, thirty distinct vertices, exact support, all thirteen required edges and shortness of every other edge by verify_q5_full_input_certificates.cpp. The residual B list is separately regenerated, not inferred from failed search.

Step2. Two crossings

For each bridge pair s,t and remaining hole u, the short part N of an A path forest has degree two at u and degree one at every other vertex of A except omitted0. Enumerate it by choosing two distinct short neighbors of u, then every short perfect matching on the remaining twelve vertices. There are116 patterns when u=3 or5 and96 when u=15.

Discard a pattern that repeats an original A edge or creates a cycle. The surviving graph FA∪N is a spanning forest of two paths, with endpoints the two original ports and s,t. The three pairings of these four endpoints give three bits for each of three bridge pairs. Enumerate all62370 A internal partial matchings and record their available nine-bit spectra.

For each of all945945 B internal partial matchings, test all three pairings for each bridge pair. Map A ports to the ordered B ports, attach the two bridges, include FB, reject any closed component and suppress the degree-two bridge vertices and the abstract A stubs. Mark a bit admissible when the resulting six-edge matching lies outside its exact negative table. A common A/B bit expands a thirteen-cycle to the required thirty-cycle. Reversing the crossing bijection exchanges the two port-to-bridge pairings and preserves the port-pair/bridge-pair option.

Every nonzero B spectrum works for every A input in both orientations. Exactly616 unordered B inputs have zero spectrum, leaving76839840 full inputs. Step4 closes every one of these. The core4 B2 list is independently compared with precisely the zero-signature rows of the complete B input file; the producer also records every B input incompatible with any A spectrum and the two lists agree.

Step3. The remaining large-crossing B lists

Apply the five-mode double-bridge theorem in R4_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_BLOCKING.md, for all three choices from retained holes3,5,15. Its hypotheses hold: all four A holes are even; the retained holes are nonzero and distinct from the B holes0,1. It handles distinct internal mates, internally paired bridge mirrors, one occupied mirror in either orientation, and both occupied mirrors. The prescribed artificial edges in the occupied and paired modes are removed or replaced by the original B path as specified there; no artificial edge remains in the final cycle.

For a fixed B matching, every reported positive auxiliary blocker disconnects every bad output pairing. N14 supplies an output connected with the chosen auxiliary pairing, hence a positive output. This argument pulls every pairing through the actual arbitrary crossing bijection. A missing blocker is retained as unresolved and is never treated as a negative theorem.

Let J={(6,7),(10,11),(12,13)}. Choose two retained holes s,t∈{3,5,15} and let u be the third. Choose an even endpoint z of one J edge and an odd endpoint w of a different J edge. This gives18 bridge sets

S={s,t,z,w}.

All bridge labels are distinct, avoid0,1, and lie in the support of the required cycle. Each u is distinct from every bridge label.

Enumerate every short A graph N having degree two at u, degree zero at 0,z,w, and degree one at every other A vertex. Choose the two short edges at u, then every short perfect matching on all remaining vertices after deleting 0,u,z,w and the selected neighbors. This is a complete degree enumeration.

If FA∪N is simple and acyclic, it provides a pairing R of the abstract external endpoints consisting of the c original crossing stubs and four bridge stubs. Endpoints at the same A vertex are kept as distinct stubs. In particular, if z or w is an original A port, that A vertex is isolated in FA∪N and its original-crossing stub is paired directly to its bridge stub. The isolated vertex is retained as an interior vertex during expansion.

Map each original-crossing stub through its actual partner in B, attach the four short bridges, and add FB. If the resulting multigraph H has a cycle component, reject this choice. This includes a bridge equal to an original crossing: they form a two-cycle and cannot be merged as one edge. For an accepted choice every A vertex except0 and every B bridge vertex has degree two, every other covered B vertex has degree one, and retained free 0B has degree zero. H therefore consists of five nontrivial paths and the isolated free vertex. Compress its paths to a matching L on the ten B vertices outside {0,1}∪S. A positive eleven-cycle on B⧵({1}∪S) containing L expands through those five paths to a thirty-cycle. Expansion restores fifteen A vertices and four B bridge vertices, adding nineteen vertices to the eleven-cycle. All original edges survive, and all new edges are short.
