Complete T15 core 5

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Complete candidate proof for one marked core; fresh independent overall review pending. Full T15 and the full eight-hole layer remain unproved by this package.

Claim

Let F be any matching of K(Q5) whose holes are {0,1,2,7,13,14}. There is a simple cycle on Q5−{1,2} containing every edge of F, with every new edge a cube edge. All cube-automorphic images of this marked geometry are included. Original matching edges may have arbitrary length and parity.

Status

PROVABLE AS STATED, with the explicitly retained previously audited N14 and balanced-table imports below. The new finite checks, including every residual positive cycle, pass. A fresh review of this complete package is requested before integration.

Assumptions
  1. Q4 N14: every arbitrary complete-graph matching with two holes of the same parity extends to a 15-cycle omitting either specified hole, using short new edges.
  2. The audited complete balanced Q4 tables, each covering all 10395 complete-graph matchings on twelve covered vertices. See T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW.md/.json.
  3. The already independently checked small-crossing kernels in T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md and t15_r3_small_verification.json. Their core-5 statements are independently checked exhaustive B computations, rather than an assumed full T15 result.
Notation and normalized geometry

Cut coordinate zero. A vertex vA has global label 2v+1 and a vertex vB has global label 2v. Thus A has holes {0,3,6} and omits 0A; B has holes {0,7,1} and omits 1B. These are exactly the displayed original global holes and omissions; no additional normalization is assumed.

Write FA,FB for the internal matching edges, XA,XB for the crossing ports, C:XA→XB for the arbitrary original crossing bijection, and c=|C|. Each face has thirteen originally covered vertices. Therefore c is odd, 1≤c≤13, and each internal matching has (13−c)/2 edges.

We use the bridge label z=6 except in the already checked small-crossing kernels, which permit either z=3 or z=6. The complete balanced table for holes {0,7,6,1}, omitting 6,1, has exactly two negative matchings. It is the coordinate image of q4_balanced_two_avoided_3_4.bin. The table for bridge 3 has three negative matchings.

Proof Strategy

N14 supplies a boundary pairing compatible with every artificially chosen boundary matching. A boundary matching can be deliberately chosen to exclude a small forbidden set. Two forbidden pairings on at least six boundary vertices can be excluded by an elementary shared-edge argument. Only c=1,3, and an occupied bridge at c=5, require additional finite inputs. The three-crossing kernel is already complete. Five one-crossing exceptional B inputs are closed by 675675 independently verified explicit cycles. The occupied five-crossing inverse kernel has at most one forbidden quotient for every fixed B input.

Dependency Map
  1. N14 gives every needed A forest and the connectedness of its induced boundary pairing with the chosen artificial pairing.
  2. The exact balanced tables classify the compressed B matchings.
  3. The two-pairing exclusion lemma below closes every c≥7 and the internal-bridge case at c=5; it has no finite computational dependency.
  4. verify_t15_core5_c5_inverse.py checks the thirty nonempty inverse cases for an occupied bridge at c=5 directly from the audited raw tables.
  5. The independently checked core-5 c=3 kernel and the new one-crossing residual certificates close the remaining cases.
Proof
Step 1. Boundary pairings supplied by N14

Fix z∈{3,6} and put E=XA∪{z}. For every perfect matching D on E, the matching FA∪D has exactly the two same-parity holes 0 and the other retained A hole. N14 supplies a 15-cycle on A−0 containing that matching. Delete all edges of D. This gives a spanning path forest whose endpoints are E and whose endpoint pairing is a perfect matching R on E.

The multigraph D∪R is connected: compressing the forest paths in the original single cycle produces that multigraph. Every non-original edge surviving in the forest is short. The path interiors are disjoint and exhaust the other vertices of A−0.

Step 2. An internal bridge mirror

Suppose zB∉XB. Attach the original crossings and the short bridge zAzB to the forest. Its endpoint pairing is transported to XB∪{zB}. Let k=FB(z) and let q be the transported partner of zB. Suppress zB, replacing the two incident edges by kq.

The vertex k is internally covered whereas q is a crossing port, so they are distinct. The resulting L is a matching on B−{0,7,1,z}. For fixed FB and C, the map R↦L is injective: replace the edge of L incident to k by the two-edge path through zB, remove the other fixed internal edges, and pull endpoint labels back through C. Hence at most two boundary pairings R are bad when z=6.

If L is positive, expand its fourteen-vertex cycle by restoring the suppressed paths. This restores zB and all fifteen A−0 vertices, yielding one simple thirty-vertex cycle. Every original matching edge is restored, all artificial edges are gone, and every new edge is short.

Step 3. An occupied bridge mirror

Suppose zB∈XB, and write d=C−1(zB). Since z is an A hole, d≠z. Prescribe the edge zd in D and write D={zd}∪D′, where D′ is any perfect matching on XA−{d}.

In the N14 cycle replace the artificial edge zAdA by the path zAzBdA. This uses the new short bridge and the original crossing incident to zB. Delete D′ and attach every other original crossing. When c≥3, the nonempty set D′ breaks the cycle into a forest whose interiors cover (A−0)∪{zB} and whose endpoints are XB−{zB}.

Let Q be the endpoint pairing, pulled back to XA−{d}. Then D′∪Q is connected, by compressing these forest paths in the cycle before deletion of D′. The matching L=FB∪C(Q) has holes {0,7,1,z}. For fixed FB,C, its dependence on Q is injective, because FB covers precisely the internally covered vertices and the quotient pairing covers precisely the remaining ports. Thus at most two Q are bad for bridge 6. Any positive L expands to the required thirty-vertex cycle.

Step 4. Excluding two bad pairings on at least six vertices

Let V have even size N≥6, and let at most two perfect matchings R1,R2 be forbidden. With no forbidden matching, choose any perfect matching D. With one forbidden matching, choose one of its edges and extend it to D. Then D∪R1 has an isolated two-vertex component.

With two forbidden matchings, choose an edge e1 of R1. At most two edges of R2 meet its endpoints. Since R2 has at least three edges, it has an edge e2 disjoint from e1. Extend the two disjoint edges to a perfect matching D. For each i, the shared edge ei is an isolated two-vertex component of D∪Ri. Because N>2, both unions are disconnected. This proves the exclusion lemma without a computational basis or a third-matching lemma.

Step 5. Every c≥7, and an internal mirror at c=5

Always choose bridge z=6. If its mirror is internal and c≥5, the boundary set has c+1≥6 vertices. Step 2 gives at most two forbidden R. Choose D by Step 4 to disconnect it from each forbidden R. Step 1 must produce a connected union, so its output is not forbidden. It therefore gives a positive L and the required expanded cycle.

If its mirror is occupied and c≥7, the quotient boundary has c−1≥6 vertices. Step 3 gives at most two forbidden Q. Choose D′ by Step 4, and then apply Step 3. Connectedness again excludes every forbidden output. This closes all crossing counts at least seven.

Step 6. The occupied mirror at c=5

Here FB has four edges, and the quotient Q is one of the three perfect matchings on four port vertices. A negative L=FB∪C(Q) must be one of the two exact negatives of the bridge-6 table. Conversely, every such decomposition is obtained by choosing two of the six edges of a negative L as C(Q) and keeping the other four as FB. There are only 2(62=)30 choices before deduplication.

The independent program verify_t15_core5_c5_inverse.py reads the audited raw table, applies all relevant coordinate permutations and checks their consistency, verifies that exactly two negatives occur, generates all thirty inverse inputs, and then explicitly checks all three quotient pairings on each resulting four-port boundary. It finds thirty distinct B partial matchings, each with exactly one negative quotient. The full cases and the PASS report are in t15_core5_c5_inverse_verification.json. This independently confirms the earlier producer t15_r3_c5_negative_kernels.py/.json for the bridge used here.

For any fixed FB,C, there is consequently at most one bad quotient Q0 on XA−{d}. If there is none, choose any D′. Otherwise choose D′=Q0. The multigraph D′∪Q0 has two components, since it consists of two duplicated matching edges on four vertices. Step 3 supplies an output Q with D′∪Q connected; therefore Q≠Q0, and L is positive. This closes the occupied case at five crossings.

Step 7. Three crossings

The independently checked core-5 profile in T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md has 270270 possible B partial matchings and six arbitrary crossing bijections, for 1621620 inputs. Its complete B spectrum has no zero case, and every spectrum has a bridge allowing at least two of the three pairings on its four endpoints. The independent graph-compression checker and producer agree on the entire histogram, as recorded in t15_r3_small_verification.json.

For each bridge, N14 implies at least two realizable A pairings: if only one pairing R0 were realizable, applying Step 1 with D=R0 would give the disconnected union of a pairing with itself, contradicting connectedness. Thus the realizable and admissible sets intersect on the bridge selected by the B kernel. Their common pairing expands to the required cycle. This closes all three-crossing inputs without enumerating the A matchings as a proof dependency.

Step 8. One crossing and the five exceptional B inputs

For one crossing, each bridge has a unique endpoint pairing, and Step 1 realizes it. The complete independent B enumeration in the small-crossing package checks all 135135 partial matchings. Exactly five have neither bridge admissible. The five exceptional inputs, with sole port followed by six internal edges, are:

3 : 2-4 5-6 8-10 9-11 12-14 13-15
3 : 2-4 5-6 8-12 9-13 10-14 11-15
6 : 2-4 3-5 8-12 9-11 10-13 14-15
6 : 2-4 3-5 8-14 9-11 10-13 12-15
6 : 2-4 3-5 8-15 9-11 10-13 12-14

They are saved independently as t15_r3_small_core5_c1_B_exceptions.txt, and the search uses the exactly equal list t15_core5_c1_B_inputs.txt. Every other one-crossing input is already solved by its admissible bridge.

For each exceptional B input, the A crossing port has thirteen possibilities and the other twelve covered vertices have 11!!=10395 internal matchings. Thus exactly 5·13·10395=675675 complete residual matchings remain.

Step 9. Independently checked cycles for every one-crossing residual

t15_core5_c1_residual.cpp enumerates every residual matching and emits its thirteen required edges followed by a thirty-vertex cycle. The saved result has 675675 positives and no unknown or exhausted input.

verify_t15_core5_c1_residual.cpp performs no search. It independently enumerates every expected residual input and checks exact agreement with the required edges recorded in each 56-byte record. It verifies thirty distinct cycle vertices with support exactly Q5−{1,2}, presence of every original required edge, and Hamming distance one of every other cycle edge. It asserts exactly 675675 records and rejects trailing bytes. All these checks pass. See t15_core5_c1_residual_verification.json and the combined T15_CORE5_FULL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION.json for the exact binary size and SHA-256.

The free retained vertices in these global labels are 0,7,13,14, which the producer leaves as singleton blocks. All thirteen original matching edges are preserved as indivisible blocks during the search. The independent verifier checks the resulting cycles directly, so correctness does not depend on trusting the search strategy.

The odd crossing counts 1,3,5,7,9,11,13 have now all been exhausted. The required thirty-vertex cycle exists for every matching in the displayed core-5 geometry. Cube automorphisms preserve matching incidence, prescribed holes, cycle simplicity and shortness of new edges, proving the claimed orbit statement. ∎

Reproduction

Compile the two new C++ programs with g++ -O3 -std=c++17, then run:

./t15_core5_c1_residual.exe t15_core5_c1_B_inputs.txt t15_core5_c1_residual.bin t15_core5_c1_residual_failures.txt | Out-File -Encoding utf8 t15_core5_c1_residual.json
./verify_t15_core5_c1_residual.exe t15_core5_c1_B_inputs.txt t15_core5_c1_residual.bin | Out-File -Encoding utf8 t15_core5_c1_residual_verification.json

python verify_t15_core5_full_closure.py

The small-crossing B verifier and its reproduction commands are documented in T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md. Previously submitted proof and checker files were not edited to produce this package.

Corrections or Missing Assumptions

None beyond the explicitly stated N14 and audited balanced-table imports. The two-pairing exclusion proof avoids any dependence on the separate three-pairing finite lemma.

The new complete-core proof should receive a fresh semantic and finite-input audit before being promoted to integrated status. This file does not itself update parent orbit counts or claim a full eight-hole theorem.

The four retained original holes in global labels are {0,7,14,31}.

Write FA,FB for internal matchings, XA,XB for crossing ports, C:XA→XB for the original arbitrary crossing bijection, and c=|XA|=|XB|. Both faces have thirteen original covered vertices. Thus c∈{1,3,5,7,9,11,13} and each internal matching has m=(13−c)/2 edges. A bridge is the short new edge zAzB for z∈{3,15}.

Proof Strategy

Use N14 for every chosen artificial boundary matching. Its connectedness condition allows complete negative-output families to be blocked by saved explicit pairings. This closes all larger crossing counts except one fixed five-port B skeleton. The complete small-crossing B spectra reduce c=1,3 to twenty-two and ten fixed B inputs respectively. Positive cycle certificates close every complete input in all three residual families.

Dependency Map
  1. N14 gives spanning A forests and connectedness with an arbitrary artificial pairing.
  2. Audited balanced tables classify the resulting B matching after path compression.
  3. verify_t15_core8_blockers.py reconstructs every inverse family and checks each explicit blocker by graph traversal.
  4. verify_t15_core8_B.cpp reconstructs the complete small-crossing spectra by graph tracing from the raw balanced tables.
  5. verify_t15_core8_residual.cpp proves exact full-input coverage and validates every saved positive residual cycle, without search or the producer's enumeration order.
  6. verify_t15_core8_full_closure.py checks all reductions, counts, input lists, geometry, import hashes, and certificate hashes.

No T15 theorem, eight-hole result, P6 result, or core8 conclusion is used upstream.

Proof
Step 1. Arbitrary boundary pairing and path expansion

Choose z∈{3,15} and write w for the other retained A hole. Put E=XA∪{z}. For every perfect matching D on E, FA∪D has exactly the two even local holes 0,w. N14 gives a simple 15-cycle on A−0 containing that matching. Delete D. Its nonempty, vertex-disjoint edges break the cycle into a spanning path forest. The induced endpoint pairing R is a perfect matching on E, and D∪R is connected, because contracting the paths recovers the original single cycle. Every surviving edge outside FA is short.

If zB is internal, attach the original crossings and the short bridge. The transported endpoint pairing has boundary XB∪{zB}. Let k=FB(z) and let q be the transported partner of z. Here k is internally covered and q is a port, so k≠q. Suppress zB to replace the original edge kz and the path ending at zB by kq. The result is a six-edge matching L with holes {0,7,z,1}. This operation is invertible for fixed FB,C.

If zB is occupied and c≥3, let d=C−1(zB) and prescribe zd∈D. Write D={zd}∪D′. Replace zd in the N14 cycle by zAzBdA, using the new short bridge and the original crossing. Delete the nonempty matching D′ and attach the remaining original crossings. The result is a spanning path forest with interiors (A−0)∪{zB} and boundary XB−{zB}. Its compressed pairing Q has connected union with the transported D′, and L=FB∪Q is a matching with the same four holes.

Whenever L is positive in its balanced table, expand each compressed edge in its fourteen-vertex cycle. Path interiors are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from those fourteen B vertices. The expansion adds the fifteen vertices of A−0 and zB, producing a simple thirty-vertex cycle. It preserves every original edge, including the suppressed original kz, every original crossing and every long original edge. All artificial D edges have been deleted; every compressed edge is expanded; all remaining new edges are short.

Step 2. Complete inverse families and explicit blockers

For each bridge z, let L run over its exact negative table entries.

For occupied mode, every negative output is L=FB∪Q. Enumerate each m-edge subset J⊆L and set FB=J, Q=L−J.

For internal mode, choose every oriented edge kq of L and every (m−1)-edge subset J⊆L−{kq}. Set

FB=J∪{zk},RB=(L−J−{kq})∪{zq}.

These are both directions of the inverses in Step 1. For a fixed actual FB, the resulting family contains all possible negative boundary pairings. If FB does not occur in the inverse list, it has no negative output. No restriction on its edge lengths or on any A matching is used. The arbitrary crossing bijection only relabels boundary vertices and preserves connectedness.

r3_boundary_blocking_3_1.json and r3_boundary_blocking_15_1.json save these complete families and explicit blocking pairings. verify_t15_core8_blockers.py independently rebuilds every family from the raw negative tables, checks exact set equality, checks all matching supports, and uses graph traversal to verify that each saved blocker has disconnected union with every forbidden output. Its output is t15_core8_blockers_verification.json.

For bridge 3, the complete family counts in internal/occupied modes are 312/43 at c=5, 264/52 at c=7, 100/33 at c=9, 12/10 at c=11, and occupied 1 at c=13. All have explicit blockers except one occupied c=5 family.

For bridge 15, the corresponding counts are 1080/146, 856/180, 240/107, 12/24, and occupied 1. All have explicit blockers except two occupied c=5 families. There is no internal mode at c=13.

Pull the applicable blocker back through C and use it as D in internal mode, or as D′ in occupied mode. Every forbidden output has disconnected union with it, whereas Step 1 supplies an output with connected union. Hence the supplied output is positive. This proves every c≥7 case and every c=5 input with an internal bridge. For c=5 with both bridges occupied, the two null-family sets have exactly one common matching:

J={(2,4),(5,6),(9,11),(10,13)}.

Its port set is S={3,8,12,14,15}. This intersection is verified exactly, not inferred from a failed blocker search. Every other c=5 input has a blocker on at least one bridge. The remaining FB=J inputs are handled in Step 5.

Step 3. Small-crossing spectra, including occupied mirrors

For c=3, each bridge has four A endpoints and three possible endpoint pairings. At least two are realizable: if only R0 were realizable, choose D=R0 in Step 1; its two doubled edges would give two connected components, contradicting connectedness. For c=1 the sole two-endpoint pairing is realizable by N14.

For a fixed B input and crossing bijection, transport A ports to their B partners and the bridge endpoint to zB. Add these compressed edges to FB as a multigraph. Reject a self-loop or any closed component. Otherwise trace the paths between degree-one endpoints and compress them to L, testing it against the balanced table. This defines B-admissibility on the same original A endpoint pairings. In particular, at an occupied mirror two endpoint labels become the same B vertex; the graph test, rather than an assumption of distinct boundary labels, handles this. For occupied c=1 the sole pairing can form a loop and is then rejected.

verify_t15_core8_B.cpp independently traces this multigraph and extracts negative sets from the thirteen audited raw tables and their coordinate images. It checks all 135135 one-crossing B inputs, and all (133)9!!·3!=1621620 three-crossing B/bijection inputs. Its full histograms equal the saved producer histograms.

At c=1, exactly twenty-two B inputs have neither bridge admissible. At c=3, exactly ten B partial matchings, each with all six bijections, have zero admissible pairing on both bridges; every other B/bijection input has at least two admissible pairings on some bridge. Its two-of-three admissible set intersects the at-least-two realizable A set, closing that input by Step 1.

The ten exceptional B partial matchings are exactly

FB=J∪{e},e∈(S2),

with ports S−V(e). This equality is checked directly from the complete independent exception list. It also identifies the relation between the c=3 and c=5 residuals, without assuming that proving one automatically proves the other.

Step 4. Exact residual input domains

The saved inputs are t15_core8_c1_B_inputs.txt, t15_core8_c3_B_inputs.txt, and t15_core8_c5_B_inputs.txt. Each begins with its number of B cases; each row contains its c ports and its (13−c)/2 internal edges. For c=1,3 the lists equal the independently regenerated exceptions, with no duplicate B input. For c=5 the sole row is J with ports S.

For each fixed B case, the A side has

(13c)(12−c)!!

partial matchings, and there are exactly c! crossing bijections. Consequently the complete residual domains have sizes:

c B cases A partial matchings Bijections Full inputs
1 22 135135 1 2972970
3 10 270270 6 16216200
5 1 135135 120 16216200

These are complete domains, with every original internal pairing and arbitrary crossing partner represented. They total 35405370 original matchings.

Step 5. Positive certificates and independent coverage verification

t15_core8_residual.cpp constructs one explicit positive cycle for each residual input. It treats each original matching edge as an indivisible block and the four retained holes as singleton blocks. It joins these blocks only by short edges. Precomputed bitsets and a memo table accelerate the search; the proof uses only the saved positive cycles.

Each certificate record is exactly 56 bytes: thirteen original matching edges, followed by thirty cycle vertices. The three binary files are t15_core8_c1_residual.bin, t15_core8_c3_residual.bin, and t15_core8_c5_residual.bin.

The separate verifier verify_t15_core8_residual.cpp performs no search and does not reproduce the producer's enumeration order. From each record it validates that the required edges form a matching covering exactly Q5−H, with the prescribed B case and exactly c crossings. It computes an independent dense input index: the A port subset has a combinadic rank, the remaining A perfect matching is ranked recursively by the partner of its least unused vertex, and the crossing bijection has a permutation rank. Combining these ranks with the B case index gives a bijection onto the domain in Step 4. A bitmap rejects repeated indices; exact record count and an entirely filled bitmap prove no omission.

For each record the verifier also checks thirty distinct cycle vertices with support exactly Q5−{1,2}, all thirteen original edges present, and Hamming distance one for every other edge. It checks exact EOF with no incomplete or trailing record. The three verification reports are t15_core8_c<c>_residual_verification.json.

All 35405370 residual inputs have positive certificates, with zero UNKNOWN and zero exhausted inputs. Their exact byte sizes are 166486320, 908107200, and 908107200, respectively, totaling 1982700720 bytes. Counts, file sizes and SHA256 hashes are recorded in T15_CORE8_FULL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION.json by the aggregate checker. No finite node cap contributes a negative or universal assertion: each accepted input has its own fully checked positive cycle.

Step 6. Conclusion

Step 2 closes all larger crossing counts except the single five-port B skeleton, which Step 5 closes. Steps 3--5 close every one- and three-crossing input. These cases exhaust every possible odd crossing count. Undo the global coordinate swap and transport by arbitrary cube automorphisms to obtain the original marked claim. All original edges survive and all new edges are short. ∎

Reproduction

From this directory, compile with g++ -O3 -std=c++17; -march=native is optional for the producer. Run the producer as t15_core8_residual.exe <c> t15_core8_c<c>_B_inputs.txt t15_core8_c<c>_residual.bin t15_core8_c<c>_residual_failures.txt for c=1,3,5, saving its JSON stdout. Run the verifier as verify_t15_core8_residual.exe <c> t15_core8_c<c>_B_inputs.txt t15_core8_c<c>_residual.bin, saving each verification JSON. Run verify_t15_core8_B.exe for the B spectra, python verify_t15_core8_blockers.py for all inverse blockers, and python verify_t15_core8_full_closure.py for the aggregate package.

Initial bounded pilots checked 10000 inputs in each residual family, all positive. After bitset optimization a 100000-input three-crossing pilot took about 1.55 seconds on the local environment; full enumeration was chosen using this measured cost, rather than an unbounded blind run. Pilot data are not used to establish universal coverage.

Corrections or Missing Assumptions

None beyond the explicitly retained N14 and audited balanced-table imports. The ten three-crossing B exceptions and the common five-crossing B exception are handled as full positive-certificate domains, not discarded because both bridges fail.

Open Risks

A fresh independent overall proof audit is required before integrating this one core into parent counts. This candidate package does not establish the other T15 cores, full T15, the complete eight-hole layer, or P6. Previously audited core23 files and global proof status were not changed.

T15_EDGE_PRESCRIPTION_REDUCTION.md — An alternative T15 route through one optional edge in an A4 cycle

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json。

An alternative T15 route through one optional edge in an A4 cycle

Date: 2026-11-01. New conditional reduction, independent review pending. The edge-prescription obligation below is UNPROVED. This document does not close T15 or any remaining Q6 endpoint instance.

Exact input and a geometric choice that always exists

Let F be a Q5 T15 input, with minority hole a, forbidden majority holes x,y, and three other majority holes B={b,c,d}. Two distinct vertices of one parity in Q5 have distance two or four. At most two majority vertices are at distance four from BOTH x and y.

To prove this, translate x to 0. If y has weight two, a vertex z of weight four has distance four from y exactly when its support contains one of the two y coordinates and all three other coordinates: two choices. If y has weight four, two four-element subsets of a five-element set intersect in at least three coordinates, so no weight-four z has distance four from y. Consequently among the three vertices of B, one has distance two from at least one of x,y.

Exchange the names of the forbidden vertices if necessary and select z in B with d(y,z)=2. There are exactly two common short neighbors p,q of y and z, both of minority parity.

A sufficient prescription

Adjoin the auxiliary same-parity edge yz to F, obtaining L=F+yz. Its four holes are a, x, and the two members of B other than z. Thus L is an A4 input and x is its forbidden majority hole. The established A4 theorem supplies a 31-cycle on Q5-x containing L with short new edges. What it does NOT guarantee is the following extra condition:

There exists such a cycle C with yp or yq as an edge.

If this prescription holds, say yp is present, y has exactly the two cycle edges yz and yp. Delete y and replace the two-edge segment p-y-z by the short edge pz. The result is a single 30-cycle on Q5-{x,y}. It retains every edge of F because y,z were original holes, and its only new replacement edge pz is short. The artificial yz has disappeared. Thus it proves precisely the T15 conclusion.

For the preprocessed T15 inputs, a is nonadjacent to every member of B, so neither common neighbor p,q equals a. This is not needed for the cycle deletion argument, but matters if a later proof uses coverage of the prescribed-edge endpoints.

Remaining quantified obligation

A sufficient global lemma would assert the edge prescription for every A4 matching L with a specified required same-majority-parity distance-two edge yz and forbidden majority hole x. That is a stronger demand than the existing A4 theorem and is not assumed true here.

An alternative, weaker sufficient demand is: for every original T15 F, there exists at least one ordered choice of forbidden endpoint y and nonforbidden hole z at distance two for which the prescription holds. The geometry above proves that eligible pairs exist, but not that their short common-neighbor edges can occur in an A4 extension. The latter quantifier is the exact unproved step in this alternative route.

This route may handle several of the 23 orbit cores at once. It is independent of the earlier (2,0) EP0 condition: that condition concerns a near-perfect local Hamilton path, whereas the present one concerns an A4 avoided cycle and a required same-parity edge.

T15 prescription analysis: exact equivalence and universal factors

Date: 2026-11-01. Local proof package; no project-wide status is changed.

Claim

The original T15 statement remains: for every matching F of K(Q5) with holes {a,x,y}∪B, where a is even and x,y and the three members of B are odd, there is a cycle on Q5−{x,y} containing F and having only short edges outside F. Original matching edges may have arbitrary length and parity.

This package proves three narrower statements:

  1. For every eligible ordered pair (y,z), with z∈B and d(y,z)=2, and every p∈N(y)∩N(z), the A4 cycle prescription is exactly equivalent to a T15 cycle with the extra prescribed edge pz.
  2. In the preprocessed case N(a)∩B=∅, each one of these prescriptions has a spanning simple cycle factor, uniformly for all F. The factor need not be connected.
  3. T44_5 gives a Hamilton a--z path on Q5−{x,y} for every z∈B, preserving F. A precisely oriented local pattern suffices to close one such path.
Status

PROVABLE AS STATED for Claims 1--3, relative to the explicitly imported CF1 and T44_5 below. The universal connected prescription and full T15 are NOT CURRENTLY JUSTIFIED. No strict counterexample to either is claimed.

Assumptions and notation

N(v) denotes the five short neighbors of v. A cycle factor is a simple spanning 2-regular graph, possibly disconnected. A prescribed new edge must be short; an original edge in F need not be short.

The preprocessed case is sufficient for T15: if az is short for some z∈B, apply T44_5 to the matching F+az, whose holes are the other four odd holes, avoiding x,y. The added edge is short.

The roles of x,y can be exchanged. The elementary geometry proved in T15_EDGE_PRESCRIPTION_REDUCTION.md guarantees at least one eligible ordered pair: at most two vertices of a fixed parity can be at distance four from both x and y, whereas |B|=3.

Proof strategy and dependency map
  1. Suppress or expand one degree-two vertex to prove an exact equivalence.
  2. Import CF1 from A4_SPANNING_FACTOR.md, audited in A4_FACTOR_REVIEW.md, then apply the same suppression to its factors. CF1 depends on a complete 65,535-subset geometry certificate and a matching-independent Hall loss bound. It is a universal statement about arbitrary complete-graph matchings, rather than a matching sample.
  3. Import T44_5 from T44_Q5_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md, with its accepted scope recorded in T44_Q5_CLOSURE_REVIEW.md. Delete one auxiliary edge.

Neither the proofs below nor these dependencies import full P6.

Proof
1. Fixed-prescription equivalence

Fix an eligible (y,z,p) and put L=F+yz. Its four holes are a,x and the other two members of B. The following statements are equivalent:

  • There is a 31-cycle C on Q5−x containing L and yp, with every edge outside L short.
  • There is a 30-cycle D on Q5−{x,y} containing F and pz, with every edge outside F short.

In the forward direction the two edges at y are exactly yz,yp. Replace the path z,y,p by the edge zp. Because C is one cycle of length 31, zp cannot already be an edge of C: otherwise p,y,z would themselves form the entire cycle. Suppression gives a simple cycle of length 30. The edge zp is short by the choice of p, and every edge of F remains, since y,z were holes of F.

In the reverse direction replace zp in D by z,y,p. The new vertex y was absent from D, so expansion produces a simple 31-cycle. The only newly introduced edges are the required edge yz of L and the short edge yp. These two operations are inverse.

Thus even the fixed-p strong prescription is a concrete optional-edge extension question on the original T15 target graph. The weaker sufficient global obligation is exactly

∀F ∃(y,z,p) ∃D:z∈B, d(y,z)=2, p∈N(y)∩N(z),pz∈E(D),

where the ordered forbidden vertex y may be either member of the specified avoided pair. Replacing the two existential choices by universal quantifiers is a stronger assertion, not a consequence of this reduction.

2. Each fixed prescription has a simple spanning cycle factor

Assume N(a)∩B=∅. Fix any eligible (y,z,p). For L=F+yz, its two nonforbidden majority holes are the two members of B−{z}, and neither is adjacent to a. Thus it falls in the nonadjacent branch required by CF1. The edge yp is an allowed short edge outside L: y is matched only to z in L, and p has opposite parity. CF1 therefore gives a simple spanning 2-factor J on Q5−x containing F+yz+yp.

Here p≠a, since p is adjacent to z∈B. Consequently p is covered by F. It already has its F edge and the edge py in J. There cannot be an edge pz in J: it would give p degree three, because pz∉F as z is a hole of F. Hence y is not in a triangle of J. Suppressing y produces a simple spanning 2-factor J′ on Q5−{x,y} containing F+pz. It preserves the number of components. Expansion is inverse, also on factors under these hypotheses.

This proves the universal quantification

∀F ∀(y,z,p) ∃J′:J′ is a simple spanning 2-factor containing F+pz.

It proves neither that one such factor is connected nor that an arbitrary chosen factor can be merged. In particular Hall feasibility of the prescribed edge is already settled; the remaining issue is connectedness.

The exclusion of a triangle above matters: without preprocessing one can have p=a, which has no required F edge. A general factor could then contain the triangle p,y,z; suppressing y would create a doubled edge. The cycle equivalence in Step 1 is valid without preprocessing because a 31-cycle cannot have a separate triangle component.

3. Exact form of the remaining completion problem

Still assume preprocessing. For any target factor J′ put H=J′−F. The new degree is two at the four included holes a and B, and one at every covered vertex. These four holes are independent in the cube: members of B have the same parity, and none is adjacent to a. Every component of H containing a hole is therefore a two-edge path centered at that hole. Its two ends are covered vertices and have degree one in H. These four paths are disjoint. The remaining 18 covered vertices are nine isolated edges of H.

Thus H always consists of exactly four two-edge paths and nine single edges, with 17 short edges in total. The completion problem can equivalently be stated as choosing these paths and edges, disjoint from F, such that F∪H is connected; under a fixed prescription, require pz∈H.

Contracting the 13 edges of F gives a 2-regular multigraph on 17 vertices (the 13 contracted pairs and the four holes). It has no loops, since H avoids F, but it may have parallel edges. Connectivity of this multigraph is exactly connectivity of J′. CF1 establishes that at least one such completion exists for every eligible prescribed pz; it supplies no connectivity conclusion about this multigraph.

4. T44 supplies every hole-to-hole Hamilton path

Fix z∈B and add the auxiliary edge az to F. This is a matching whose holes are the four odd vertices x,y and B−{z}. T44_5 gives a 30-cycle on Q5−{x,y} containing F+az. Delete az to obtain a Hamilton path from a to z containing F, with every new edge short. The edge az need not be short: it was prescribed as an auxiliary matching edge and is deleted before the path is used. This proves the assertion for every choice of z, including the preprocessed case.

For completeness, a precise one-rotation sufficient condition is as follows. Orient such a path P from a to z. Suppose consecutive vertices v,w occur in this order, vw∉F, and the following adjacency conditions hold:

v∈N(z),w∈N(a).

Then delete vw and add vz,wa. The two resulting path components have endpoints a,v and w,z. The new edges join v to z and w to a, so their union is one spanning cycle. Both new edges are short and the deleted edge is outside F. This closes T15 for that particular path.

The order v,w is essential. If the order is w,v, the same operation closes each path component separately and yields two cycles. No argument here proves that a path with the required ordered pattern always exists.

Corrections or missing assumptions

There is no new universal connected-prescription proof in this package. The exact missing lemma is that, for every preprocessed T15 matching F, at least one eligible prescribed pz admits a connected completion F∪H of the form in Step 3. Requiring this separately for every eligible p is a potentially unnecessary strengthening.

Open risks
  • The factor result imports CF1's complete finite geometry certificate; it is not presented as a purely analytic proof of that certificate.
  • T44_5 is imported at its audited scope for arbitrary K(Q5) matchings.
  • The ordered rotation criterion is sufficient only. Failure of this criterion for some chosen path would not refute T15.
  • Full T15, the connected A4 optional-edge strengthening, and full P6 retain their previous open status.
T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md — Proof Package: r3 small-crossing kernels

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：8218505ba8b0c8833272760aa353abb827f20bd2dfe28d68fa8d1bf235bc72f4。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_CORE0_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_CORE15_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_CORE23_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_CORE27_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_CORE5_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_CORE8_FULL_REVIEW.json。

Proof Package: r3 small-crossing kernels

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. This file supplies the complete small-crossing pieces for core 0; it does not claim full T15 or the complete eight-hole layer.

Claim

Consider an arbitrary complete-graph matching on two adjacent four-dimensional cube faces. In the common local labels, its uncovered vertices are {0,3,5} in face A and {0,7,1} in face B. The prescribed omitted vertices are 0A and 1B. If the matching has exactly c∈{1,3} crossing edges, it extends to a simple cycle on the other thirty vertices using only short new edges. This is the core-0 profile.

The c=3 conclusion also holds for the profiles called cores 5 and 23 below. For the remaining profiles, only the explicitly stated finite reduction is proved here.

Status

PROVABLE AS STATED for the preceding claim, conditional on the previously imported Q4 N14 theorem and the independently audited complete balanced four-hole tables. Independent checking performed in this work is recorded in t15_r3_small_verification.json (PASS). A fresh overall proof review remains appropriate before integration.

Assumptions
  • Q4 N14: every arbitrary complete-graph matching with two holes of the same parity extends to a 15-cycle omitting either specified hole, with short new edges.
  • The audited complete Q4 tables for holes {0,7,z,y}, omitting z,y, are exact. Each contains all 11!!=10395 matchings on the other twelve vertices. See T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW.md/.json and q4_balanced_two_avoided_*_*.bin.
  • The common local labeling preserves short edges and mirrors across the cut. No restriction is imposed on crossing partners or on the lengths of original matching edges.
Notation

Let x be the omitted A hole, let r,s be its two retained holes, and let y be the omitted B hole. Write FA,FB for the two internal matchings, XA,XB for their crossing ports, and C:XA→XB for the arbitrary crossing bijection. Both faces have thirteen originally covered vertices. The retained B holes are 0,7. For a bridge z∈{r,s}, define Ez=XA∪{z}.

An A pairing is a perfect matching on Ez obtained by compressing the path components of a spanning path forest on A−x that contains FA and uses short added edges. No cyclic component is permitted in that forest.

Proof Strategy

For c=3, every bridge has at least two realizable A pairings among the three possible pairings. A complete independent finite enumeration shows that every core-0 B input has a bridge permitting at least two of these pairings. The two sets intersect. For c=1, the same construction leaves exactly six B inputs; all 6·135135=810810 complete residual inputs have explicit independently verified thirty-vertex cycles.

Dependency Map
  1. N14 supplies the A path forests and the two-of-three pairing lemma.
  2. The audited balanced tables decide which compressed B matchings have the required fourteen-vertex cycle.
  3. verify_t15_r3_small_B.cpp independently enumerates every B input and reconstructs each compression as a graph.
  4. verify_t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.cpp independently checks both exhaustive residual-input coverage and every saved positive cycle.
Proof
Step 1. Pairing abundance for three crossings

Fix a bridge z and suppose c=3. There are exactly three perfect matchings on the four vertices of Ez. For any such artificial matching D, the matching FA∪D has precisely the two same-parity holes x and the other retained A hole. N14 gives a 15-cycle omitting x. Deleting the two edges of D produces two paths spanning A−x, whose endpoint pairing is some R on Ez.

The pairing R cannot equal D: if equal, restoring the two artificial edges would close each path separately, yielding two components instead of the N14 cycle. If the realizable pairing set were a singleton {R0}, applying N14 with D=R0 would contradict this fact. Consequently every bridge has at least two realizable pairings. This argument avoids dependence on the producer's exhaustive A spectra.

For c=1, the endpoint set has two vertices and its unique pairing is realized by deleting the single artificial edge supplied to N14.

Step 2. Exact meaning of an admissible B pairing

Map each endpoint a∈XA to C(a)∈XB and map endpoint z∈Ez to the mirror zB. Regard each pair of R as the compression of its corresponding A path with the attached original crossings and the new short bridge zAzB. Unite these compressed edges with FB to obtain a multigraph J on B−{0,7,y}.

Every vertex of J except zB has degree one and zB has degree two. Reject a pairing if J contains a closed component, including a loop at zB. Otherwise its path components compress to a perfect matching L on B−{0,7,y,z}. Its six pairs contain all original B edges not incident to z, and the original edge incident to z, if present, is recovered by expanding the corresponding path.

Call R admissible if this L is positive in the audited balanced table. Expanding its fourteen-vertex cycle restores all fifteen A−x vertices and zB, giving a simple thirty-vertex cycle. All original matching edges survive; all added edges are short. Distinct path interiors ensure that expansion preserves simplicity.

Step 3. Complete independent B enumeration

The producer t15_r3_small_spectra.cpp enumerates the B partial matchings, all crossing bijections, and all one or three pairings for each of the two bridges. Its implementation explicitly suppresses the degree-two vertex.

It does not read the producer's prepared negative list. Thus it does not reuse the producer's suppression procedure.

For c=1 it checks all 13·11!!=135135 internal partial matchings. The bit positions for c=3 are the three pairings 01|23, 02|13, 03|12 on the ordered ports followed by the bridge endpoint, first for r and then for s.

T15_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING.md — T15 in Q5: all six holes in one face, zero required crossings

原件：打开文件。SHA-256：1aec13d85973868163a2560945de84abf6a459f45382f8c8b53e35c020df0be5。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json, T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json。

T15 in Q5: all six holes in one face, zero required crossings

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer/proof-checker scoped package. Semantic assurance: same-family / provisional. The deterministic finite checks are separate from this semantic assurance. No global state is changed.

Exact quantified claim

For every matching F of the complete graph on V(Q5), suppose its uncovered vertices are exactly {a} union H, where |H|=5 and each member of H has cube parity opposite to a. For every pair of distinct specified vertices v,w in H, suppose a coordinate cut Q5=A union B has all six holes in A and no edge of F crosses that cut. Then a simple cycle exists on exactly V(Q5) minus {v,w}, contains every edge of F, and has only short cube edges outside F. Thus the cycle has 30 vertices. Required edges of F may be long and may join vertices of the same parity. The claim includes either parity for a.

This is a theorem for every input satisfying this particular cut condition. It is not the unrestricted Q5 T15 theorem and does not prove full P6.

Inputs, symbols, and obligations

Identify the two faces with the same Q4 by deleting the cut coordinate. A vertex x in A corresponds to bar(x) in B, and x--bar(x) is a short Q5 edge. Write F_A and F_B for the two restrictions. The zero-crossing hypothesis implies that F_B is a perfect matching, while F_A has precisely the six holes.

The imported theorem T44_5 is the statement in T44_Q5_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md, with current PASS provenance in T44_Q5_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json. It says that four holes of one parity allow omission of any prescribed two holes in a 30-cycle. Its proof and its Q4/Fink dependencies are explicit imports here; they are not rerun in this package. The import has same-family/provisional semantic assurance. No Q5 T15 or P6 result is used to prove a local step.

The new independent checker imports no generator or earlier checker. It reads all four positive path files and both complete opposite-hole circle tables directly. Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION.md supplies context and the name of the triangle condition; its cycle classification is not needed as an unproved shortcut in the path argument below.

Dependency DAG:

  • Complete opposite-hole circle tables, including exhaustive negative complements -> perfect-matching root-endpoint bounds.
  • Four T15 positive path tables + full matching coverage -> A path bounds.
  • Lossless cube automorphisms + complete marked-hole geometry partition -> those four residual representatives cover all nonadjacent inputs.
  • T44_5 -> adjacent available-hole branch.
  • A and B endpoint bounds + two-bridge construction -> residual branch.

All objects are finite. There are no limit interchanges or asymptotic uniformity assumptions. Bounds are uniform over all complete-graph matchings of the stated vertex supports.

1. Adjacent available-hole branch

If some b in H minus {v,w} is short-adjacent to a, add ab to F. Both are holes, so this is still a matching. Its four remaining holes are H minus {b}, all of one parity, and contain v,w. Apply imported T44_5, omitting exactly v,w. The resulting cycle contains F union {ab}; the edge ab was short, so relative to the original F every added edge is short as required.

2. Lossless residual normalization and complete coverage

Suppose no member of H minus {v,w} is adjacent to a. Translate the common local labels on both faces by a, putting the root at 0 in A and bar(0) in B. The five majority holes then have odd local parity, regardless of a's original local or global parity. Each of the three available holes is a nonneighbor of 0, hence has Q4 weight 3. Permute coordinates, on both faces simultaneously, so these three vertices become {7,11,13}. This is possible because the four weight-3 vertices are the complements of the four distinct coordinate units; any choice of three can be sent to this choice. These transformations preserve all short edges and transport any arbitrary matching bijectively; they also preserve the correspondence of the two faces and the identities of the two omitted holes.

The omitted pair is now drawn from {1,2,4,8,14}. The permutations preserving {7,11,13} fix coordinate unit 1 and permute units {2,4,8}. Their four unordered-pair orbits have representatives

(1,2), (2,4), (1,14), (2,14).

Independently enumerating all binomial(8,5)*binomial(5,2)=560 marked geometries at root 0 gives 520 adjacent geometries and 40 residual ones. The four full coordinate-permutation orbits have sizes 12,12,4,12 and are disjoint. Every residual geometry belongs to exactly one. Translation handles every minority root, including the parity-reversed case; there is no assumption that an arbitrary input was already in a representative.

3. Independently checked A path bounds

For each representative pair (v,w), the holes are {0,7,11,13,v,w}. The remaining ten vertices admit exactly 9!!=945 complete-graph matchings. The checker generates this entire matching set independently and deletes one matching for each parsed record. At the end the set is empty. Invalid mate arrays, duplicate inputs, missing inputs, incomplete records, and trailing bytes all cause failure.

Each row gives a lower set S of odd endpoints q: every q in S has an explicit 0--q path on precisely Q4 minus {v,w}. Each path has 14 distinct vertices, retains all five required matching edges, and has only short edges outside that matching. Distinct witnesses in a row have distinct endpoints. No claim that S lists every possible endpoint is required.

Let N={1,2,4,8} and D3={7,11,13,14}. Define the triangle condition by

{v,w} subset N, N minus {v,w}={p,q}, and pq in F_A.

The deterministic checks establish:

  • If the triangle condition fails, S is all six allowed odd endpoints, namely ODD minus {v,w}.
  • If the triangle condition holds, S contains all four members of D3. In particular these endpoints are allowed, since v,w are neighbors.

The 3780 complete matching records give 22260 positive paths. There are 210 triangular records, each with four listed endpoints; all other 3570 records have six listed endpoints. The two families with both omitted vertices neighboring 0 have histograms {4:105,6:840}; each other family has {6:945}. The checker also confirms the generation JSON against these counts, but does not trust the producer's search or its failure behavior.

The triangle condition obstructs a corresponding 14-cycle through 0 in the older classification. It does not obstruct the endpoint paths used here: the root 0 has degree one in an A path. Its positive paths are checked directly, including all 210 records.

4. Independently checked B endpoint bounds

For every complete-graph perfect matching P on Q4 and every root r, let G(P,r) consist of opposite-parity vertices q for which a Hamilton r--q path contains P and uses only short additional edges. Then

|G(P,r)| >= 4,
G(P,r) intersects {q: d_Q4(r,q)=3}.

The package independently checks the full finite basis behind Q4_PERFECT_ENDPOINT_ABUNDANCE.md, rather than treating the saved 4708 rows as a complete proof by themselves. At root 0, for odd endpoint y, P(0)=y is necessarily impossible: the mandatory edge 0y would already exhaust both endpoint degrees, leaving the remaining vertices disconnected. Otherwise put a=P(0), b=P(y). The four vertices 0,y,a,b are distinct. Deleting 0,y from a desired Hamilton path and adding the auxiliary edge ab is equivalent to a 14-cycle containing

T = P minus {0a,yb} union {ab}

on Q4 minus {0,y}. The reverse removes ab and restores the two endpoint edges. The auxiliary edge cannot coincide with a retained P edge, and the 14-vertex path cannot already contain ab: that would isolate its two endpoints from its other twelve vertices. Thus both constructions give simple paths/cycles and preserve all original required edges.

The two complete tables with omitted sets {0,1} and {0,7} each contain 135135 distinct valid matchings, exactly 13!!, which proves full coverage. All 270166 positive circles pass direct support/edge/shortness checks. For all 104 negatives (51 and 53), the checker exhausts complementary short perfect matchings disjoint from T. Any required cycle must be such a union, since T covers each surviving vertex once and a cycle covers it twice. Every enumerated union has more than one connected component; therefore the claimed negatives are rigorously impossible.

Coordinate permutations transport the negative tables to all eight odd endpoints. For every negative T and every oriented edge ab in T, construct P=T minus {ab} union {0a,yb}. These are all failed endpoint pairs other than the exceptional trivial case P(0)=y, by the preceding equivalence. There are 5824 labeled inverse instances and 4708 distinct candidate P. For each candidate the checker recomputes all eight endpoints by the forward rule, adds the trivial bad endpoint when present, and agrees with every saved exact endpoint row. The bad-endpoint histogram is {1:2072,2:2180,3:36,4:420}; the good distance-3 histogram is {1:420,2:276,3:2212,4:1800}. These imply the two stated bounds within the candidate universe. Outside it, only a possible odd partner P(0) can be bad, giving at least seven good odd endpoints and at least three good distance-3 endpoints. This proves the bounds for every P, without a quantifier gap caused by inspecting only the exceptional candidates. Translation gives every root r.

5. Endpoint intersection and exact two-bridge gluing

Apply Section 4 to F_B at root bar(0), in the same local labels. Let G be its set of good odd local endpoints. If the A record is nontriangular, |S|=6 and |G|>=4 inside an eight-element universe, so |S intersect G|>=2. If it is triangular, S contains D3 and G intersects D3, so again their intersection is nonempty. Choose any q in the intersection and its two witnessing paths R_A and R_B.

The A path goes from 0_A to q_A and visits exactly A minus {v,w}; the B path goes from 0_B to q_B and visits all of B. Their supports are disjoint, and q is odd while 0 is even, so each path has two distinct endpoints. Add the two short edges

0_A--0_B and q_A--q_B.

Starting at 0_A, traverse R_A to q_A, cross to q_B, traverse R_B backwards to 0_B, then cross back to 0_A. This explicitly visits every retained vertex once and gives one simple cycle, not a disconnected 2-factor. It has 14+16=30 vertices and omits exactly v,w. Every original matching edge is internal to a face by hypothesis and is retained by its path. Every other path edge is short; the two bridges are also short. Undoing the shared automorphism proves the precise claim above.

Reproduction and scope boundary

Run D:/anaconda/python.exe research/six_directions/T15_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING_check.py from E:/新问题. The dedicated JSON contains input hashes, every family count, orbit coverage, the full negative-complement evidence, and the independent perfect endpoint census. The review records a hash of this proof too.

This closes only the all-six-holes-in-a-coordinate-face, zero-required- crossing T15 branch, conditional on imported T44_5 for its adjacent subbranch. The nonadjacent subbranch is established directly from the independently checked Q4 certificates. Inputs with required crossings, hole sets in no common coordinate face, the remaining T15 cases, and full P6 are not resolved here. No global closure ledger is edited.

T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_CLOSURE.md — Eight T15 hole orbits with a singleton avoided face

Eight T15 hole orbits with a singleton avoided face

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer package. Status: PROVABLE AS STATED relative to the listed Q4 finite certificates; independent audit pending. Full T15 and full P6 remain unproved.

Exact claim

Let F be any matching of the complete graph on V(Q5), with holes {a,x,y,b1,b2,b3}, where a has parity opposite to all five other holes. The specified omitted holes are x,y. For every input whose marked hole geometry is a cube-automorphic image of any of the eight rows below, there is a simple cycle on Q5−{x,y} containing F, with only short edges outside F. The cycle has exactly 30 vertices.

The eight rows refer to zero-based orbit IDs in t15_analytic_geometry.json and are equivalently specified by the local table below. The original minority hole is normalized to 0 before reading the orbit IDs. The claim is for every matching realizing each geometry; required edges may be long or join equal parities.

Normalization, notation and dependencies

Choose the indicated cut. Its one-face A contains exactly one original hole, the omitted vertex y; the other face B contains the other five holes. Delete the cut coordinate and translate the common local labels by the local label of y, so yA=0. The corresponding vertex of B has the same local label and is joined by a short bridge. In these labels the minority hole in B is even, its other four holes are odd. Both coordinate deletion and the common translation preserve adjacency within faces and the correspondence across the cut.

orbit cut (zero-based) B minority a B omitted x B included holes I
13 1 0 1 7,11,13
14 1 0 1 7,11,14
19 2 3 2 4,8,14
31 3 6 7 1,11,13
32 3 6 7 1,8,13
35 3 6 7 8,11,13
37 0 0 7 11,13,14
38 4 15 14 2,4,8

Write FA,FB for the internal restrictions, C for the original crossing edges, XA,XB for their endpoint sets, and c=|C|. There are 15 covered original vertices in A and 11 in B. Consequently c is odd and 1≤c≤11.

Dependencies, with no use of Q5 T15 or P6:

  1. Complete Q4 two-opposite-hole cycle tables, including their certified 51+53 exceptions (q4_distance1_avoided_table_verification.json and q4_distance3_avoided_table_verification.json), decide the A paths below.
  2. Q4 A4: holes 1:3, omit a specified majority hole, obtain a 15-cycle (Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md).
  3. Exact Q4 T15 classification (Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION.md): for holes 1:5, omitting two majority holes fails precisely when both omitted vertices neighbor the minority and the required matching joins its other two neighbors. In particular it succeeds if either omitted vertex is not a neighbor of the minority.
  4. Finite completion accounting in t15_single_avoided_face_probe.py/.json.
  5. Positive optional-edge spectra in t15_single_crossing_spectra.json, whose paths/cycles are independently checkable without trusting search.

Every application below specifies the resulting hole set and omitted vertices. These are finite statements; no asymptotic or limiting argument is used. All local degree-two contractions are expanded at the end.

1. The exact A path test

Choose d∈XA and a perfect pairing D on XA−{d}. Then L=FA∪D is a matching on Q4 with holes 0,d. For an odd vertex z≠d, let k=L(z). Define Tz=L−{zk}+{dk}, a matching with holes 0,z.

A 14-cycle on Q4−{0,z} containing Tz is equivalent to a 15-vertex d--z path on A−{0} containing L and using short new edges. In the forward direction delete dk, then append kz. In the reverse direction zk must be the last edge, since z is covered by L and is an endpoint; delete z and add dk. Both graphs are simple: d,k,z,0 are distinct, and adding an edge between endpoints of a 14-vertex path cannot duplicate one already in that path. The case z=d is declared unavailable. Thus the complete Q4 tables give an exact test.

2. Transfers for safe and occupied endpoints

Set

S={z∈O(Q4):z≠x, d(a,x)≠1 or d(a,z)≠1}.

The three vertices in I belong to S in every row. Suppose Section 1 gives an A path P with endpoint z∈S. Delete D, attach all original crossings C, and add the short bridge zAzB.

2a. Safe endpoint: zB∉XB

This is a path forest with endpoint set XB∪{zB} and interiors partitioning A−{0}. If zA itself is a port different from d, its mandatory edge belongs to D and is the last edge of P; deleting it isolates zA temporarily. Its original crossing and its new bridge restore degree two, yielding a valid path component. No original matching edge is lost. Compress each path to obtain a matching R on the endpoint set.

If z∈I, the matching FB∪R has holes {a,x}∪(I−{z}), of type 1:3. Q4 A4 omits x, giving a 15-cycle. Expand R to obtain the desired 15+15=30 cycle.

Otherwise zB is internally covered, since it is neither an original hole nor a port. Write k=FB(z) and q=R(z). The sets of internal matching endpoints and crossing ports are disjoint, so k≠q and replacing kz,zq by kq creates a matching LB. Its holes are {a,x}∪I∪{z}, of type 1:5. At least one of x,z is nonadjacent to a by the definition of S. The exact Q4 T15 theorem therefore gives a 14-cycle omitting x,z. Expand kq and the remaining compressed edges. This restores zB and all 15 A vertices, producing a single 14+1+15=30 cycle.

2b. Occupied endpoint: zB∈XB, c≥3

Here require d=C−1(zB) to be a good root for z in Section 1. Then d≠z and D is nonempty. Deleting D from P separates its two endpoints. Attaching the original crossings adds distinct B leaves. The bridge zAzB joins the two different endpoint components, because zB was attached at d. It creates no cycle. If zA is also a port, its separate crossing ends at a different B port; the temporary isolated vertex boundary is covered by the same argument.

The resulting forest has endpoints XB−{zB} and interiors precisely (A−{0})∪{zB}. Compress it to R. Now FB∪R is a matching with holes {a,x}∪I∪{z}. Apply the same Q4 T15 theorem omitting x,z and expand. The resulting cycle has 30 vertices. All artificial edges are deleted or expanded, so all surviving new edges are short. Section 4 treats the excluded case c=1 separately.

3. Complete accounting of roots and port pairings

For each odd z, inverse-enumerate every failing state (d,L) with z≠d from the negative Q4 table for holes 0,z. For every such negative matching T and oriented edge dk of T, the inverse is L=T−{dk}+{zk}. Set storage removes duplicates. These inverses are complete by Section 1; d=z is handled separately in each test.

Any state failing all three fixed targets I belongs to the union of their inverse lists, since at most one target equals d. Test all three conditions in that union. There are 105 failed states for each of orbits 13,14,31,35,37, and none for 19,32,38.

For fixed c, a partial FA has (15−c)/2 edges. It has exactly c(c−2)!! states (d,FA∪D), with (−1)!!=1. Count appearances of each submatching of that size in all failed states. It is stalled exactly when the count equals c(c−2)!!; smaller counts leave a successful fixed-target choice. Every stalled partial is listed this way, including those not selected by any prior construction.

For each of the five nonempty rows the stalled counts at c=1,3,5,7,9,11 are respectively 105,105,21,1,0,0. For each stalled partial and root d, there are (c−2)!! pairings. For each z∈S, count failed completions at that root. A root is good exactly when d≠z and this count is smaller than (c−2)!!.

Let G be the endpoints in S with at least one good root. If |G|>c, some endpoint is safe. Otherwise, failure of both transfers would require G⊆XB and an injective assignment z↦C−1(zB) mapping every z to a bad root. The finite check tests Hall's condition on these bad-root sets and stores a deficient subset whenever no such injection exists. For every stalled partial at c≥3, there is either a safe endpoint by |G|>c or no bad-root injection. Thus Section 2 applies to every actual crossing endpoint set and every actual crossing bijection.

For orbit 37 the same check gives a safe endpoint also at c=1. For the other four rows 13,14,31,35, the only usable endpoint in each c=1 stalled state is the following h:

orbit 13 14 31 35
h 14 13 8 1

If XB≠{h}, h is safe and Section 2a applies. The only remaining case is XB={h}, treated next.

4. One crossing: two cycles and a certified common optional edge

Fix one of the four rows and one of its 105 stalled A matchings. The only crossing is dAhB. The available A path P goes from dA to hA through all of A−{0}. Add dAhB and the short bridge hAhB to close a simple 16-cycle CA whose support is (A−{0})∪{hB}. The endpoints d,h are distinct.

The B matching has holes {a,x,h}∪I and five edges, since its only port is h. Thus there are exactly 9!!=945 possible FB. Since h is not a neighbor of a, Q4 T15 gives a 14-cycle CB on B−{x,h} containing FB.

It remains to choose P,CB with a common optional short edge in their local coordinates. This is a finite positive-certificate assertion: for each of the 105 A matchings, retain a collection of valid d--h paths, and for each of the 945 B matchings retain valid 14-cycles. Let UA,UB be the unions of their short edges outside FA,FB. Every one of the 105·945 pairs has UA∩UB≠∅. The minimum intersection sizes, by row 13,14,31,35, are 7,5,9,6. The four rows comprise 396900 pairs, with no empty intersection.

The files t15_single_crossing_spectrum_inputs.json and t15_single_crossing_spectra.json contain all 4200 matching inputs and the witnessing paths/cycles. t15_single_crossing_spectra.py checks every witness's exact support, endpoints, matching containment and shortness, reconstructs every stored union, and tests every pairwise intersection. Completeness of the B matching lists is by all pairings of their ten covered vertices; completeness of the A lists is Section 3. Only these lower bounds on optional-edge unions are needed; no failed search or assertion of maximality of a spectrum is used in the proof.

Choose st∈UA∩UB, and choose its witnessing P,CB. Build CA from that P as above. Delete sAtA from CA and sBtB from CB, then insert the two short bridges sAsB,tAtB. The cycles were vertex-disjoint. The deleted edges belong to neither original matching, and s,t are distinct and avoid 0,x,h because they occur in both local supports. The two opened paths joined by the two bridges form one simple cycle on their union. It covers precisely Q5−{0A,xB}, retains FA,FB,dAhB, and all added edges are short. This resolves the last one-crossing case.

Conclusion and limits

Sections 2--4 exhaust all roots, pairings, crossing counts and internal matchings for all eight displayed marked geometries, so the exact claim follows relative to the listed finite inputs. Undo their normalizations and any cube automorphism to cover their entire marked-hole orbits.

This does not prove all T15 geometries. It does not address Q6 EP0 or claim full eight-hole P6. Its concrete Q6 coverage must be recomputed against all allowed cuts before updating any remaining-parent count. The prescribed-edge route remains a separate unproved connectivity route.

Four same-parity holes in Q5: avoiding any prescribed two

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft. Proposed complete proof relative to the specified Q4 certificates and preceding gluing lemmas. Independent proof-checker audit pending; full P6 and full Q5 T15 remain open.

Claim T44_5

For every matching F of K(Q5) with exactly four uncovered vertices, all of one parity, and every specified pair of distinct holes x,y, there is a cycle through exactly Q5 minus {x,y}, containing F and having every edge outside F short. Thus the cycle has 30 vertices. Original required edges are arbitrary, including long and same-parity edges.

Inputs and dependency map
  1. Q4 N14 (two same-parity holes, omit one) and T44_4 (four same-parity holes, omit two), certified in Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md and Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_TRANSFER.md with their independent reviews.
  2. Q4_RICH_GLUING.md, reviewed PASS in Q4_RICH_GLUING_REVIEW.md/.json: two avoided Q4 cycles with opposite LOCAL forbidden parities have intersecting optional-new-edge unions in the stated two-hole cases.
  3. T44_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING.md: all four holes in one face and no crossings are handled by two local paths and two short bridges. It uses the complete Q4 perfect-endpoint classification and the 311850 four-hole path certificates. Its separate audit is required.
  4. Complete Q4 opposite-parity two-avoided circle tables, already audited in CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.md. There are 51 negative matchings for holes 0,1 and 53 for holes 0,7; all positives have explicit circles and all negatives have exhaustive complementary-short-matching checks.
  5. The finite completion/root accounting of Section 5 below, independently checkable from those complete tables. No Q5 T15 or Q6 theorem is used.
1. Reduction to two geometries

Translate the first forbidden hole to 0. The second forbidden hole is even, so by coordinate permutations it is 3 or 15. Let s,t be the two other holes. A coordinate splitting both the forbidden pair and {s,t} puts two same-parity holes in each face. Such a coordinate exists exactly when supp(x xor y) intersects supp(s xor t).

In that case the claim follows for positive crossing count by pairing the first-face ports, using N14 there, deleting the artificial pairs, attaching crossings, compressing on the second face, using N14 there, and expanding. The crossing count is even because each face has two original holes. At zero crossings, Q4_RICH_GLUING supplies common optional edges; deleting them and adding the two corresponding short crossings joins the two 15-cycles into the desired 30-cycle.

If the forbidden distance is four, the support of s xor t is nonempty and has even size, hence cannot be confined to the sole coordinate outside the forbidden difference. Thus this split always exists.

For forbidden holes 0,3 and no such split, s and t agree in coordinates 0 and 1 and differ in two of the other three. The subgroup preserving the unordered pair {0,3} consists of translations by 0 or 3, permutations of coordinates 0,1, and permutations of coordinates 2,3,4. Its 18 eligible unordered pairs {s,t} fall into three orbits of size six, represented by

{12,20}, {5,9}, {5,29}.

This finite geometric claim can also be checked by enumerating all 91 pairs of remaining even vertices, as in t15_analytic_geometry.py/.json. For {5,9}, all four holes lie in one coordinate face. More generally any such same-face geometry is handled as follows. At positive crossings, pair ports in the hole face, use Q4 T44_4, delete the nonempty artificial matching, transfer and compress onto the other face, and use Fink's perfect-matching circle extension there. At zero crossings use input 3.

Only the representatives {0,3,12,20} and {0,3,5,29}, forbidden {0,3}, remain. Section 2 puts both into a common canonical cut description.

2. The canonical one-hole/three-hole cut

In the first representative split coordinate 0 and let A be the odd face. It has the sole hole 3, which is forbidden. Drop coordinate 0 and translate both faces by local vector 1. In their common Q4 labels A has sole forbidden hole 0; B has holes {1,7,11}, with 1 forbidden.

In the second representative split coordinate 0 and let A be the even face, whose sole forbidden hole is 0. Dropping that coordinate without translation gives B holes {1,2,14}, with 1 forbidden.

Thus it suffices to handle either target pair (f,g)=(7,11) or (2,14), with A's sole original hole 0, B's original holes {1,f,g}, and 0_A,1_B the prescribed forbidden vertices. The B holes are all odd in the shared local labeling. The A forbidden hole is even locally; their global parities agree as required. New bridges join equal local labels.

Write C for original crossing edges, X_A,X_B for their endpoint sets, and c=|C|. Then c is odd and positive: the original matching covers 15 vertices in A. Also c<=13 because B has three holes. Required crossing edges may connect arbitrary labels; their actual partners are retained.

3. Local path availability from the complete tables

Choose d in X_A and a perfect matching D on X_A minus {d}. Put L=F_A union D, whose holes are 0,d. For any odd z different from d, z is covered by L; write k=L(z) and set

T_z = L - {zk} + {dk}.

Its holes are 0,z. A 14-cycle on Q4 minus {0,z}, containing T_z and using short new edges, yields a 15-vertex d--z path on A minus 0: delete dk to open the cycle between d,k and append the original edge kz. Conversely any such path ends at z via zk, since zk is its required matching edge; removing z and adding dk gives the 14-cycle. The new edge dk is artificial and is removed in the forward construction.

Consequently the audited Q4 tables decide exactly which (d,D,z) work. For z=d the path with equal endpoints is disallowed. If z is one of f,g and some choice works, the safe free-hole transfer in Section 4 already proves the canonical claim. Otherwise use the full availability classification in Section 5.

4. Safe and occupied endpoint transfers

Suppose a path P as above has been chosen with odd endpoint z != 1. Delete D and attach all original crossing edges. Also attach the new short bridge from z_A to z_B. All A vertices except 0 have degree two: at d the crossing edge supplies the missing endpoint degree; at z the bridge supplies it. If z is itself a port, deleting D removes its sole path edge, so z is temporarily isolated; its original crossing plus the bridge restore degree two. This boundary is included, not excluded.

Safe endpoint z outside X_B

The attached B vertices are distinct. The graph is a path forest with endpoints X_B union {z_B}, and its interiors partition A minus 0. Compress it to a matching R on that endpoint set.

If z is f or g, F_B union R is a matching with precisely two same-parity holes, including 1. Q4 N14 omits 1 and gives a 15-cycle; expanding R produces the required 30-cycle.

If z is not f or g, it is internally covered by F_B, since z != 1 and z is not a port. Write k=F_B(z), q=R(z). Suppress the two-edge path k--z--q by replacing zk,zq with kq. The resulting matching has holes {1,f,g,z}, four odd vertices. Q4 T44_4 avoids 1,z. Expanding kq restores z and its original matching edge together with the transfer path; expanding all remaining R edges restores A minus 0. The result has 14+1+15=30 vertices and omits exactly 0_A,1_B.

Occupied endpoint z in X_B

Assume c>=3 and choose the root d to be the original A partner of z_B. Availability in Section 3 ensures d != z. The matching D is nonempty. Every edge of D occurs on P, so deleting D separates P's endpoints d,z into different components, even when z is a port and becomes isolated. After all original crossings have been attached, these components remain different: each attachment adds a distinct B endpoint. Adding bridge z_A z_B joins the z component to the endpoint z_B already attached at d. It creates no cycle. If z is an A port, its separate original crossing attaches at another B port because the crossing partners of d and z are distinct. Thus the temporarily isolated case also gives a path, not a closed component.

All resulting components are paths with endpoints X_B minus {z_B}, and their interiors partition (A minus 0) union {z_B}. Compress to R. Now F_B union R has exactly the four odd holes {1,f,g,z}; apply Q4 T44_4 avoiding 1,z and expand. Again this gives the required 30-cycle.

Only c=1 is excluded from occupied transfer: D would be empty and the two attachments would close a separate A-side cycle. Section 5 always provides a safe endpoint when c=1.

5. Complete finite coverage of choices of roots and pairings

For each odd z, inverse-enumerate the bad near-perfect states (d,L) from the audited negative tables. Given a negative T with holes 0,z and any oriented edge dk of T, the inverse state is

L = T - {dk} + {zk}, with root d.

Every failed state with z != d is included, by the forward equivalence in Section 3. Add the special failure z=d when testing availability. To fail both fixed targets f,g, at least one of them is different from d; therefore the union of these two inverse lists contains every possible double-failure state. Intersecting the two failure conditions gives 256 states for (7,11) and 187 for (2,14).

For a fixed odd crossing count c, an internal partial matching F_A has (15-c)/2 edges. Its completions are the c choices of d and the (c-2)!! pairings D of the other ports, totaling c(c-2)!! distinct states. The convention (-1)!!=1 applies for c=1. Each completion (d,L) contains F_A. Enumerate every submatching of the double-failure states of the required size and count its occurrences. It is a stalled partial matching exactly when the count is c(c-2)!!; any partial not enumerated or with a smaller count has a successful fixed-target completion.

The complete stalled partial counts are:

c 1 3 5 7 9 11 13
f,g=7,11 256 210 42 2 0 0 0
f,g=2,14 187 110 21 1 0 0 0

For each stalled F_A and each odd z, count failed completions separately for each root d. At a fixed d there are (c-2)!! completions; d is a good root for z exactly when z != d and fewer than all those completions are in the inverse negative list. This respects the necessary quantifier: for a good root one may then select an appropriate D.

Let G be all odd z != 1 with at least one good root. If |G|>c, some z in G is outside X_B, and the safe transfer works. This holds for all stalled inputs with c=1.

For the remaining inputs, c>=3. If any z in G lies outside X_B we again use the safe transfer. Otherwise G is a subset of X_B. The original crossing partners define an injective map phi:G -> X_A. If phi(z) is a good root for any z, the occupied transfer applies. Failure would require an injection assigning EVERY z in G to one of its bad roots.

t44_canonical_completion_probe.py exhaustively tests this finite injection condition for every stalled partial in the table. In every case either |G|>c or no such bad-root injection exists. The unresolved count is zero at every c for both target pairs. It stores all partials, all good-root sets, exact failed-completion counts, and the injection test outcome in t44_canonical_completion_probe.json.

This checks all possible crossing endpoint sets and all partner bijections without enumerating them: if G is not contained in X_B a safe endpoint exists, and if it is contained there its actual partner map is one of the injections ruled out above. No assumption of short original crossing edges is used. No random matching test supplies a universal step.

Conclusion and scope

The split lemma, same-face lemma and the two canonical completion arguments exhaust the normalized four-hole geometries, proving T44_5 relative to the stated finite certificates and gluing inputs, subject to their independent audits. In particular the canonical occupied transfer allows an endpoint that is itself an A port, a boundary not needed in the earlier, more restrictive A4 canonical proof.

T44_5 gives the adjacent-hole reduction for Q5 T15: if its minority hole is short-adjacent to a nonforbidden majority hole, add that short edge and apply T44_5 to the remaining four majority holes, avoiding the prescribed two. It does not prove the nonadjacent T15 core or EP0, and does not close full eight-hole P6 or the higher 10--18-hole layers.
